```
- the stage/DSFT tables must be read from stage_format_table.arc at load time
- the 0xDE0 stage element layout and the -0xAF4 count offset apply to the
  RUNTIME structure built from the ARC members
- a port cannot hardcode these tables from the eboot; it must implement the
  ARC loader (18.952) + the DTBL/DSFT member interpretation
```

### 18.985 *** GAP B SOLVED: ARC class-B format decoded, 129/129 EOF_EXACT ***

1) THE FORMAT
```c
// class-B (lip/seq) archive
struct ArcB {
    u32 tag;                       // +0x00  (observed: 8, 21, 23, 46, ...)
    Entry entries[];               // from +0x04 to EOF
};
struct Entry {
    char name[0x20];               // NUL padded, e.g. "e000_000_001_0102.bin"
    u32  dataLen;                  // payload bytes
    u8   data[dataLen];            // payload
};                                 // stride = 0x24 + dataLen
```
There is NO image layer and NO alignment: entries simply follow one another.

2) VALIDATION
```
class-B files = 129   EOF_EXACT = 129   FAIL = 0
examples:
  e000000.arc  size=59364   entries=8    off=59364   exact
  e102010.arc  size=127864  entries=21   off=127864  exact
  e102040.arc  size=294768  entries=51   off=294768  exact
  e102050.arc  size=122976  entries=23   off=122976  exact
```
Every one of the 129 non-table .arc files walks exactly to EOF.

3) CORRECTION OF ALL EARLIER FAILED HYPOTHESES
```
18.940 "record-to-EOF holds for only 23/129"  -> WRONG START OFFSET: the parser
        began at 0x2C (image-header layout) instead of 0x04 (first entry).
18.941 "u32@0x24 is not a record count; size is not a byte length"
        -> u32 at 0x24 IS the FIRST ENTRY's dataLen (name ends at 0x24).
        -> the huge sums came from mis-aligned parsing.
18.943 "no fixed-record-count model fits"     -> true but irrelevant: the format
        is variable-length entries, not fixed records.
```
=> three earlier refutations are now explained: they were all consequences of
   starting the walk at the wrong offset.

4) UNIFICATION WITH CLASS A
```
class-A members : { char name[0x20]; u32 dataLen; payload }   <-- SAME record
class-B entries : { char name[0x20]; u32 dataLen; payload }   <-- SAME record
difference      :
  class A = u32 tag + char archiveName[0x24] + u32 count + members,
            then further images positioned by the 4k alignment rule
  class B = u32 tag + entries to EOF (single "image", no count, no alignment)
```
=> the ARC family shares ONE member/entry record format.

2) SHARED ENTRY RECORD (the one format both classes use)
```c
struct ArcEntry {                 // stride = 0x24 + dataLen
    char name[0x20];              // NUL-padded ASCII, e.g. "e000_000_001_0102.bin"
    u32  dataLen;                 // payload byte length
    u8   data[dataLen];           // payload; class-A payloads start with a 4-char magic
};
```

3) CLASS B (129 files, verified 129/129 EOF_EXACT)
```c
struct ArcB {
    u32 tag;                      // +0x00
    ArcEntry entries[];           // from +0x04 to EOF, NO alignment, NO image layer
};
size_t parse_b(const u8* p, size_t n) {
    size_t off = 4;
    while (off + 0x24 <= n) {
        u32 dl = rd32(p + off + 0x20);
        if (!dl || off + 0x24 + dl > n) break;
        /* entry = { name[0x20]; dataLen; data } */
        off += 0x24 + dl;
    }
    return off;                    // == n for all 129 files
}
```

4) CLASS A (6 files, verified 6/6 zero residue)
```c
struct ArcA {
    u32 tag;
    char archiveName[0x24];        // image #1 only
    u32 count;
    ArcEntry members[count];
    /* then image #2..#N positioned by the 4k rule below */
};
// image k (1-based) name offset must satisfy: off % 32 == (4*k) % 32
size_t align_image(size_t off, int k) {
    size_t want = (4u * (unsigned)k) % 32u;
    return off + (want + 32u - (off % 32u)) % 32u;
}
// image 1 has the tag word, images 2..N do not:
//   { char name[0x24]; u32 count; ArcEntry members[count]; }
```

### 18.988 CLASS-B TRAILER is a RECORD whose first word equals the count

1) OBSERVATION
The bytes after the count*20 record area are BINARY (no strings), and their
first u32 equals the record count:
```
entry                       dl    cnt   rec_end trailer  trailer words
e000_000_001_0102.bin       1952   96    1924    28       {96,  1, -20, 1126, 2, 0, 1}
e000_000_002_0102.bin       8064  402    8044    20       {402, 0, -66,  361, 2}
e000_020_001_0102.bin       7264  362    7244    20       {362, 0, -53, 1213, 2}
e000_020_002_0102.bin       8064  402    8044    20       {402, 0, -66,  361, 2}
e000_020_003_0102.bin       9120  455    9104    16       {455, 0, -52, 1085}
e000_020_004_0103.bin       8992  448    8964    28       {448, 0, -90,  478, 2, 0, 0}
```

2) INTERPRETATION
```
- the trailer is not a string table: it is a RECORD
- its first word == count (same value as payload+0x00)
- its length varies: 16, 20, 28 bytes observed
- 20 bytes = one full record
- 16 bytes = a record truncated by 4 bytes
- 28 bytes = a record plus 8 trailing bytes (padding or an extra field pair)
```
=> the file appears to be bracketed: header count + count records + a FOOTER
   record that repeats the count. This is a terminator/validation record.
=> the variable length of that footer is still not explained.

3) WHAT IS CONFIRMED
```
payload = { u32 count;
            count * 20-byte records {flag, delta, size, type, value};
            footer record beginning with the SAME count value }
```

4) STILL OPEN
```
- why the footer is truncated (16) or padded (28) in some entries
- exact semantics of the footer's remaining fields (delta/size/type)
- semantics of size/value inside the main records
```

5) METHOD NOTE
The trailer was directly read, not inferred: its bytes are binary and start with
the count value, which rules out the "variable string tail" hypothesis of 18.987.

### 18.989 CLASS-B FOOTER STATISTICS: variable in 4-byte units (0..28)

Measurement over 103 entries (four lip archives).

1) DISTRIBUTION
```
footer = dataLen - 4 - count*20
footer distribution : {0:13, 4:4, 8:18, 12:19, 16:13, 20:16, 24:5, 28:15}
dataLen % 20        : {0:13, 4:29, 8:9, 12:33, 16:19}
count % 2           : {0:54, 1:49}
```

2) WHAT THE NUMBERS SAY
```
- the footer is NOT fixed (28 does not hold: only 15/103)
- it is NOT zero either (only 13/103)
- every observed footer length is a MULTIPLE OF 4, values 0..28
=> the region after the count*20 records is variable-length in 4-byte units
```
That is consistent with one of two structures (both still open):
```
(a) a terminator record whose payload is variable-length
(b) the LAST record having a variable-length extension
```
No decision between (a) and (b) is justified by the data yet.

3) WHAT IS SOLID (unchanged from 18.987/18.988)
```
payload[0x00] = record count (values 96..455 observed)
payload[0x04] = start of count 20-byte records {flag, delta, size, type, value}
the 20-byte stride is directly observable
the trailing region begins with a u32 equal to the count in the samples inspected
```

4) NEGATIVE RESULTS RECORDED (avoid future repeats)
```
- fixed 28-byte footer: refuted (15/103)
- fixed 20-byte footer: refuted (16/103)
- variable STRING tail : refuted (bytes are binary, not text)
```

### 18.990 CLASS-B: record array is integral in 29/103; others end mid-record

1) MEASUREMENT
```
(dataLen - 4) % 20 == 0 :  29 / 103 entries
   for those 29:
      footer =  0  ->  (dataLen-4)/20 == count      (e.g. e102_040_001: 2784 -> 139)
      footer = 20  ->  (dataLen-4)/20 == count + 1  (e.g. e000_000_002: 8064 -> 403)
(dataLen - 4) % 20 != 0 :  74 / 103 entries (footer 4/8/12/16/24/28)
```

2) WHAT THIS MEANS
```
a) when the payload is an exact multiple of 20 bytes, the u32 at +0x00 is
   EITHER the record count (footer 0) OR the record count minus one (footer 20).
   => the field at +0x00 is not always "count"; it may be a last-index or a
      count that excludes a terminator record.
b) the other 74 entries END MID-RECORD (payload size is 4 mod 20, 8 mod 20, ...).
   A fixed 20-byte-only record array cannot produce that.
   => SOME records must have a VARIABLE-LENGTH extension.
```

3) HYPOTHESIS (marked as such, with its test)
```
【推测】records carry a variable-length part, most likely when a flag in the
record header indicates it (the first field is observed as 1 or 2).
验证法: parse records sequentially from +0x04; for each record read the flag;
        if the cumulative position reaches dataLen exactly, the model is right.
        If a mismatch appears, print the offending record index.
```

4) NEGATIVE RESULTS ACCUMULATED (do not repeat)
```
fixed 28-byte footer   : refuted (15/103)
fixed 20-byte footer   : refuted (16/103)
string tail            : refuted (binary bytes)
pure 20-byte array     : refuted (74/103 end mid-record)
```

```
"EVENT_VOICE" and "lipsyncView.c" sit next to the path format.
=> the lip archives carry LIPSYNC (mouth shape) keyframe data for voice events.
=> the 20-byte records observed in the payload are lipsync keyframes:

   and value a mouth-shape parameter. This is CONSISTENT with the measured data
   but the individual field semantics are NOT yet verified in code.
```

4) WHY THE EARLIER STRUCTURAL SEARCHES WERE HARD
```
lipsync keyframe streams are typically variable-length (silence gaps are encoded
as deltas with occasional resync records), which explains:
  - 29/103 entries being an exact multiple of 20 bytes (no gaps)
  - 74/103 entries ending "mid-record" (the last keyframe carries a variable tail)
All five tested fixed/variable stride models failed (18.987..18.990), which is
consistent with a stream that is not a homogeneous record array.
```

0x81181FA0  movw  r6, #0x414c ; movt r6, #0x812b    ; stack canary address
0x81181FA8  ldr   r2, [r6] ; str r2, [sp, #4]
0x81181FAC  adds  r4, r0, #0                        ; r4 = arg0
0x81181FAE  cmp   r1, #0
0x81181FB0  bgt   0x81181FB8
0x81181FB2  cmp   r1, #0
0x81181FB4  blt   0x81181FDA
0x81181FB6  b     0x81181FBE                        ; case r1 == 0
0x81181FB8  cmp   r1, #1
0x81181FBA  ble   0x81181FC6                        ; case r1 == 1
0x81181FBC  b     0x81181FDA                        ; case r1 >  1
0x81181FBE  adds  r0, r4, #0
0x81181FC0  bl    0x81181F1A                        ; branch A
0x81181FC6  adds  r0, r4, #0
0x81181FC8  add   r1, sp, #0
0x81181FCA  movs  r4, #0
0x81181FCC  bl    0x81181D90                        ; branch B (r1 == 1)
0x81181FD0  cmp   r0, #0
0x81181FD2  beq   0x81181FD6
0x81181FD4  movs  r4, #1
0x81181FD6  sxtb  r0, r4
0x81181FD8  b     0x81181FFA
0x81181FDA  movs  r5, #1
0x81181FDC  add   r1, sp, #0
0x81181FDE  adds  r0, r4, #0
0x81181FE0  bl    0x81181D90                        ; branch C
0x81181FE4  cmp   r0, #0
0x81181FE6  bne   0x81181FF8
```

2) WHAT THIS ESTABLISHES
```
- signature: f(void* arg0, int mode)
- the loader is a MODE DISPATCHER, not a straight-line parser:
      mode == 0  -> 0x81181F1A
      mode == 1  -> 0x81181D90(arg0, stackbuf)  -> boolean result
      mode >  1  -> 0x81181D90(arg0, stackbuf)  -> other post-processing
- it has a stack canary (0x812B414C) and returns a sign-extended byte
```

3) NEXT TARGETS (exact)
```
0x81181F1A   : branch A
0x81181D90   : branches B/C, takes (arg0, &stackbuf) and returns bool
one of these two contains the actual class-B archive open + entry selection +
payload walk.
```

4) METHOD NOTE
The chain now is:
```
0x8106DD08 -> 0x8115FCB4 (tramp1) -> 0x8115FD74 (tramp2) -> 0x81181F9C (dispatch)
                                                     -> 0x81181F1A / 0x81181D90
```
Every step recorded with its role, so no round is wasted re-reading trampolines.

### 18.995 LIP: 0x81181D90 is a NAME BUILDER (shares helpers with the LBN reader)

1) DISASSEMBLY (the mode-1/mode>1 branch target of 0x81181F9C)
```asm
0x81181D90  push.w {r4,r5,r6,r7,r8,sb,sl,fp,lr}
0x81181D94  subw   sp, sp, #0x414            ; 1044-byte frame
0x81181D98  movw   r2,#0x414c ; movt r2,#0x812b
0x81181DA2  str.w  r2,[sp,#0x40c]            ; stack canary
0x81181DA6  adds   r4, r0, #0                ; r4 = arg0 (source)
0x81181DAC  add.w  fp, sp, #0x204
0x81181DB0  cmp    r1, #0
0x81181DB4  add    r0, sp, #0x100            ; default buffer when arg1==0
0x81181DC0  add    r0, sp, #0x104
0x81181DC2  mov    r1, sp
0x81181DC4  blx    0x812b22d0                ; string init/copy
0x81181DC8  mov    r0, sp
0x81181DCA  blx    0x812b22e0                ; strlen
0x81181DD0  add.w  r2, sp, r0                ; dest = base + len
0x81181DD6  ldrsb.w r0,[r3]                  ; loop over source bytes
0x81181DDA  cbnz   r0, 0x81181DE4
0x81181DE4  adds   r4, #1
0x81181DE6  strb.w r0,[r2,#0x104]            ; append
0x81181DEE  cmp    r4, #0xff                 ; max 255 chars
```

2) WHAT IT IS
```
a NAME/LABEL BUILDER: copies a base string, appends arg0 up to 255 bytes.
=> this is NOT the archive parser; it prepares a name (consistent with building
   entry names of the form e<AAA>_<BBB>_<CCC>_<DDDD>.bin).
```

3) CROSS-VALIDATION WITH THE LBN READER (important)
```
0x812b22e0 is used here to get the name length.
The SAME function 0x812b22e0 was identified in 5GG as the LBN entry-name
length function.
=> two independent work lines converge on the same runtime helper, which
   strengthens both identifications.
```

4) CHAIN STATUS
```
0x8106DD08 -> 0x8115FCB4 (tramp1) -> 0x8115FD74 (tramp2)
           -> 0x81181F9C (mode dispatcher)
              mode 0   -> 0x81181F1A   [STILL TO READ: likely the parser]
              mode >=1 -> 0x81181D90   [name builder, decoded here]
```

5) NEXT (single target)
```
0x81181F1A is now the only unread branch and therefore the likely location of
the class-B open + entry selection + payload walk.
```

### 18.996 LIP CHAIN IS A NAME-REGISTRATION API, NOT THE PARSER (honest conclusion)

1) 0x81181F1A DISASSEMBLY (mode 0 branch)
```asm
0x81181F1A  push  {r4,r5,r6,lr}
0x81181F1C  sub.w sp, sp, #0x238
0x81181F20  movw  r6,#0x414c ; movt r6,#0x812b
0x81181F28  ldr   r1,[r6] ; str r1,[sp,#0x230]    ; stack canary
0x81181F2E  strb.w r5,[sp]
0x81181F34  add   r0, sp, #0x130 ; mov r1, sp
0x81181F38  blx   0x812b22d0                      ; string init
0x81181F3C  mov   r0, sp ; blx 0x812b22e0         ; strlen
0x81181F42  movw  r1,#0x174 ; movt r1,#0x813b     ; global @ 0x813B0174
0x81181F4A  ldr   r3,[r1]                          ; global base pointer
0x81181F4C  add.w r1, sp, r0
0x81181F54  ... append arg0 bytes, max 255
```

2) THE GLOBAL IS RUNTIME-INITIALIZED
```
reading 0x813B0174 from the file gives 0x00000000 (and the same for 0x813B014C)
=> these are BSS globals, assigned at runtime
=> the base prefix cannot be read statically
```

3) CORRECTED ROLE OF THE PEELED CHAIN
```
0x8115FCB4 -> 0x8115FD74 -> 0x81181F9C -> {0x81181F1A , 0x81181D90}
```
Both branches build a NAME by appending arg0 to a prefix
(one uses a stack buffer, one uses the global at 0x813B0174).
=> the chain is a NAME REGISTRATION / VALIDATION API, not the lipsync parser.
=> earlier assumption (18.992/18.994) that it led to the payload parser was WRONG
   and is corrected here.

4) WHAT THIS MEANS FOR GAP B
```
container layer : CLOSED (129/129 EOF_EXACT)                     [verified]
semantics       : EVENT_VOICE lipsync, path sound/lip/e%03d%03d.arc [rodata]
loader/parser   : NOT YET LOCATED
                  the peeled chain only registers/builds names
```
=> the payload structure still has to be obtained from a different function,
   one that actually reads the bytes of an entry (not one that formats a path).

5) NEXT STEP (revised)
```
Follow the RETURN VALUE of the chain: 0x8106DCF0 stores r0 into [r4,#0x24]
BEFORE the path is built; the object [r4] is the consumer. Find who reads
[r4+0x24] later and walks the entry payload -> that is the parser.
Alternative: search for functions that compare 4-byte tags like the archive tag
values (8, 21, 23, 46) rather than name strings.
```

### 18.997 CLASS-B PAYLOAD: sixth model refuted; byte-side approach exhausted

1) NEW TEST (this round)
```
hypothesis: payload = { u32 count1; count1*20 records; u32 count2; count2*20 records }
test      : parse count1, then read u32 at 4+count1*20 as count2, check total
result    : OK = 0 / 103   -> REFUTED
```

2) COMPLETE LIST OF REFUTED MODELS (all measured, not guessed)
```
(1) fixed 28-byte footer                      15/103
(2) fixed 20-byte footer                      16/103
(3) variable string tail                      bytes are binary
(4) pure 20-byte fixed array                  74/103 end mid-record
(5) type-driven variable record sizes         5 variants, all failed
(6) two-section count/records repetition      0/103
```

3) WHAT THE DATA STILL SAYS (facts, not models)
```
- payload[0x00] is a small integer (96..507) that correlates with entry length
- records with 20-byte stride ARE present (directly observable in the head of
  every sampled payload)
- the payload total length is NOT always a multiple of 20 after the 4-byte header
=> a straightforward homogeneous record array is excluded, and every simple
   variation tried so far is excluded too.
```

4) CONCLUSION ON METHOD
```
Byte-side inference has reached its limit for this format: six independent
models have been refuted by measurement.
The structure must be taken from CODE, not from bytes.
The name-registration chain peeled in 18.992..18.996 is NOT the parser (18.996),
so the parser still has to be located by a different route.
```

```
a) find the consumer of the object field [r4+0x24] written at 0x8106DCF0
b) search for comparisons against the archive tag values (8, 21, 23, 46)
c) use the lipsyncView.c debug path: the debug viewer necessarily parses the

```

### 18.999 NEGATIVE: the two candidate "callbacks" are NOT code; interpretation revised

1) TEST
```
disassemble at 0x8100270D : 0 valid instructions (first byte not a valid Thumb opcode)
disassemble at 0x8100279D : nonsense stream (ldrh r4,[r3,r0] repeated, etc.)
=> neither address is a function start.
```

2) WHAT THIS MEANS
```
The reading in 18.998 ("registration code storing two function pointers")
is NOT confirmed. The two values 0x8100270D / 0x8100279D are most likely DATA
addresses (strings or table entries), not callbacks.
=> 18.998's "callbacks" label is RETRACTED.
```

3) WHY THE MOVW/MOVT PAIRING WAS WRONG
```
the code at 0x81002664.. is a long byte-wise initialisation interleaved with
movw/movt pairs; pairing r6/r7 by register name across interleaved instructions
is unreliable. A movt for the same register may belong to a different value.
=> register-based pairing must be checked against the actual instruction window
   before concluding a pointer value.
```

### 18.1001 CLASS-B ASSET INVENTORY: 5,159 lip entries, name-field semantics

Measured over all 129 non-table .arc files.

1) TOTALS
```
matched entries (names of form e<AAA>_<BBB>_<CCC>_<DDDD>.bin) : 5159
distinct AAA : 17
distinct BBB : 9
distinct CCC : 137   (values 001..137, each appearing about 128-130 times)
distinct DDDD: 17
```

2) DDDD VALUE SET (voice code)
```
0102 0103 0104 0105 0106 0107 0108 0111
0202 0203 0204 0205 0206 0207 0208 0210 0211
```
Pattern: two groups (01xx / 02xx) each with a two-digit subtype in
{02,03,04,05,06,07,08,10,11}. This is consistent with a VOICE CATEGORY code
(first digit = group, last two = variant), i.e. 17 voice categories total.

3) CCC = SEQUENCE / VARIANT INDEX
```
001..137, each appearing ~128-130 times
=> every archive contributes one entry per variant index
=> 137 variants x ~129 archives is the natural reading, matching 5159 entries
```

4) WHAT A PORT CAN DO WITH THIS
```c
// voice/lipsync asset set:
//   for each of 17 AAA groups, 9 BBB variants, 137 CCC sequence slots,
//   pick one of 17 DDDD voice categories -> the corresponding .bin entry
// The archive is chosen by (AAA, BBB):  "sound/lip/e%03d%03d.arc"
```
=> the asset inventory is complete and countable; no unknown members remain.

5) WHAT IS STILL OPEN
```
- meaning of AAA (character? scene?) and BBB (its 9 variants)
- meaning of the DDDD first digit group split (01xx vs 02xx)
- the payload structure of each .bin (18.987..18.999, unresolved)
```

      case 9:  fun_81121040(obj[0x112],0); *obj = 10; break;

               *obj = 0xB; break;
      default: fun_810485CC(obj[0x107]); fun_8103F2F6(obj[0x119],obj[0x10B]);

### 18.1011 GAP ANIMATION FORMAT: implementable spec (from 5S8/5T0/5T1/4DM)

Status: consolidation of existing sections (75 GAP-related sections exist).
Covers the 6,972 .gap files, the largest format group in the data set (18.1010).

1) FILE STRUCTURE (from 5S8.1)
```c
struct GapFile {
    Gfs0Header hdr;      // 48 bytes: magic "GFS0" at +0x00,
                         // +0x04 = 01 10 50 90, +0x14 = 0xFD
    Bone bones[82];      // 82 variable-length bone records
};
struct Bone {
    u8    nameLen;       // u8  (NOT u16 - differs from .GMD/.GFS)
    char  name[nameLen]; // e.g. "RootNode", "Hips", "RightHandThumb1"
    u8    meta[3];       // 3 bytes (channel count / flags)
    f32   matrix[16];    // 64 bytes, 4x4 (identity diagonal 3F800000)
    u8    channels[];    // variable channel data, 0 .. ~3000 bytes
};
// minimum record = 1 + nameLen + 67
// average        = 119578 / 82 ~= 1458 bytes per bone
// sample size    = 119626 bytes (pcp201_1.GAP)
```

2) MINIMUM RECORD PROOF (from 5S8.2, three different name lengths)
```
bone            nameLen   spacing   spacing - nameLen - 1
RootNode           8        76            67
Spine1             6        74            67
Spine2             6        74            67
=> 67 = 64-byte matrix + 3-byte meta   (base block confirmed)
```

3) SPACING DISTRIBUTION (from 5S8.3)
```
minimum 74, maximum 3140 (42x range)
static bones  (no channels) : ~74 .. 80
animated bones (channels)   : up to 3140
```

4) KEYFRAMES (from 5T0/5T1)
```
keyframe = [ time f32 ][ value f32 ] pair, little-endian
timeline is variable-length; values are +2-level quantized
verified 158 / 159 samples in the cited section
```

5) CHANNEL PATHS (from 4DM)
```
31 keyType path templates are documented, plus a suffix/target system
coverage reported as 2/3 of 6 remaining in that section (partially open)
```

6) DIRECTLY PORTABLE C SKELETON
```c
typedef struct { f32 t, v; } GapKey;
typedef struct {
    const char* path;   // e.g. "translation.x"
    int   nkeys;
    GapKey* keys;       // [time][value] pairs
} GapChannel;
typedef struct {
    char name[64];
    f32  bind[16];      // 4x4 bind matrix
    u8   meta[3];
    int  nchannels;
    GapChannel* ch;
} GapBone;
typedef struct { GapBone bones[82]; } GapFile;

size_t gap_parse(const u8* p, size_t n, GapFile* out) {
    // 1. check magic "GFS0" at +0
    // 2. off = 48
    // 3. for (b = 0; b < 82; b++) {
    //       nameLen = p[off++];
    //       name    = p + off; off += nameLen;
    //       meta    = p + off; off += 3;
    //       memcpy(out->bones[b].bind, p + off, 64); off += 64;
    //       channels follow until the next bone's nameLen (variable length)
    //    }
    // NOTE: channel byte count is NOT stored explicitly in the record head;
    //       it must be derived from meta/keyType rules (4DM) - this part is
    //       the remaining open item.
}
```

7) HONEST OPEN ITEM
```
The base record (name + 3 meta + 64-byte matrix) is confirmed by three samples.
The VARIABLE CHANNEL REGION has no explicit length field in the base record,
so its length must be derived from meta[3] (channel count/flags) and the
keyType rules - that derivation is documented partially in 4DM and is the
remaining gap in this format.
```

8) WHY THIS MATTERS
```
.gap = 6972 files = 66 % of all resource files (18.1010)
header + base record + keyframe pair format are now specified in one place
```

### 18.1012 GAP HEADER BYTE-LEVEL CHECK: u32 length prefix, not u8+meta

Measurement on dance/player/p5/pose/pcp201_1.GAP (119,626 bytes).

1) RAW HEADER
```
0x0000  47 46 53 30              "GFS0"
0x0004  01 10 50 90
0x0010  01 10 50 90
0x0014  00 01 00 fd
0x0018  00 01 d3 3a              0x1D33A = 119,610 (near the file size 119,626)
0x0020  00 00 00 08
0x0028  40 00 00 01
0x002C  40 d5 55 55
0x0030  00 00 00 52              0x52 = 82  <-- BONE COUNT
0x0038  00 00 00 08              <-- length prefix, value 8
0x003C  "RootNode"               8 bytes, ends at 0x43
0x0070  3f 80 00 00 x4           1.0f x4
0x0084  00 00 00 04              <-- next record prefix, value 4
0x0088  "root"
```

2) KEY NUMBERS THAT CHECK OUT
```
RootNode record span = 0x84 - 0x38 = 76 bytes   == 5S8's documented spacing 76
bone count word  = 82 at 0x30                    == 5S8's "82 bones"
```

3) DISCREPANCY WITH 5S8
```
5S8 states the record head is:  u8 nameLen; char name[]; u8 meta[3]; f32 matrix[16]
the bytes show:                 u32 nameLen (00 00 00 08); char name[]
Both have the same total head size (1 + 3 == 4), so the SIZE conclusions of 5S8
are unaffected, but the FIELD SPLIT is different:
  - either the length is a u32 (0x38..0x3B) and there is NO 3-byte meta, or
  - the length is the byte at 0x3B (= 0x08) and the three bytes 00 00 00 are a
    prefix/padding
The evidence favours a u32 length prefix, because at the second record the same
pattern repeats (00 00 00 04 followed by "root").
```

4) WHAT THIS CHANGES FOR THE PARSER
```c
// revised reading (measured):
u32 nameLen;             // 4 bytes
char name[nameLen];      // no terminator
u8  rest[64];            // 64 bytes (matrix per 5S8) - internal split still open
// total base = 4 + nameLen + 64 = 68 + nameLen
// RootNode: 68 + 8 = 76  (matches the measured span)
```

5) HONEST STATUS
```
confirmed : magic, bone count 82, record span 76 for RootNode, u32 prefix pattern
open      : exact internal split of the 64 bytes after the name (matrix + meta vs
            matrix only), and the rule that determines the variable channel length
```

6) METHOD NOTE
This is a byte-level check against an earlier documented model (5S8). The model's
sizes survive; its field split does not. Recorded rather than silently adjusted.

              neck=80(0x50), head=81(0x51), RightShoulder=54(0x36), RightArm=55(0x37)
byte  2    : 0x00 (flag / padding in all ten sampled records)
byte  3    : nameLen (u8)
then       : char name[nameLen]
then       : u8 matrix[64]        (4x4, big-endian floats per the header endianness)
then       : u8 channels[channelBytes]   (VARIABLE, measured below)
```
=> base size = 3 + 1 + nameLen + 64 = 68 + nameLen
   RootNode: 68 + 8 = 76  -> matches the previously documented spacing 76

3) ENDIANNESS (new, decisive)
```
integers in the header and in the record head are BIG-ENDIAN:
  0x18 : 00 01 d3 3a  -> 119610 (file length minus 16) when read BE
  0x30 : 00 00 00 52  -> 82 (bone count) when read BE
  0x38 : prefix 00 00 00 -> bone id 0
=> a little-endian parser produces invalid lengths immediately (observed).
```
The previously documented model (5S8) did not record this endianness.

4) CHANNEL LENGTHS (measured by scanning to the next valid record)
```
RootNode 0   root 574   Hips 1510   Spine 880   Spine1 0   Spine2 0
neck 664     head 1852  RightShoulder 1744      RightArm 2698
static bones (Spine1/Spine2) have 0 channel bytes, matching 5S8's
"static bones ~74..80 bytes spacing"
```

5) WHAT THIS MEANS FOR A PARSER
```c
// big-endian walk
u16 id   = (p[o] << 8) | p[o+1];
u8  flag = p[o+2];
u8  len  = p[o+3];
char* name = p + o + 4;
const u8* matrix = p + o + 4 + len;          // 64 bytes
const u8* chan   = matrix + 64;              // channelBytes (NOT yet derivable)
o_next = /* must be found by rule; see 6 */
```

6) REMAINING OPEN ITEM (narrowed)
```
The channel region length is NOT stored in the record head. It was measured here
by scanning for the next valid record. To parse without scanning, the rule must
be derived - likely from the first fields of the channel block itself.
=> record order is NOT sorted by bone id (ids 0,1,2,25,26,27,80,81,54,55 observed)
   so the file order is a traversal order, not an index order.
```

7) STATUS
```
GAP header        : magic GFS0, big-endian, bone count 82 at +0x30
GAP record head   : DECODED (id/flag/nameLen/name/matrix)  [this section]
GAP channel block : variable length measured for 10 bones; internal format OPEN
```

### 18.1014 GAP CHANNEL BLOCKS = BIG-ENDIAN FLOAT STREAMS

Measurement on pcp201_1.GAP channel regions located by 18.1013.

1) FIRST VALUES OF THREE CHANNEL BLOCKS
```
root  @0x0CC  len 574 : f32 BE = 1.8, 1.83, 1.87, 1.93, 2.33, 3.23 ...
Hips  @0x352  len 1510: f32 BE = 1.07, 1.13, 1.33, 1.37, 1.4, 1.43 ...
Spine @0x981  len 880 : f32 BE = 2.27, 2.37, 2.53, 2.7, 3.1, 3.25 ...
```
The byte patterns (3f e6 66 66, 3f 88 88 89, 40 11 11 11) decode as sensible
floats when read BIG-ENDIAN, and as garbage when read little-endian.

2) WHAT THIS CONFIRMS
```
- the GAP endianness identified in 18.1013 extends to the channel floats
- the channel block is a stream of f32 values
- this matches 5T1's documented keyframe form: [time f32][value f32] pairs
```

3) LENGTH ARITHMETIC (measured lengths from 18.1013, scan-based)
```
root : 574 bytes -> 574 / 8 = 71.75   (not an integer number of pairs)
Hips : 1510       -> 188.75
Spine: 880        -> 110
```
=> either the scan-based boundary is off by a few bytes, or the block ends with a
   non-pair trailer. Spine happens to divide by 8 exactly (110 pairs); root and
   Hips do not.
=> the exact block framing (header word / trailer) is STILL OPEN; the float-pair
   interpretation of the body is supported by the observed values.

4) FLOATS AS DATA (what they look like)
```
root  : 1.8 .. 3.23        increasing small values
Hips  : 1.07 .. 1.43
Spine : 2.27 .. 3.25
=> these look like TIMES (seconds) or translation components in cm, matching
   the project's documented world unit (cm) for models
=> the interleaved second float of each pair would then be the VALUE; that
   pairing has NOT been verified on this sample yet
```

5) STATUS
```
GAP header          : CLOSED (magic GFS0, big-endian, 82 bones at +0x30)
GAP record head     : CLOSED (u16 BE id, u8 flag, u8 nameLen, name, 64B matrix)
GAP channel body    : BIG-ENDIAN f32 stream (this section)
GAP channel framing : OPEN (exact header/trailer of the variable block)
```

6) NEXT
```
compare a static bone (channel bytes 0) with an animated one in a second file to
determine whether the block starts with a count word; alternatively use the fact
that Spine divides exactly by 8 to anchor the frame.

### 18.1015 GAP CHANNEL FRAMING: 6-byte remainder suggests per-channel sub-records

Analysis of the scan-based channel lengths measured in 18.1013.

1) REMAINDER ARITHMETIC
```
bone   block bytes   pairs (x8)   remainder
root         574          71         6
Hips        1510         188         6
Spine        880         110         0
```
=> two of three blocks have a 6-byte remainder; one divides exactly.
=> a flat f32-pair array does not describe the region consistently.

2) INFERENCE (marked as hypothesis, with its test)
```
【推测】the channel region is a SEQUENCE OF PER-CHANNEL SUB-RECORDS,
one per animated channel (keyType path), each with its own small header.
This matches 4DM's "31 keyType path templates" model: a bone is animated on a
subset of those paths, and each contributes a sub-record (count + key pairs).
```
验证法:
```
a) take a bone whose channel bytes are known (root 574) and try to split it into
   sub-records by scanning for plausible count words followed by 8*count bytes;
   accept the split only if it consumes the whole region exactly.
b) cross-check with 4DM: the number of sub-records per bone should equal the
   number of keyType paths listed for that bone in the animation data.
```

3) WHAT IS SOLID
```
- channel region bytes are big-endian f32 values (18.1014)
- the first values look like times or translation components in cm
- static bones (Spine1 / Spine2) have zero channel bytes
- block sizes measured: root 574, Hips 1510, Spine 880, Spine1 0, Spine2 0,
  neck 664, head 1852, RightShoulder 1744, RightArm 2698
```

4) WHAT IS NOT SOLID
```
- the exact framing (header/trailer) of the channel region
- whether the 6-byte remainder is a trailer, a padding, or evidence that the
  scan-based boundary is off by a few bytes
- the mapping from channel sub-records to keyType paths
```

5) HONEST STATUS OF GAP (.gap, 6,972 files = 66 % of resources)
```
header          CLOSED   (GFS0, big-endian, 82 bones at +0x30)
record head     CLOSED   (u16 BE id, u8 flag, u8 nameLen, name, 64-byte matrix)
channel body    PARTIAL  (big-endian f32 values confirmed; framing open)
channel framing OPEN     (this section narrows it to per-channel sub-records)
```

### 18.1016 GAP CHANNEL BLOCKS SHARE AN IDENTICAL 16-BYTE TAIL

2) THE MEASUREMENT
```
bone   block len   last 16 bytes
root        574    3f800000 3f800000 3f800000 00010000
Hips       1510    3f800000 3f800000 3f800000 00010000
Spine       880    3f800000 3f800000 3f800000 00010000
```
=> three values 1.0f (big-endian 0x3F800000) followed by the bytes 00 01 00 00.

2) WHY THIS IS DECISIVE
```
Three DIFFERENT bones (root / Hips / Spine) with different animated content end
with EXACTLY the same 16 bytes. Random float data would not do that.
=> the tail is a STRUCTURAL element: either
   (a) a fixed terminator record, or
   (b) the final keyframe record of a "scale = (1,1,1)" channel,
      followed by a 4-byte word 0x00010000.
```

3) ARITHMETIC AFTER REMOVING THE 16-BYTE TAIL
```
root  : 574 - 16 = 558    -> 558 / 8 = 69.75   (not integral)
Hips  : 1510 - 16 = 1494  -> 1494 / 8 = 186.75 (not integral)
Spine : 880 - 16 = 864    -> 864 / 8 = 108     (integral)
```
=> removing a fixed tail does not make all three blocks an integral number of
   8-byte pairs. Combined with 18.1015 this further supports the model:
    the channel region is a SEQUENCE of per-channel sub-records of differing
    sizes, and the identical tail is the last of them or a terminator.

4) WHAT IS NOW SOLID
```
- endianness: big-endian integers AND floats (18.1013 / 18.1014)
- record head: u16 BE bone id, u8 flag, u8 nameLen, name, 64-byte matrix
- channel body: big-endian f32 data
- channel block tail: 3 x 1.0f + 0x00010000   <-- new, identical across bones
- static bones: zero-length channel block
```

5) WHAT IS STILL OPEN
```
- the sub-record framing inside the channel body (per-channel count + keys)
- whether the identical tail is a terminator or the last "scale" keyframe
- mapping of sub-records to the 31 keyType paths (4DM)
```

6) NEXT EXPERIMENT (one step)
```
Locate a bone with a SMALL channel block (e.g. neck, 664 bytes) and check whether
its tail is the same 16 bytes. If yes, the tail is a file-wide terminator; then
subtract 16 and try to split the remainder into {u16 count; count*8} sub-records.
```

### 18.1017 GAP CHANNEL BLOCKS END WITH A SCALE KEYFRAME (1,1,1) + 0x00010000

Verification of the tail found in 18.1016, extended to seven bones.

1) RESULTS
```
bone            channel bytes   tail 16 bytes                     exact match
root                  574       3f800000 3f800000 3f800000 00010000   YES
Hips                 1510       3f800000 3f800000 3f800000 00010000   YES
Spine                 880       3f800000 3f800000 3f800000 00010000   YES
neck                  664       3f800000 3f800000 3f800000 00010000   YES
head                 1852       3f800000 3f800000 3f800000 00010000   YES
RightArm             2698       3f800000 3f800000 3f800000 00010000   YES
RightShoulder        1744       3f7fffff 3f800000 3f800000 00010000   NEAR
```
RightShoulder's first value 0x3F7FFFFF decodes as 0.99999994 - the float rounding
of 1.0, i.e. the same structural value.

2) CONCLUSION
```
Every animated bone's channel block terminates with:
    three big-endian floats approximately equal to 1.0  (a SCALE keyframe)
    followed by the 4-byte word 0x00010000
```
=> this is a structural terminator, present in 7/7 tested bones.
=> it is the most reliable anchor found so far for the channel region layout.

3) REVISED MODEL OF THE CHANNEL REGION
```
channel_region = [ per-channel sub-records ... ]
                 + [ scale keyframe: 1.0, 1.0, 1.0 ]     (12 bytes)
                 + [ 0x00010000 ]                        (4 bytes)
total trailer = 16 bytes, identical (up to float rounding) in every bone
```
=> the remaining open question is only the sub-record framing BEFORE the trailer.

4) ARITHMETIC AFTER THE TRAILER (updated from 18.1016)
```
root  : 574 - 16 = 558
Hips  : 1510 - 16 = 1494
Spine : 880 - 16 = 864   (= 108 * 8)
neck  : 664 - 16 = 648
head  : 1852 - 16 = 1836
```
Different bones still have non-multiple-of-8 remainders, consistent with a
sequence of variable-size sub-records rather than one flat pair array.

5) WHAT A PORT CAN DO NOW
```c
// walk a bone's channel region from its end:
const u8* tail = chan + channelBytes - 16;   // scale keyframe + word
// verify: BE f32 at tail+0/4/8 ~= 1.0 and BE u32 at tail+12 == 0x00010000
// then treat [chan, tail) as the per-channel sub-record area
```

6) STILL OPEN
```
- sub-record framing inside [chan, tail)
- mapping of sub-records to keyType paths (4DM)
```

### 18.1018 GAP FORMAT: CONSOLIDATED FINAL SPEC (supersedes 18.1011 head layout)

Consolidates 18.1011, 18.1013, 18.1014, 18.1016, 18.1017. All values measured on
dance/player/p5/pose/pcp201_1.GAP (119,626 bytes). ASCII-only.

1) FILE LAYOUT
```c
struct GapFile {
    u8  hdr[0x38];          // 56 bytes before the first record
                            // +0x00 "GFS0"
                            // +0x18 BE u32 = 119610  (file length - 16)
                            // +0x30 BE u32 = 82      (BONE COUNT)
    Bone bones[82];         // variable-length, in traversal order (NOT id order)
};
```

2) ENDIANNESS (decisive, new)
```
ALL 32-bit integer fields AND all floats are BIG-ENDIAN.
A little-endian parser fails immediately on the first record
(0x38 = 00 00 00 08 decodes as 134217728 LE vs 8 BE).
```

3) BONE RECORD
```c
struct Bone {
    u16 id;                 // BE, e.g. 0 RootNode, 1 root, 2 Hips, 25 Spine,
                            // 26 Spine1, 27 Spine2, 80 neck, 81 head,
                            // 54 RightShoulder, 55 RightArm
    u8  flag;               // 0x00 in all sampled records
    u8  nameLen;
    char name[nameLen];     // "RootNode" / "root" / "Hips" / ...
    u8  matrix[64];         // 4x4, BIG-ENDIAN floats
    u8  channels[];         // variable, see 4)
};
// base size = 4 + nameLen + 64 = 68 + nameLen
// RootNode: 68 + 8 = 76  (matches the independently documented spacing 76)
```

4) CHANNEL REGION (variable, measured)
```
channel bytes observed:
  RootNode 0 | root 574 | Hips 1510 | Spine 880 | Spine1 0 | Spine2 0
  neck 664 | head 1852 | RightShoulder 1744 | RightArm 2698

BODY  : big-endian f32 values (times / translation components in cm)
TAIL  : 16 bytes, IDENTICAL in 7/7 tested bones:
          BE f32 ~= 1.0, 1.0, 1.0      (scale keyframe; 0x3F7FFFFF allowed as
                                         the float rounding of 1.0)
          BE u32 == 0x00010000
```
=> a parser can ANCHOR from the end: tail = channels + channelBytes - 16, verify
   the three ~1.0 floats and the 0x00010000 word, then treat [channels, tail) as
   the per-channel sub-record area.

5) C PARSER SKELETON (big-endian)
```c
static u16 rd16be(const u8* p){ return (u16)((p[0]<<8)|p[1]); }
static u32 rd32be(const u8* p){ return ((u32)p[0]<<24)|((u32)p[1]<<16)
                                     |((u32)p[2]<<8)|p[3]; }
static f32 rdf32be(const u8* p){ u32 v = rd32be(p); f32 f; memcpy(&f,&v,4); return f; }

// walk (requires the next-record rule, see 6)
size_t off = 0x38;
for (int k = 0; k < 82; k++) {
    u16 id    = rd16be(p + off);
    u8  flag  = p[off + 2];
    u8  nlen  = p[off + 3];
    const char* name = (const char*)(p + off + 4);
    const u8* matrix = p + off + 4 + nlen;        // 64 bytes BE floats
    /* channel length must be determined to find the next record */
    off += 4 + nlen + 64 + channelBytes(id, k);
}
```

6) THE ONE REMAINING OPEN ITEM
```
The channel byte count is NOT stored in the record head.
Measured by scanning to the next valid record (18.1013).
The interior of [channels, tail) is a sequence of per-channel sub-records whose
framing is not yet derived; 4DM's 31 keyType path templates are the expected key.
=> until that rule is found, a parser must SCAN for the next valid record, or
   use the 16-byte tail anchor plus a sub-record splitter.
```

7) COVERAGE
```
.gap files = 6972 = 66 % of all resource files (18.1010)
This section supersedes 18.1011 for the header/record layout; 18.1011's
keyframe-pair description remains valid for the BODY values.
```

### 18.1021 GFS0 IS A FAMILY: +0x04 IS A TYPE/VERSION DISCRIMINATOR

Verification of the 18.1020 finding that .env and .epl start with "GFS0".

1) HEADER COMPARISON (byte-level)
```
file              bytes 0x00..0x0F                          content type
.GAP (animation)  "GFS0" 01 10 50 90 00 00 00 01 ...         82 named bone records
.GFS (camera)     "GFS0" 01 10 50 90 ...                     minimal GMD + GAP
.ENV (808 B)      "GFS0" 01 10 51 00 00 00 00 04 ...        BE u32 count = 4, then f32 data
.EPL (588 B)      "GFS0" 01 10 50 30 00 00 00 01 ...        BE u32 count = 1, then f32/matrix data
```
=> the 4 bytes at +0x04 discriminate the content type:
   0x01105090 -> named-bone record structure (GAP / GFS)
   0x01105100 -> ENV content (count + float data, no names)
   0x01105030 -> EPL content (count + float/matrix data, no names)

2) WHAT THIS MEANS
```
GFS0 is a CONTAINER FAMILY, not one format:
   magic "GFS0" at +0x00
   type/version word at +0x04 (big-endian)
   type-specific body
=> the 18.1018 spec (big-endian, header 0x38, u16 id + nameLen + 64-byte matrix +
   16-byte channel tail) applies to the NAMED-BONE type (0x01105090) only.
=> .env / .epl use simpler bodies: a BE u32 count followed by float data.
```

3) COVERAGE IMPACT
```
GFS0 family total: 6972 (.gap) + 287 (.gfs) + 36 (.env) + 51 (.epl) = 7346 files
  of these, 7259 are the named-bone type (documented in 18.1018)
  87 (.env + .epl) are count+float bodies (this section adds the discriminator)
```
=> no .env/.epl file remains unclassified at the container level.

4) WHAT IS STILL OPEN
```
- exact body layout for .env and .epl (count semantics and element sizes)
- the meaning of the 4-value count in .ENV sample
- whether .gfs camera files always use 0x01105090
```

5) NEXT
```
for one .ENV: after the header (0x38?) read the BE u32 count (4) and check whether
the remaining bytes = count * elementSize for a plausible element size. Same for
.EPL with count = 1.
```

### 18.1022 ENV/EPL BODY: the header count is NOT a whole-body element count

1) TEST
For f100_001.ENV (808 bytes, header count = 4) and f100_001.EPL (588 bytes,
header count = 1), all plausible (header size, element size) combinations were
checked against the body size:
```
.ENV  hdr 0x10: elem 4 -> 198, elem 8 -> 99,  elem 12 -> 66
      hdr 0x38: elem 4 -> 188, elem 8 -> 94,  elem 16 -> 47
.EPL  hdr 0x10: elem 4 -> 143
      hdr 0x38: elem 4 -> 133
```
NO combination yields the header count (4 for .ENV, 1 for .EPL).

2) CONCLUSION
```
The u32 at +0x08 in these files is NOT "number of elements that fill the body".
=> either it counts a sub-structure (e.g. matrices / layers / light entries),
   or the body contains variable-length parts.
=> .env/.epl body layout remains OPEN at the element level, although the
   container (GFS0 + type word) is classified (18.1021).
```

3) WHAT IS KNOWN (container level, verified)
```
.ENV  : magic "GFS0", type word 0x01105100, +0x08 = BE u32 4
        then big-endian floats starting near +0x10
        sample values: 0.4705..., 1.0, 0.988...
.EPL  : magic "GFS0", type word 0x01105030, +0x08 = BE u32 1
        then zeros then big-endian floats/matrix-like data
```

### 18.1024 CORRECTION: the type word, not the extension, discriminates GFS0 content

Full scan of all files whose first four bytes are "GFS0".

1) MEASURED TYPE-WORD DISTRIBUTION (big-endian u32 at +0x04)
```
.gap  6972 files : 0x01105090 = 6768   0x01105100 = 204
.gfs   287 files : 0x01105090 = 287
.env    36 files : 0x01105100 =  31    0x01105090 =  5
.epl    51 files : 0x01105070 =  31    0x01105090 =  8   0x01105100 = 7
                   0x01105040 =   3    0x01105030 =  2
.spr6   52 files : separate magic "SPR6" (0x53505236)
```

2) WHAT THIS REFUTES
```
18.1021 suggested the mapping  extension -> type word
    .gap/.gfs -> 0x01105090,  .env -> 0x01105100,  .epl -> 0x01105030
The full scan shows that mapping is NOT strict:
  - 204 .gap files carry 0x01105100
  - 5 .env files carry 0x01105090
  - .epl spans FIVE different type words
=> the EXTENSION is only a naming hint; the TYPE WORD is the real discriminator.
```

3) THE TYPE WORDS OBSERVED SO FAR
```
0x01105090  named-bone record layout (18.1018)      6768 .gap + 287 .gfs + 5 .env + 8 .epl
0x01105100  count + float body (18.1022)             204 .gap + 31 .env + 7 .epl
0x01105070  unknown                                 31 .epl
0x01105040  unknown                                  3 .epl
0x01105030  count + float/matrix body (18.1022)       2 .epl
```

4) WHAT A PARSER MUST DO
```c
if (memcmp(p, "GFS0", 4) != 0) { /* not GFS0 family */ }
u32 type = rd32be(p + 4);
switch (type) {
    case 0x01105090: parse_named_bone_records(p); break;   // 18.1018
    case 0x01105100: parse_count_float_body(p);   break;   // 18.1022 (partial)
    case 0x01105030: parse_count_float_body(p);   break;   // 18.1022 (partial)
    case 0x01105070: /* OPEN */ break;
    case 0x01105040: /* OPEN */ break;
    default:         /* unknown type */ break;
}
```
=> dispatch on the TYPE WORD, never on the file extension.

5) IMPACT ON COVERAGE COUNTS
```
GFS0-family files : 6972 + 287 + 36 + 51 = 7346
  type 0x01105090 (named bones) : 6768 + 287 + 5 + 8   = 7068
  type 0x01105100 (count+float) :  204 + 31 + 7        =  242
  type 0x01105070 (unknown)     :  31
  type 0x01105040 (unknown)     :   3
  type 0x01105030 (count+float) :   2
```
=> the named-bone layout covers 7068 files (not 7259 as stated from the one
   sample); 242 files are count+float; 34 files have two as-yet-unknown types.

6) HONEST CORRECTION
```
18.1021's per-extension mapping is SUPERSEDED by this distribution.
The container classification remains valid; the correspondence to extensions
does not.

### 18.1025 EPL VARIANTS SHARE ONE HEADER SHAPE (types 0x01105040 / 0x01105070)

Samples: ee500.EPL (362 B, type 0x01105040), f108_001.EPL (590 B, type 0x01105070).

1) HEADER COMPARISON
```
offset   type 0x01105040        type 0x01105070
+0x00    "GFS0"                 "GFS0"
+0x04    01 10 50 40            01 10 50 70
+0x08    BE u32 = 1             BE u32 = 1
+0x0C    BE u32 = 0             BE u32 = 0
+0x10    BE u32 = 5             BE u32 = 4
+0x14..  zeros                  zeros
+0x2C    3f800000 (1.0)         3f800000 (1.0)
+0x30    3f800000 3f800000 ...  3f800000 3f800000 ...
```
=> the two previously "unknown" types share the SAME header layout as the other
   EPL variants; they differ only in the type word and in the small count at +0x10.

2) WHAT THIS MEANS
```
The .epl format is UNIFORM at the header level:
   +0x00 magic GFS0
   +0x04 type word (big-endian): 0x01105030 / 0x01105040 / 0x01105070 /
                                 0x01105090 / 0x01105100
   +0x08 constant 1
   +0x10 small count (4 or 5 observed)
   +0x2c first identity/scale floats (1.0, 1.0, 1.0)
=> the type word likely selects a small variation (e.g. how many transform
   entries follow), not a different file format.
```

3) COVERAGE UPDATE
```
all 51 .epl files share this header shape (five type words observed in total).
The two formerly "unknown" types are therefore not unknown formats:
they are standard EPL headers with type-specific content downstream.
=> gap E's ".env/.epl body" item is narrowed to: what does the count at +0x10
   index, and what follows the identity floats.
```

4) STILL OPEN
```
- semantics of the +0x10 count (4 or 5)
- the downstream content after the identity floats
- whether .env (type 0x01105100) shares the same body framing as .epl
```

5) HONEST NOTE
```
This does NOT claim the EPL body is decoded. It removes two "unknown types" from
the unknown list by showing they use the same header as known EPL files.

### 18.1027 *** GAP C SOLVED (field map): DSFT payload = 16-byte header + 80-byte row ***

Full byte dump of stage_format_001.bin payload (96 bytes) from stage_format_table.arc,
cross-checked against the INDEPENDENT runtime measurements of 18.452.

1) DISK PAYLOAD LAYOUT (little-endian)
```
+0x00  "DSFT"        magic
+0x04  u32 = 1
+0x08  u32 = 1
+0x0C  u32 = 60
+0x10  u32 = 101       <-- ROW DATA STARTS HERE (row +0x00)
+0x14  u32 = 0
+0x18  f32 = 75.0
+0x1C  f32 = 180.0
+0x20  f32 = 180.0
+0x24  f32 = 0.0
+0x28  u32 = 0
+0x2C  u32 = 0
+0x30  u32 = 0
+0x34  u32 = 0xFFFFFFFF
+0x38  u32 = 4
+0x3C  u32 = 0
+0x40  u32 = 0
+0x44  u32 = 0
+0x48  u32 = 0x0001006A
+0x4C  u32 = 0
+0x50..+0x5F  zeros
```

2) THE OFFSET RELATION (decisive)
```
runtime row offset = disk payload offset - 0x10
```
Every independently measured runtime field of 18.452 maps onto the disk bytes:
```
18.452 runtime field     value measured   disk offset   disk value        match
+0x00 stageId            101..143         +0x10         101               YES
+0x08 f32                75.000           +0x18         75.0              YES
+0x0C f32                == +0x10         +0x1C         180.0             YES
+0x10 f32                == +0x0C         +0x20         180.0             YES
+0x14 f32                0.000            +0x24         0.0               YES
+0x24 u32                0xFFFFFFFF       +0x34         0xFFFFFFFF        YES
+0x28 u32                in {0,4}         +0x38         4                 YES
+0x38 u32                65639/65647/...  +0x48         0x0001006A=65642  YES
+0x3C u32                0                +0x4C         0                 YES
```

3) WHAT THIS ESTABLISHES
```
- DSFT payload = { "DSFT", 1, 1, 60 } (16 bytes) + one 80-byte row
- the ROW is exactly the runtime structure whose fields 18.452 measured
- therefore the disk->runtime transform is a pure +0x10 shift, no reinterpretation
- the two equal f32 fields (+0x0C == +0x10, both 180.0 here) are confirmed on disk
- the 0xFFFFFFFF sentinel and the {0,4} field are confirmed on disk
```

4) REMAINING SEMANTIC GAP (much smaller now)
```
The FIELD NAMES are still unknown (what do 75.0, 180.0, 180.0, 0.0 mean?).
But the LAYOUT is now fully established and cross-verified in two independent
places (disk payload and runtime structure).
=> a port can already read all DSFT fields; it cannot yet name their semantics.
```

5) IMPLEMENTABLE READER
```c
struct DsftRowDisk {          // 80 bytes, from payload + 0x10
    u32 stageId;              // disk +0x10  (101..143)
    u32 f04;
    f32 f08;                  // 75.0
    f32 f0C;                  // == f10
    f32 f10;                  // == f0C
    f32 f14;
    u32 pad18[3];
    u32 sentinel24;           // 0xFFFFFFFF
    u32 f28;                  // in {0,4}
    u32 pad2C[3];
    u32 f38;                  // ~65639..65647
    u32 zero3C;
    u32 pad40[4];
};
// file: 16-byte header {"DSFT",1,1,60} then one DsftRowDisk
```

### 18.1029 DSFT EQUAL PAIR: three candidate semantics and their discriminating tests

The pair row+0x0C == row+0x10 takes values 161.333 .. 221.0 across 97 payloads,
always with denominator 3 (e.g. 178.667 = 536/3). 18.452 already REFUTED the
"paired rotation angles" reading (a==-b 0/43; a+b==360 1/43; a+b==0 0/43).

1) CANDIDATE A: SONG BPM
```
range 161..221 is a plausible BPM range for dance music, values are BPM-like, and
being stored twice matches a per-difficulty or per-mode duplicate.
```
test: read the BPM of the corresponding song from the music data (musicData
tables 18.969 or the chart header) and compare.

2) CANDIDATE B: A DURATION OR PERIOD IN FRAMES
```
values with denominator 3 suggest a time quantity quantised to thirds; 180.0
frames at 60 fps = 3 s, 161.333 frames = 2.689 s.
```
test: compare with the chart length or with a measure duration; the value should
equal (frames per measure) or a similar unit.

3) CANDIDATE C: AN ANGLE IN DEGREES
```
range 161..221 degrees is a plausible orientation; the earlier paired-angle
reading was refuted, but a SINGLE orientation angle duplicated is not refuted.
```
test: find the danceFormat.c consumer that reads this field and check whether it
feeds a rotation (e.g. passed to a sin/cos or a matrix builder).

4) WHICH TEST IS CHEAPEST
```
A is cheapest: the music data already contains per-song parameters (18.969).
If the value equals the song BPM for several stages, A is confirmed; otherwise it
is refuted for all rows at once.
```

5) STATUS
```
The field stays UNNAMED in the document. No candidate is asserted.
This section exists so the next round does not re-derive the options.

### 18.1037 *** GAP: the 64-byte area is a RECORD HEADER, not a bare matrix ***

Final-round measurement on pcp201_1.GAP. This CORRECTS the "64-byte matrix"
wording of 18.1018.

1) FIRST FOUR u32 OF THE AREA AFTER THE NAME (big-endian)
```
bone       chan bytes   area[0]      area[1]  area[2]  area[3]
RootNode       0        0x48e1b0e5   1        0x2      1
root         574        0xb8d2b110   1        0x1C     33
Hips        1510        0x70f74e5a   1        0x1C     85
Spine        880        0x5dccb9a6   1        0x1C     50
Spine1         0        0xe8a2b8f0   1        0x2      1
Spine2         0        0x71abe94a   1        0x2      1
neck         664        0x8e379e18   1        0x1C     38
head        1852        0x9d5bed7    1        0x1C     104
```

2) THE PATTERN
```
area[0] : a per-bone hash/checksum (varies, no obvious structure yet)
area[1] : always 1
area[2] : 0x1C (=28) for ANIMATED bones ; 0x2 for STATIC bones (chan = 0)
area[3] : a small count, 1 for static bones, 33/85/50/38/104 for animated ones
```

3) THE RELATION BETWEEN area[3] AND CHANNEL BYTES
```
root : 574 / 33  = 17.39
Hips : 1510 / 85 = 17.76
Spine:  880 / 50 = 17.60
neck :  664 / 38 = 17.47
head : 1852 / 104= 17.81
=> channel bytes is consistently ABOUT 17.5x area[3] (range 17.39..17.81)
```
This is a STRONG correlation but not an exact formula. Candidates:
```
a) area[3] = number of keys, and each key block is 17.5 bytes on average
   (17.5 = not an integer, so unlikely to be a fixed stride)
b) area[3] = number of channels, and the average channel block is ~17.5 bytes
c) channel bytes = area[3] * 16 + something (variable per channel)
```
=> the exact rule is NOT derived; the correlation is recorded as a lead.

4) WHAT THIS CORRECTS
```
18.1018 described the 64 bytes after the name as "u8 matrix[64] (4x4 floats)".
The first four u32 are clearly NOT matrix floats (they are a hash, a constant,
a type-like 0x1C/0x2, and a count). The 4x4 identity floats DO appear later
(e.g. 0x3F800000 at 0x70 for RootNode), so the area contains metadata followed by
matrix/values.
=> the record layout is now:
     u16 BE id | u8 flag | u8 nameLen | name | u32 hash | u32 1 | u32 kind
     | u32 count | ... (matrix floats and channel data follow)
```
The exact offset where the matrix starts is not yet pinned.

5) NEXT-CYCLE LEAD (concrete)
```
(a) Locate the matrix start by looking for the first 4x4 identity-like pattern
    after the count word (RootNode has 0x3F800000 at 0x70).
(b) Test whether area[3] equals the number of channel sub-records: parse the
    channel region with that count and see whether it divides cleanly.
(c) area[2] (0x1C vs 0x2) is a bone CLASS selector - likely "animated" vs
    "static", and may also encode the matrix width.
```

6) STATUS
```
This is the single most promising lead for the GAP channel framing item
(18.1030 item 2). It is recorded as a MEASURED CORRELATION, not as a solved rule.

### 18.1039 GAP CHANNEL: prior art (5ZY) says [u16 0x40DE][253 f32]; new marker count

Found via the mandatory kb_lookup step (protocol 18.963).

1) PRIOR ART (5ZY, round 1412) - read, not re-derived
```
channel structure : [ u16 0x40DE (2 B) ][ 253 x f32 = 1012 B ] = 1014 B
NO name field
"3-character channel names" was RETRACTED in 5ZY.3 (it was a float byte
coincidence: bytes 03 33 33 41 = LE float 11.2000)
bone block sizes in that file set: S = 10,764 ; F = 11,778 (not fixed)
```

2) NEW MEASUREMENT ON pcp201_1.GAP (this round)
```
byte pattern 40 DE (big-endian u16 0x40DE) : 0 occurrences
byte pattern DE 40 (little-endian u16 0x40DE): 305 occurrences
random expectation for a 2-byte pattern in 119,626 bytes: about 1.8
=> 305 is FAR above chance: the marker is real, but it appears LITTLE-ENDIAN
```

3) THE CONTRADICTION TO RESOLVE
```
18.1013 established that INTEGER fields in this file are BIG-ENDIAN
(bone count 82 = 00 00 00 52 at +0x30; LE would be 0x52000000).
5ZY's channel header 0x40DE appears here only in LITTLE-ENDIAN byte order.
=> either
   (a) the channel header is a byte-swapped value relative to the integer
       fields (possible if it is a half-float bit pattern, not an integer), or
   (b) this file uses a different GAP variant than the one 5ZY analysed.
```

4) THE SIZE CONTRADICTION
```
5ZY channel size = 1014 bytes (2 + 253*4)
18.1013 measured channel lengths for pcp201_1: root 574, Hips 1510, Spine 880,
neck 664 ... none equals 1014
=> those measured lengths came from a SCAN heuristic (18.1034 showed the scan is
   unreliable), so they may simply be wrong boundaries.
   A 1014-byte fixed channel block should be TESTED as the replacement model.
```

5) DECISIVE NEXT TEST (one command, no new theory needed)
```
Take the 305 DE40 positions. Check whether they form a regular lattice:
   for each candidate start s, test s + k*1014 for k = 1..n
If a lattice exists, the channel block is 1014 bytes and the earlier scan-based
lengths are all wrong.
If no lattice exists, the 305 markers are coincidences of float bytes and the
5ZY structure does not apply to this file.
```

6) WHY THIS MATTERS
```
18.1030 item 1 (GAP channel sub-record framing) is the blocking item for a
correct multi-bone walk. 5ZY already solved the CHANNEL layout for its file set;
this round shows the same marker pattern exists here but with conflicting
endianness and size, so the immediate step is a lattice test rather than a new
model.

### 18.1040 LATTICE TEST REFUTES 1014-BYTE CHANNELS FOR pcp201_1; DE40 = half-float

Executing the decisive test proposed in 18.1039 step 5.

1) RESULT (decisive negative)
```
DE40 (= little-endian u16 0x40DE) occurrences : 305
chains with step 1014 and length >= 3          : 0
most frequent inter-marker deltas              : 248(9) 236(9) 200(8) 2663(8)
                                                 240(7) 292(7) 2699(7) 2619(7)
longest chain for any candidate step           : 3 (step 200)
```
=> NO lattice exists. The 1014-byte channel model of 5ZY does NOT apply to
   pcp201_1.GAP.

2) THE EXPLANATION FOR THE HIGH MARKER COUNT
```
half-float 0x40DE = 3.4297 ; stored little-endian its bytes are DE 40
7E.3 records that GAP KeyType 31 stores 3 x half (6 bytes) per key.
=> animation payloads are full of half-floats, so the 2-byte pattern DE40 occurs
   hundreds of times as DATA, not as a header marker.
This removes the contradiction: the 305 hits are data values, not channel starts.
```

3) WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE TWO GAP VARIANTS
```
5ZY's file set   : bone blocks S = 10,764 ; F = 11,778 ; channel = 1,014 bytes
pcp201_1.GAP     : average record ~1,458 bytes incl channels; measured channel
                   regions 574 / 1510 / 880 / 664 (scan-based, unreliable)
=> these are DIFFERENT GAP variants (different bone sets and key encodings).
   The 5ZY channel layout cannot be transplanted to pcp201_1 without proof.
```

4) CONSEQUENCE FOR 18.1030 ITEM 1
```
The channel framing rule must be derived from the KeyType stride table (7E.3):
   kt31 -> 6 bytes per key (3 x half)
   kt33 -> 20 bytes per key (5 x single)
   kt28 -> 14 bytes per key (NodePRHalf_2)
=> a correct parser needs, per channel: a KeyType byte, a key COUNT, and then
   count * stride(keyType) bytes. The exact channel header layout (where the
   keyType and count sit) is still to be determined for THIS variant.
```

5) NEXT TEST (cheap, no new theory)
```
In pcp201_1, take a channel region (e.g. root at 0xCC) and try to find a
consistent (keyType, count) header by checking for a byte whose value is a known
KeyType (22/28/31/33) followed by a count that makes the region consume exactly.
Keys should then decode as plausible values:
   kt31: half-float triples of angles (range +-pi)
   kt33: five floats
If a header candidate makes 100 % of a region decode to |value| < 4, it is the
right one (angles are small; random bytes are not).
```

### 18.1041 *** BREAKTHROUGH: GAP channel header is [u32 1][u32 kt][u32 N+1][u32 0] ***

Prior art found via STEP 0 (kb_lookup -> section 7P / 9O.1): the channel header format
for GFS camera files is exactly `[u32 1][u32 keyType][u32 N+1][u32 0]`.
This round applied the same scan to pcp201_1.GAP and it WORKS.

1) SCAN RESULT (pcp201_1.GAP)
```
channel-header hits : 82   (EXACTLY the bone count of this model)
kt distribution     : kt=2 -> 12 files bones (static)
                      kt=28 -> 68 bones (animated)
                      kt=27 -> 2 bones
first hits:
  @0x48  kt=2   N+1=1    (RootNode, static, N=0)
  @0x90  kt=28  N+1=33   (root,  N=32)
  @0x316 kt=28  N+1=85   (Hips,  N=84)
  @0x945 kt=28  N+1=50   (Spine, N=49)
  @0xCFF kt=2   N+1=1    (Spine1)
  @0xD49 kt=2   N+1=1    (Spine2)
  @0xD91 kt=28  N+1=38   (neck)
  @0x1071 kt=28 N+1=104  (head)
```

2) CROSS-VALIDATION WITH 18.1037
```
18.1037 measured, per bone, the four u32 right after name+hash:
  RootNode {hash, 1, 0x2, 1}    -> kt=2   N+1=1
  root     {hash, 1, 0x1C, 33}  -> kt=28  N+1=33
  Hips     {hash, 1, 0x1C, 85}  -> kt=28  N+1=85
  Spine    {hash, 1, 0x1C, 50}  -> kt=28  N+1=50
  Spine1   {hash, 1, 0x2, 1}    -> kt=2   N+1=1
  neck     {hash, 1, 0x1C, 38}  -> kt=28  N+1=38
  head     {hash, 1, 0x1C, 104} -> kt=28  N+1=104
=> PERFECT match: 18.1037's "kind" IS the keyType and its "count" IS N+1.
The per-bone correlation (channel bytes ~ count*17.5) is thereby explained: the
body size is driven by N and by the keyType stride.
```

3) THE RECORD LAYOUT (now fully determined at header level)
```c
struct GapRecord {
    u16 id;              // BE bone id
    u8  flag;            // 0 in samples
    u8  nameLen;
    char name[nameLen];
    u32 hash;            // per-bone value
    u32 one;             // == 1
    u32 keyType;         // 2 = static, 28 = NodePRHalf_2, 27 = variant
    u32 nPlus1;          // N+1 = number of keys + 1
    u32 zero;            // == 0
    u8  body[];          // size still to be derived from keyType and N
};
// header starts at: record_start + 4 + nameLen + 4
```

4) BODY SIZE STATUS

Two bodies measured from consecutive header positions (using
next_record_start = next_header - 8 - nameLen(next)):

  root     : kt=28, N=32 -> body = 618 bytes
A first formula attempt (16-byte tail + N*stride + (N+1)*4) does not fit exactly:
  16 + 32*14 + 33*4 = 596 vs measured 618
=> the exact body formula is NOT yet derived. It is now the ONLY remaining
   unknown in the GAP record layout.
```

5) NEXT (exact, one command)

Compute all 82 header positions, derive every body size (need each next record's
nameLen, which is readable at next_record_start+3), then fit

separately for kt=2, kt=27, kt=28. With 82 samples the fit will be unambiguous.

### 18.1042 GAP BODY: kt=27 formula established (60 + 24*N); kt=2/28 need boundary fix

Fitting over the 81 inter-header gaps of pcp201_1.GAP (82 channel headers from 18.1041).

1) RESULT
```
kt=27 : body = 60 + 24 * N     samples N=3 -> 132 (60+72), N=20 -> 540 (60+480)
                               ALL samples match exactly
kt=2  : N is always 0 (static bones) but the derived body takes values
        47, 49, 54, 56, 57  -> NOT constant, although it must be
kt=28 : for the SAME N=6 two different bodies were derived (162 and 164)
        -> the derivation is sometimes off by ~2 bytes
```

2) DIAGNOSIS OF THE AMBIGUITY
```
The body size was derived as:
   body = next_record_start - (header_pos + 16)
where next_record_start was found by scanning backwards from the next header:
   next_record_start = next_header - 8 - nameLen(next)
and nameLen was taken as the FIRST candidate (nl = 1..40) whose name bytes are
printable. Multiple nl values can satisfy that test, so the chosen start can be
off by a small amount.
=> kt=27 samples are unambiguous because both happened to land on the correct
   candidate; kt=2 and kt=28 include at least one mis-detected boundary.
```

3) WHY kt=27 IS STILL A FIRM RESULT
```
Both kt=27 samples give the SAME slope 24 and intercept 60, from different N
(3 and 20). A coincidence is very unlikely: two independent N values fitting a
two-parameter line exactly is strong evidence.
=> body(kt=27, N) = 60 + 24*N  is recorded as an ESTABLISHED formula.
```

4) THE CLEANEST NEXT CONSTRAINT (one command)
```
kt=2 records have N = 0, so their body MUST be one constant value.
Solve that constant first:
   for every kt=2 header, try all valid nameLen candidates for the NEXT record
   and keep the candidate that makes body equal across ALL kt=2 records.
That single constraint fixes the nameLen disambiguation rule, after which the
kt=28 slope can be fitted cleanly.
```

5) WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE GAP FORMAT
```
record layout (18.1041):
   u16 id | u8 flag | u8 nameLen | name | u32 hash
   | u32 1 | u32 kt | u32 N+1 | u32 0 | body
body formula:
   kt=27 : 60 + 24*N                      ESTABLISHED
   kt=2  : constant (value TBD)           one degenerate case
   kt=28 : linear in N (slope TBD)        fit blocked by boundary ambiguity
```

### 18.1043 *** GAP RECORD LAYER CLOSED: body formulas validated on 5 files ***

This closes the blocking item of 18.1030 #1 (GAP channel sub-record framing) at the
record level. Only a small file trailer remains unexplained.

1) THE ESTABLISHED FORMULAS (each `kt` = channel keyType)
```
kt = 2  : body = 44                     (static bones, N always 0)
kt = 27 : body = 48 + 24 * N
kt = 28 : body = 42 + 18 * N            (53/53 distinct (N,body) pairs matched)
```
CORRECTION: 18.1042's kt=27 formula (60 + 24*N) was a circular two-point fit built
from one mis-detected boundary. The corrected formula is 48 + 24*N, derived from
two independently located boundaries: (N=3 -> 120) and (N=20 -> 528).

2) THE COMPLETE RECORD LAYOUT
```c
struct GapRecord {
    u16 id;              // BE bone id
    u8  flag;            // 0 in samples
    u8  nameLen;
    char name[nameLen];  // e.g. "RootNode", "Hips", "R_Arm_Roll_02"
    u32 hash;            // per-bone value
    u32 one;             // == 1
    u32 keyType;         // 2 / 27 / 28 observed
    u32 nPlus1;          // N + 1 keys
    u32 zero;            // == 0
    u8  body[];          // size = f(keyType, N) as above
};
// record start = header_pos - 8 - nameLen
```

3) VALIDATION (deterministic walk, formulas only, no scanning)

file                  size     bones  recs parsed  end        residual
pcp201_1.GAP          119626     82       82       0x1D332    24 bytes
pc111340_p34.GAP      459025     39       39       0x700E9    40 bytes

The trailer bytes decode as plausible big-endian floats mixed with zeros, e.g.

5) IMPLEMENTABLE C PARSER (complete for the record layer)
```c
static size_t gap_body(u32 kt, u32 N) {
    switch (kt) {
        case 2:  return 44;
        case 27: return 48 + 24u*N;
        case 28: return 42 + 18u*N;
        default: return 0;              // unknown keyType -> stop
    }
}
size_t gap_walk(const u8* p, size_t n) {
    size_t off = 0x38;
    while (off + 28 < n) {
        u8  nl = p[off+3];
        const char* nm = (const char*)(p + off + 4);
        if (nl < 1 || nl > 40 || !gap_name_ok(nm, nl)) break;
        size_t h = off + 8 + nl;
        u32 one = rd32be(p+h), kt = rd32be(p+h+4),
            n1 = rd32be(p+h+8), z = rd32be(p+h+12);
        if (one != 1 || z != 0) break;
        size_t b = gap_body(kt, n1 - 1);
        if (!b) break;
        off = h + 16 + b;
    }
    return off;                         // n - off is the trailer
}
```

6) SIGNIFICANCE
```
.gap = 6972 files = 66 % of all resource files (18.1010)
the record layer and body sizes are now derived and cross-validated, so a native
port can walk every bone of every animated model and reach the per-keyframe body.
The remaining work inside .gap is interpreting the BODY CONTENT (keyframe values),
not the container framing.
```

### 18.1044 GAP BODY CONTENT: N time floats + value array + 16-byte tail

Follows 18.1043 (record layer closed). Measured on pcp201_1.GAP.

1) BODY PREFIX = TIME ARRAY (big-endian f32)
```
root (kt=28, N=32, body=618 at 0xA0):
  times[0..5] = 0.0333, 0.0667, 0.1333, 0.1667, 0.2, 0.2667 ...
  times last  = 6.6000
  count read by "increasing float" scan = 32 = N
=> the body starts with N big-endian time values (seconds, increasing)
```

2) BODY SUFFIX = THE 16-BYTE TAIL ALREADY KNOWN
```
root body end - 16: 3f800000 3f800000 3f800000 00010000
= three 1.0f + 0x00010000   (the same tail found in 18.1017)
=> the tail is the END of every body, not a separate record
```

3) UNIFIED SIZE DECOMPOSITION
```
body(kt,N) from 18.1043 :  kt=2 -> 44 ; kt=27 -> 48+24N ; kt=28 -> 42+18N
Rewrite as body = N * keySize(kt) + trailing(kt):
    kt=2 : keySize 20, trailing 44   (N=0)
    kt=27: keySize 24, trailing 48
    kt=28: keySize 18, trailing 42
Within keySize the first 4 bytes are the time float:
    kt=28: 4 time + 14 value
    kt=27: 4 time + 20 value
    kt=2 : 4 time + 16 value
trailing(kt) is a fixed per-kt block whose interior split is NOT yet derived
(42 / 48 / 44 bytes; the last 16 of them are the known tail, leaving 26 / 32 / 28).
```

4) LINK TO EXISTING KEYFRAME PRIOR ART (read via kb_lookup, not re-derived)
```
4KP : keyframe interpolation system; keyframe VALUES = position[0..2] + quaternion[3..6]
4LD : position + quaternion + neighbouring position = 10 floats
4KJ : value lookup = base + t*rate, sampler FUN_8119B700
=> the value strides found here (14 / 20 / 16 bytes) are consistent with the
   half-float and reduced-precision variants of that 10-float keyframe model,
   but the exact per-kt value layout is NOT yet mapped field by field.
```

5) WHAT IS NOW ESTABLISHED vs OPEN FOR .gap
```
ESTABLISHED (record layer, 5 files, 238 records):
  magic GFS0, big-endian
  header 0x38, bone count at +0x30
  record = id/flag/nameLen/name/hash/[1][kt][N+1][0]/body
  body size formulas for kt = 2, 27, 28
  body begins with N big-endian time floats and ends with the 16-byte tail
OPEN (body interior):
  exact value stride and field layout per keyType
  the trailing block interior (26 / 32 / 28 bytes before the 16-byte tail)
  the per-file trailer after the last record (24 / 40 bytes)
```

### 18.1045 *** GAP BODY LAYOUT SOLVED: unified formula matches all three keyTypes ***

Continues 18.1043 (record layer) and 18.1044 (body prefix/suffix).

1) THE UNIFIED BODY LAYOUT
```c
struct GapBody {
    f32  times[N];              // N big-endian time values (seconds, increasing)
    u8   values[(N+1) * vsz];   // vsz depends on keyType
    f32  last[3];               // 3 big-endian floats (12 bytes)
    f32  tail0, tail1, tail2;   // 1.0, 1.0, 1.0
    u32  tailword;              // 0x00010000
};
// valueSize: kt=28 -> 14 (7 x half) ; kt=27 -> 20 (5 x float) ; kt=2 -> 16 (4 x ?)
```

2) ARITHMETIC PROOF (each matches the independently measured body formulas)
```
kt=28 : 4N + 14(N+1) + 12 + 16 = 18N + 42   == measured 42 + 18N   MATCH
kt=27 : 4N + 20(N+1) + 12 + 16 = 24N + 48   == measured 48 + 24N   MATCH
kt=2  :  0 + 16*1    + 12 + 16 = 44         == measured 44          MATCH
```
Three independent keyTypes fitting the same structure is strong evidence that the
layout is correct, not a coincidence.

3) MEASURED CONTENT OF root (kt=28, N=32, body 618 bytes at 0xA0)

values[0] decoded as 7 big-endian half-floats:

 = 0.9839 1.0000 0.9263 0.4998 0.4998 0.4998 0.4998
values[1] = 0.9844 0.9995 0.9346 0.4998 x4
values[2] = 0.9844 0.9995 0.9497 0.4998 x4
last 3 floats before the tail (bytes 401d7e5f 42ca5bfd c0cdcf4c)
 = 2.4609, 101.18, -6.4306

### 18.1049 GFS0 BUILDER FOUND (code-side); header layout confirmed by code

Code-side search (18.1048 decision) with the corrected magic constant.

1) MAGIC CONSTANT CORRECTION
```
"GFS0" bytes are 47 46 53 30 ; as a big-endian u32 that is 0x47465330
(earlier round used 0x47534630 which was a digit-order mistake)
```

2) THE ONLY movw/movt REFERENCE TO 0x47465330
```
address 0x811DEAF6 builds the constant; the code that follows is a GFS0 BUILDER:
0x811DEAF6  movw  r0, #0x5330
0x811DEAFA  movt  r0, #0x4746          ; r0 = 0x47465330 = "GFS0"
0x811DEAFE  str   r0, [r4]             ; obj[+0x00] = magic
0x811DEB00  movs.w r0, #0x5100
0x811DEB04  movt  r0, #0x110           ; r0 = 0x01105100  (type word)
0x811DEB08  str   r0, [r4, #4]         ; obj[+0x04] = type
0x811DEB0A  bl    0x811EE776           ; produce a value/pointer
0x811DEB0E  str   r0, [r4, #8]         ; obj[+0x08] = that value
0x811DEB10  movs  r0, #0x10
0x811DEB12  bl    0x811DA534           ; allocate 16 bytes
0x811DEB16  adds  r5, r0, #0
0x811DEB18  adds  r1, r4, #0
0x811DEB1A  movs  r2, #0x10
```

3) WHAT THIS PROVES (authoritative, from code)
```
- the header layout is exactly: +0x00 "GFS0" magic, +0x04 type/version word
  (this independently confirms 18.1021/18.1024, now from executable code)
- a builder exists that creates the type 0x01105100 variant
  (= the count+float variant of 18.1022, used by .env / .epl / 204 .gap files)
- the pointer at +0x08 is produced by FUN_811EE776
```

4) WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE
```
This is the builder for the "count+float" variant, NOT the named-bone animation
variant (type 0x01105090) whose record layout was derived in 18.1043/18.1045.
The named-bone file LOADER is still to be located.
```

4K5 records three in-memory GFS0 structures and their loaders:

0x811AA88C  movw  r1, #0x5090
0x811AA892  movt  r1, #0x110          ; r1 = 0x01105090
0x811AA890  ldr   r2, [r4, #4]        ; r2 = obj->type  (the +0x04 field)
0x811AA896  cmp   r2, r1
0x811AA898  bls.w 0x811AB14E          ; type <= 0x01105090 -> branch A
...
0x811AA8A8  movw  r0, #0x5070
0x811AA8AC  movt  r0, #0x110          ; r0 = 0x01105070
0x811AA8B0  cmp   r2, r0
0x811AA8B2  bls.w 0x811AB0C8          ; type <= 0x01105070 -> branch B

=> this is a TYPE-WORD DISPATCHER: it reads obj->type from +0x04 and branches to

18.1021/18.1024/18.1049 established the header layout (magic +0x00, type +0x04)
from bytes and from a builder. This section confirms that the GAME ITSELF
dispatches on exactly that +0x04 type field, and gives the parser entry points.
=> the type word is not an inference: it is a runtime dispatch key.
```

the same function fills fields at [r5+0x218], [r5+0x22c], [r5+0x230], [r5+0x231],

=> the loader builds a runtime object from the file fields; the reader helpers are

### 18.1051 CORRECTION: the "branch targets" are JOIN POINTS inside one loader function

18.1050 reported two branch targets 0x811AB14E / 0x811AB0C8 as per-type parsers.
Disassembly of those addresses shows they are JOIN POINTS of the SAME function.

1) EVIDENCE
```asm
0x811AB14E  strb.w r0, [r5, #0x233]
0x811AB152  b.w    0x811AA8A8        <-- jumps BACK into the main flow
0x811AB0C8  strb.w r6, [r5, #0x235]
0x811AB0CE  strb.w r6, [r5, #0x236]
0x811AB0D2  b.w    0x811AA8D0        <-- jumps BACK into the main flow
```
=> these are not independent parsers; they are continuation blocks of one big
   loader function that builds a runtime object at r5.

2) WHAT THE DISPATCH ACTUALLY DOES
```
it compares obj->type ([r4+4]) against a SERIES of type words and, for each
range, executes a different sequence of field reads:
   0x01105090  (named-bone type)   seen
   0x01105070                      seen
   0x01105040                      seen (cmp r3, 0x01105040 ; bls ...)
=> the loader reads variant-specific fields via helpers:
   0x811DF23A   (byte-like reader, used repeatedly)
   0x811DF182   (u32-like reader)
   0x811DED54   / 0x811DED24  (buffer access)
=> it fills runtime fields at r5+0x218, r5+0x22c, r5+0x230, r5+0x231, r5+0x232,
   r5+0x233, r5+0x235, r5+0x236, r5+0x238, r5+0x2dc, r5+0x32c
   and stores a float constant 0x3E4CCCCD (0.2) into s0 at one point.
```

### 18.1052 *** CODE-LEVEL CONFIRMATION: GFS0 integers are BIG-ENDIAN (reader primitives)

Disassembly of the two helpers called by the GFS0 loader (18.1050/18.1051).

1) helper A = 0x811DF182 = READ U32 BIG-ENDIAN
```asm
0x811DF182  push  {r4, lr} ; sub sp, #8
0x811DF186  movw  r4, #0x414c ; movt r4, #0x812b    ; stack canary slot
0x811DF192  add   r1, sp, #0
0x811DF194  movs  r2, #4
0x811DF196  bl    0x811DE912                         ; read 4 bytes into [sp]
0x811DF19A  ldr   r0, [sp]                            ; raw little-endian u32
0x811DF19C  lsrs  r1, r0, #0x18                       ; 0x811DF19E  bfi   r1, r0, #0x18, #8                   ;  |
0x811DF1A2  ror.w r2, r0, #8                          ;  | byte-swap
0x811DF1A6  bfi   r1, r2, #0x10, #8                   ;  | sequence
0x811DF1AA  ror.w r0, r0, #0x10                       ;  |
0x811DF1AE  bfi   r1, r0, #8, #8                      ; /
0x811DF1B2  adds  r0, r1, #0                          ; result = swapped u32
```
=> this function reads 4 bytes and swaps their order: it is a BIG-ENDIAN u32 reader.

2) helper B = 0x811DF23A = READ U8
```asm
0x811DF23A  push  {r4, lr} ; sub sp, #8

byte-swaps every 4-byte integer it reads.

=> helper A is the authoritative "read BE u32" primitive; helper B the "read u8".

static u8  rd_u8    (const u8** p) { u8  v = **p;        *p += 1; return v; }
// the loader's reads map 1:1 onto these two primitives
```
