```
- program size is an independent per-program value (roughly 0x150..0x294+ observed);
- the E401 pair observation of 18.1404 (exactly two per program, 16-byte spacing) was
  measured on three programs only and should be re-checked on a wider sample before use;
- the tail structure (declaration strings + table) is still real, but its layout must be
  derived from the data, not from an assumed constant base.
```
3) METHOD LESSON (recorded for future rounds)
```
a relation verified on 3 samples is NOT a formula. Any candidate invariant must be tested
over the FULL population before it is written as a rule; otherwise record it explicitly as
a hypothesis with its sample size.

### 18.1409 *** RETRACTION 2: THE "E401 PAIR" IS NOT A STRUCTURAL MARKER ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: E401 refuted, coincidence bytes, code bytes.

1) FULL-SAMPLE TEST (340 programs)
```
E401 (bytes 01 E4 00 00) occurrence-count histogram:
   0 hits: 6 programs      1 hit: 8 programs
   2 hits: 29 programs     3 hits: 201 programs
   4 hits: 81 programs     5 hits: 15 programs
delta between hits in the 29 two-hit programs: always 16
```
2) CONCLUSION
```
"exactly two E401 markers per program" is FALSE (only 29/340). The marker count varies 0..5
and the mode is 3, which is inconsistent with a per-declaration or fixed-count structure.
The most plausible reading is that 01 E4 00 00 occurs INSIDE the bytecode by chance
(instruction bytes), and the observed 16-byte spacing in the 29 cases is coincidental.
=> THE E401 FINDINGS OF 18.1404 ARE RETRACTED.
```
3) WHAT REMAINS VALID
```
- declaration strings exist in the tail of each program (real text: "vertex.position",
  "mtxLocalToWorld", ...) and their presence/count correlates with the +0x2C field;
- the program header fields and the 340-program inventory;
- the retracted items are only the assumed constant-base formula (18.1405/18.1407) and the
  E401 structural marker (18.1404/18.1409).
```
4) METHOD NOTE
```
two consecutive three-sample coincidences show that small samples on binary data are
extremely misleading. Any structural claim now requires population-level testing BEFORE it
is recorded as a rule (already recorded in 18.1407; reinforced here).

### 18.1411 *** +0x2C == DECLARED-NAME COUNT: 304/340 DIRECT MATCH, RESIDUE EXPLAINED ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: 304 of 340, declaration count confirmed, truncation artifacts.

1) POPULATION TEST RESULT
```
predicate: (# occurrences of "vertex." attribute strings) + (# known uniform names) == +0x2C
matched: 304 / 340 programs = 89.4 %
```
2) THE MISMATCHES
```
mismatch samples are overwhelmingly pred = count - 1 (or -2):
  @0x40   nv=1 nu=1 pred=2 count=3
  @0x1730 nv=3 nu=1 pred=4 count=5
  @0x33D4 nv=2 nu=0 pred=2 count=4
  @0x5060 nv=2 nu=0 pred=2 count=3
```
3) WHY (measured evidence)
```
the names are stored at the END of each program: in @0x40 the last visible uniform string is
"mtxV" because the program size (0x244) cuts the string "mtxViewProj" across the record
boundary. So some declarations are truncated by our per-record scan and were not counted.
This explains the systematic pred = count-1 residue and supports (rather than contradicts)
the interpretation.
```
4) CONCLUSION
```
+0x2C is the number of declared names (vertex attributes + uniforms) for a program.
Confidence: 304/340 direct + residue explained by record-boundary truncation.
This is a format invariant usable by a parser (with name scanning extended across the
record boundary).
```
5) NEXT
```
re-run the count allowing the last string to continue past the record end; expect the match
rate to approach 340/340, which would close this rule.

### 18.1413 CROSS-BOUNDARY TEST INVALID; +0x2C RULE REMAINS UNPROVEN (OPEN)

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: cross-boundary invalid, overrun contamination, count open.

1) WHAT HAPPENED
```

to the FOLLOWING program (e.g. @0x40 nv=1 but nu=3, with two extra names from the next

2) WHERE THE +0x2C RULE STANDS
```

overrun scan: invalid experiment.
The rule is therefore SUPPORTED but NOT PROVEN; it stays OUT of the confirmed list and in
the open questions until a correct name-boundary parser is built (one that reads the
length-prefixed names table the format actually uses).
```

entries in the tail), then count entries exactly and compare with +0x2C on all 340.
Only that closes the rule.

### 18.1425 *** DEFINITIVE RECORD LAYOUT: [stage magic][u32 size][GXP program] + optional 32-byte metadata ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: record layout, size prefix, metadata block, 2.0 float marker.

1) THE SMALL-GAP RULE (verified on 6 consecutive cases)
```
gap bytes between program end and next GXP = u32 value equal to the NEXT program's size:
  prev prog size 0xD4 -> gap d4000000 -> next GXP size 0xD4
  prev prog size 0xD4 -> gap c4000000 -> next GXP size 0xC4
  prev prog size 0xD4 -> gap dc000000 -> next GXP size 0xDC
  prev prog size 0xE8 -> gap cc000000 -> next GXP size 0xCC
=> each GXP program is preceded by a u32 SIZE field.
   For tagged programs the layout is:  [PVSG|PFSG] [u32 size] [GXP program]
   Where the stage magic exists it occupies those same 4 bytes before size? No - the stage
   magic is 4 bytes then size then GXP (8 bytes total before GXP): verified at 0x2AC PFSG +
   0x2B0 size 0xD4 + 0x2B4 GXP. For untagged programs the 4-byte size directly precedes GXP.
```
2) THE 40-BYTE GAP = 32-BYTE METADATA + 8-BYTE NEXT TAG
```
prog@0x48 gap(40):
  00010000 042c0000 00002002 00000000
  00000000 00000000 3ffffff8 3ffffff8   <- 32-byte metadata (ends with two 2.0f markers)
  50465347 d4000000                      <- "PFSG" + size (next stage tag)
prog@0xA60 gap(40):
  00000000 026c0000 00002002 00010000
  00000000 00000000 3ffffff8 3ffffff8
  50565347 64020000                      <- "PVSG" + size
=> metadata block = 32 bytes ending with two floats ~2.0; then the next stage tag.
```
3) PARSER RULE
```
walk: at current position read optional 4-byte stage magic (PVSG/PFSG); read u32 size read GXP;
      after program: if next bytes begin with a stage magic -> that's the next tag;
      otherwise a u32 size of the next program appears directly, or a 32-byte metadata block
      precedes the next tag.
The size field is authoritative for program length; tags assign stage.
```

```

number of programs found (expect 4,312 GXP magic hits, 340 PVSG, 536 PFSG).

### 18.1427 *** GAP MODEL REFINED: gap = (4 or 40) + 0..3 BYTES OF 4-BYTE ALIGNMENT PADDING ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: alignment padding, gap 4..7, gap 40..43, refined rule.

1) MEASURED GAP HISTOGRAM (all 4,311 gaps)
```
0x4: 899   0x5: 681   0x6: 917   0x7: 939     -> 4 + padding(0..3)
0x28: 243  0x29: 162  0x2A: 232  0x2B: 238     -> 40 + padding(0..3)
```
2) THE RULE
```
gap = BASE + PAD
  BASE = 4  : u32 size field preceding the next program
  BASE = 40 : 32-byte metadata block + u32 size field (metadata cases)
  PAD  = 0..3 bytes to align the next record to a 4-byte boundary
Example verified: program size 0x261 ends at 0xDC5; +43 (0x2B) -> next record at 0xDF0
which is 4-byte aligned. 0xDC5 + 0x2B = 0xDF0.
=> every program is preceded by its u32 size; some are additionally preceded by a 4-byte
   stage magic (PVSG/PFSG) and some have a 32-byte metadata block before the next tag.
   Records are 4-byte aligned, padding fills the remainder.
```
3) PARSER RECIPE
```
pos = first record (0x40)
loop:
  if d[pos:pos+4] in {PVSG,PFSG}: tag = that; size = u32(pos+4); gxp = pos+8
  else:                           tag = none;  size = u32(pos);   gxp = pos+4
  assert d[gxp:gxp+4] == "GXP␀"
  after = gxp + size
  align after to 4
  if next bytes start with PVSG/PFSG -> continue there
  else if a 32-byte metadata block precedes -> skip metadata then read stage magic
```
4) NOTE
```
the earlier interpretation of 18.1425 (fixed 4 or 40) is superseded by this alignment-aware
version. The 32-byte metadata identification stands.

### 18.1429 *** DECISIVE RULE: u32 AT GXP-4 == align4(size@GXP+8) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: align4 size prefix, decisive rule, all programs.

mismatches: []
```
2) THE RULE
```
every GXP program is preceded by a u32 equal to align4(program size). The preceding field is
the ALIGNED size, not the raw size (raw size at GXP+8 may be unaligned).

   programs are 4-byte aligned; the size prefix stores the aligned length.

### 18.1430 *** CONFIRMED INVARIANT: EVERY GXP IS PRECEDED BY align4(size) - 4312/4312 ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: align4 size prefix confirmed, 4312 of 4312, format invariant.

1) THE POPULATION RESULT
```
u32 at GXP-4 == (size + 3) & ~3    :  4312 / 4312  (100 %, zero exceptions)
```
2) THE CONFIRMED RECORD LAYOUT
```
[ optional 4-byte stage magic: "PVSG" (vertex) or "PFSG" (fragment) ]
[ u32 aligned_size = align4(program_size) ]
[ "GXP\0" program of program_size bytes ]        <- raw size at GXP+8
[ zero to 3 bytes alignment padding ]
[ optional 32-byte metadata block (ends with two 2.0f = 3FFFFFF8) ]
=> every record is 4-byte aligned; the size prefix is authoritative for stepping.
```
3) WHY THIS IS STRONG
```
100 % over all 4,312 programs, with an exact arithmetic rule (align-up by 0..3) that explains
every previously irregular gap (0x4..0x7 and 0x28..0x2B). This replaces the retracted
formulas of 18.1405 and the provisional model of 18.1425/18.1427.
```
4) PARSER (final)
```
pos = 0x40 (first PVSG)
loop:
  tag = d[pos:pos+4] if in {PVSG,PFSG} else None
  p = pos + (4 if tag else 0)
  aligned_size = u32(p)
  assert d[p+4:p+8] == "GXP\0"
  prog_size = u32(p+8)
  assert aligned_size == align4(prog_size)
  pos = p + 4 + aligned_size
  # optionally: if next 0x24 bytes contain metadata, it is consumed before the next tag
```

### 18.1459 *** METADATA BLOCKS ARE PER-GROUP TRAILERS; WORD0 IS A STAGE FLAG ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: metadata per-group, stage flag 0x100, 875 blocks.

1) MEASURED (875 metadata blocks found by the walker)
```
+0x00 : 0x100 x 536  |  0x0 x 339      <- two values only
+0x04 : 393 distinct values
+0x08 : 37 distinct values (0x11C08900 x263, 0x11C09B00 x157, 0x10C00900 x152)
+0x0C : 219 distinct values
+0x10 : 52 distinct values (0x0 x453, 0x10000 x66, 0x80000000 x34)
+0x14 : 3 distinct values (0x0 x700, 0x1000000 x106, 0x2000000 x69)
+0x18 and +0x1C : identical value distributions (59 distinct each, same frequencies)
```

2) THE GROUP CORRELATION (exact)
```
876 groups = 340 vertex + 536 fragment;  875 metadata blocks = 876 - 1.
word0 = 0x100 in exactly 536 blocks  ==  the 536 fragment groups.
word0 = 0x0   in exactly 339 blocks  ==  the vertex groups minus one.
=> each metadata block trails one GROUP (not one program); word0 is a stage flag:
     0x100 = fragment group, 0x0 = vertex group.
```

3) ALIGNMENT NOTE (important for the other fields)
```
the walker slice starts at program-end, which can be followed by 0..3 alignment padding
bytes before the metadata. Therefore the offsets +0x04..+0x1C above are shifted by the
padding in some blocks; only word0 (which matched group counts exactly) is unaffected in
interpretation. A padding-aware slice is required before assigning meanings to the other
metadata words.
```

### 18.1476 SHADER LAYER REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION (pseudocode, from confirmed findings)

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: shader parser pseudocode, implementation reference.

1) DATA STRUCTURES
```
typedef struct {
  uint32_t offset;        /* file offset of the program (at GXP magic) */
  uint32_t size;          /* raw program size from GXP+0x08        */
  uint8_t  stage;         /* 0 = vertex, 1 = fragment (tag/inherited) */
  uint32_t name_count;    /* GXP+0x24 field (meaning still open)    */
} ShaderProgram;
typedef struct {
  uint8_t  stage;         /* 0x100 -> fragment else vertex (metadata word0) */
  uint32_t word[8];        /* 32-byte metadata block                       */
} ShaderGroupMeta;
```
2) PARSER (confirms with the walker validated in 18.1432/18.1433)
```
pos = 0x40;
while (pos + 8 <= file_size) {
    tag = (peek32(pos) == 'PVSG') ? VERTEX :
          (peek32(pos) == 'PFSG') ? FRAGMENT : NONE;
    p = pos + (tag != NONE ? 4 : 0);
    aligned = u32(p);              /* == align4(program_size) */
    gxp = p + 4;                   /* must read 'GXP\0' */
    prog = u32(gxp + 8);           /* raw size */
    assert(aligned == (prog + 3) & ~3);
    program_end = gxp + prog;
    aligned_end = gxp + aligned;
    /* optional 32-byte metadata block before the next tag */
    next_tag = find_tag(aligned_end, aligned_end + 0x30);
    if (next_tag && next_tag - aligned_end >= 32)
        meta = bytes[next_tag - 32 .. next_tag];   /* word0 stage flag */
    append_program(gxp, prog, tag, meta);
    pos = next_tag ? next_tag : aligned_end;
}
```
3) GROUP FORMATION (18.1455/18.1457)
```
groups = consecutive programs where a tagged program starts a group and the following
untagged programs (exactly 4, except 17 vertex groups with 0) belong to it.
group stage = leading tag stage. 876 groups total in GFDPSP2.GSC.
```
4) NATIVE PORT HOOKS
```
for each group: build one GL program pair:
  vertex   = GLSL re-authored from declared attributes + uniforms
  fragment = GLSL re-authored from declared uniforms + material semantics
bind the 49-uniform contract (18.1350) at draw time using the group's declared names
(docs/shader_index.tsv).
```

### 18.1493 *** EXACT DECLARATION-TABLE LAYOUT (residue = 8 for all 1632 programs) ***

```

back to count - so the 1632/1632 match was correct but did not pin the 8-byte trailer.

refined from floor-based to exact.

### 18.1495 ENTRY ORDER DOES NOT ALIGN WITH NAME ORDER (mapping remains OPEN)

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: entry order mismatch, type codes, mapping open.

```

entry1 type word top : 0x0000E311 x2260, 0x00090400 x1440, 0x000E0400 x141, 0x00060400 x40
trailer 8 bytes top  : 00400000 01000000 x1292 ; 01000000 03000000 x545 ;
                       01000000 00000000 x540 ; 01000000 0A000000 x345
```
2) THE PROBLEM
```
in the example program 0xFA84 the first name string is 'vertex.position' and the first
descriptor entry's type word was 0x000B0400 (an attribute-like code). But over the whole
population the first entry is dominated by 0x0000E311 (uniform-like). Therefore the
descriptor array order does NOT correspond 1:1 to the name-string order in general.
Mapping entries to names needs an additional rule (e.g. names may be ordered by kind,
or entries store name offsets/keywords).
```
3) WHAT IS SAFE
```
SAFE: count == number of descriptor entries (1632/1632 exact); layout is
      prologue(32) + count*16 entries + 8-byte trailer + name strings (residue==8 x1632).
NOT SAFE: that entry[i] corresponds to name[i]. Do not use that assumption in a port.
```

### 18.1503 *** .GSC SHADER CONTAINER - CONSOLIDATED PORT-READY SPECIFICATION ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: GSC spec consolidated, port-ready shader format.

Single authoritative statement of the shader container, built from 18.1378-18.1502.

1) FILE LAYOUT
```
GFS0 header (0x00), then GSC0 header (0x10), then a sequence of records from 0x40.
record = [ optional 4-byte stage magic: PVSG(vertex) | PFSG(fragment) ]
         [ u32 aligned_size = align4(program_size) ]
         [ GXP program, program_size bytes ]
         [ 0..3 alignment padding ]
         [ optional 32-byte metadata block (per group) ]
validation: tools/gsc_parse.py consumes both .GSC files byte-exactly (GSC_PARSE_OK);
            every program is preceded by align4(size): 4312/4312 (18.1430).
```
2) PROGRAM HEADER (at GXP magic)
```
+0x00 'GXP\0'    +0x04 type 0x03500501    +0x08 program_size
+0x0C hashA      +0x10 hashB              +0x14 flags
+0x24 descriptor count                   (1632/1632 verified)
+0x28 offset of the declaration table    (< size, 4312/4312)
+0x2C constant 0x70 (all programs)
+0x6C constant 0x33E40 (all programs)
```
3) DECLARATION TABLE (at GXP+w28)
```
+0x00 : 32-byte prologue
+0x20 : count x 16-byte descriptor entries
after : 8-byte constant trailer           (residue == 8, 1632/1632)
then  : NUL-separated name strings
entry  : { u32 a, u32 b, u32 slot, u32 type }
name_start = w28 + 0x20 + count*16 + 8  (exact)
```
4) TYPE CODES (f3 word of each entry)
```
f3 & 0xFF == 0  -> vertex attribute descriptor
f3 & 0xFF != 0  -> uniform descriptor
attribute codes: position 0x000B0400, texcoord0 0x000E0400, normal 0x00090400,
  texcoord1 0x010E0400, binormal 0x00030400, color 0x00060400, texcoord2 0x020E0400
uniform codes: mtx* 0x0000E401, fog scalars 0x0000E211, eyePosition 0x0000E301,
  light0Vec 0x0000E311, constColor 0x0000E411
```
5) NAME VOCABULARY (complete; docs/shader_vocabulary.txt)
```
attributes (9): vertex.position, vertex.texcoord0, vertex.normal, vertex.indices,
  vertex.weights, vertex.texcoord1, vertex.binormal, vertex.color, vertex.texcoord2
uniforms (14): constColor, mtxViewProj, mtxView, fogFactor, skinBlendMatrices,
  eyePosition, heightFogFactor, mtxLocalToWorld, mtxWorldLightViewProj, light0Vec,
  mtxUV0Transform, mtxUV1Transform, mtxWorldViewProj, screen
```
6) GROUP MODEL
```
tagged program + following untagged programs form a group;
GFDPSP2.GSC: 4312 programs -> 876 groups (340 vertex-led + 536 fragment-led);
536 fragment groups have exactly 4 untagged; 323 vertex groups have 4, 17 have 0;
untagged accounting exact: 536*4 + 323*4 = 3436.
metadata: one 32-byte block per group (875 blocks), word0 = 0x100 fragment / 0x0 vertex.
```
7) KNOWN OPEN
```
(a) GXP VM bytecode instruction encoding (region identified, opcodes not decoded);
(b) semantics of entry fields a/b/slot beyond the type word;
(c) identity of the extra UNNAMED uniform descriptor in 1298 programs;
(d) metadata block fields +0x04/+0x08/+0x0C/+0x10;
(e) the 8-byte trailer contents between descriptors and names.
```
8) TOOLS
```
tools/gsc_parse.py (byte-exact walker), tools/gsc_index.py (inventory),
tools/gsc_groups.py (group model), docs/shader_index.tsv, docs/shader_vocabulary.txt.
```

fragment programs with a decoded declaration table: 0
=> every named program in the collection is VERTEX-stage.

2) WHY / WHAT IT MEANS
```
the declaration table is located via the first 'vertex.' string inside the program. Fragment
programs contain no such strings (verified earlier: program @0x2B4 and other D4 fragments
have no printable declaration names at all). Therefore the decode chain of
18.1499/18.1500/18.1501/18.1502/18.1506 applies to VERTEX programs only.
The earlier notes that said '1600+/1632 programs' were correctly scoped to named programs,
but the consolidated spec 18.1503 should be read as the VERTEX declaration-table spec.
```
3) FRAGMENT BINDING - OPEN
```
fragment programs still carry a nonzero count field (18.1436: fragment count values 0x9..0xD),
so they have some interface table, but it holds no name strings. The likely mechanism is
slot/index binding shared with the paired vertex group, or a fixed uniform layout. This is
OPEN and must be decoded before automatic fragment-shader regeneration.
```
4) IMPACT ON THE PORT
```
route B (re-authored GLSL) can already regenerate VERTEX shaders from the decoded interface;
fragment shaders need the additional step of determining how their uniforms are bound.

96.6 percent of programs). However NO program has every entry satisfying the strict
four-field model, and typical programs match 6-10 entries. Therefore the offset is likely
correct while some field assumptions are wrong for fragments (e.g. word0 not always 1,
word1 not always 2k, or additional type codes).
=> fragment table start = w28+0x30 is a SUPPORTED candidate (not yet proven); entry field
   semantics for fragments remain OPEN.
```

distribution of word0/word1/word3 over the count entries) to identify which assumption

### 18.1536 ENTRY WORD1 IS A RUNNING INDEX: STRIDE 2 FOR FRAGMENTS, STRIDE 4 FOR VERTEX

```
word1 is not a semantic field but a position/index accumulator: k*stride where the stride
differs by stage (2 for fragments, 4 for vertex). Earlier attempts to match word1 to
declaration counts failed (18.1511) because it is an index, not a count.
```

  = 'vertex.color\0screen\0'  (ASCII, not instructions)
```
2) STRUCTURAL CONSEQUENCE
```
vertex programs carry a TAIL NAME BLOCK as well (same as fragments). Therefore the layout
is NOT [forward names][code]; it is:
  header ... forward declaration table + forward names ... [code region] ... tail names
or the code sits between the two name blocks. The previous A1 result (code start after
forward names, 20..224 bytes) actually located the boundary of the TAIL block for small
programs, so the A1 conclusion must be refined: the 20..224 range is the tail-name/tail
region size, not the code size.
```

in this vertex tail. This supports the idea that 'screen' is a real implicit uniform name
present only in a few programs.

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: 16-bit instruction hypothesis, packed two per word.

1) MEASURED (340 tagged vertex programs, 40,498 words)
```

low16 top : 0x8F80 2458, 0x0DBC 2210, 0x8982 2139, 0x0000 1666, 0x0D7E 1484, 0x0F84 1214
high16 top: 0x18B1 4880, 0x40C0 3282, 0x10C0 1461, 0x08A4 1248, 0x4081 1038
```
2) INTERPRETATION
```
neither half behaves like a clean opcode field (both have ~500-600 distinct values with
comparable concentration). This WEAKENS the 'one 32-bit word = one instruction' assumption.
The most plausible alternative is that the GXP stream is made of 16-BIT instruction units
packed two per 32-bit word; then both halves are independently meaningful instruction
fields (opcode+operand mixed), which matches the similar distinct counts.
```
3) NEXT

units is even (always true if 4-byte aligned) and whether known 16-bit opcode families

the same 16-bit value appears as both half of consecutive words in consistent ways.

### 18.1612 GMD HEADER WORDS ARE NOT LITERAL CONSTANTS IN EBOOT

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: negative search, header words not constants, correction.

1) MEASURED
```
search eboot.bin (6,283,968 bytes) for the little-endian pattern of 0x90501001
(bytes 01 10 50 90): 0 hits.
=> the GMD header word at +0x04 is NOT compared as a literal constant in code.
```
2) INTERPRETATION
```
0x90501001 = bytes 01 10 50 90, which looks like a packed version/flags field
(e.g. minor/major/type bytes), not a magic signature. The same applies to 0xFC000100 and
0x01000000. Model loading must therefore VALIDATE the header structurally (or compare the
GFS0 magic 0x30534647 which IS present widely) rather than these fields.
=> the header-word attack on the model loader is closed; use the GFS0 magic or the model
   loading table instead.
```
3) NEXT
```
search eboot for the GFS0 magic (47 46 53 30 / 0x30534647) and for RotoNode/Bone strings
to locate the model block parser; from there follow the vertex-stream setup calls.
```

### 18.1615 NEGATIVE: NO LITERAL ADDRESS REFERENCES -> USE MOVW/MOVT SEARCH

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: movw movt search plan, no literal refs, negative result.

0x813366D8, 0x813B1F08, 0x813B297C (GFS0) and 0x8153CB8D, 0x8153CDD4, 0x8153D054,
0x8153D304 (skin strings): ZERO references for all seven targets.

2) INTERPRETATION
```
Thumb-2 code constructs 32-bit addresses with MOVW/MOVT pairs (16-bit immediates), so a
full 32-bit literal does not appear in the image. This closes the literal-pool attack and
prescribes the next method.
```
3) NEXT METHOD
```
decode MOVW/MOVT immediate pairs across the code segment, resolve register values, and
find the loads whose combined value equals one of the seven target addresses. This yields
the code that references the GFS0 strings / skin strings and anchors the model loader.
Tooling: use tools/trace_func.py infrastructure or a small Thumb-2 MOVW/MOVT scanner with
capstone md.detail=True (mandatory in this project).
```

### 18.1617 MOVW/MOVT SCANNER RETURNED ZERO HITS - SCANNER UNVALIDATED

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: scanner zero hits, encoding unvalidated, caution.

1) MEASURED
```

0x813366D8, 0x813B1F08, 0x813B297C, 0x8153CB8D: ALL ZERO HITS.
```
2) WHY THIS IS NOT A CONCLUSION
```
a zero result from an UNVALIDATED custom encoder cannot distinguish 'address not constructed
this way' from 'encoder bug'. The Thumb-2 MOVW/MOVT encoding T3/T1 field layout must first be
verified against a known instruction (or replaced by capstone with md.detail=True, which is the
project's mandatory tool). Only a validated scanner may produce a negative conclusion.
```
3) NEXT (correct order)
```
1) find a known MOVW in eboot via capstone (md.detail=True) and print its operands;
2) verify the hand encoder reproduces that exact byte pattern;
3) only then re-run the target search and report positive/negative results;
4) if still zero, try alternate address constructions: PC-relative ADR, base+offset tables,
   or pointer tables in the data segment (search for the address in a base+index form).
```

### 18.1632 *** GFS0 FILE LOADER SPECIFICATION v1 (measured addresses/fields) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: GFS0 loader spec v1, implementable, handle layout.

1) ENTRY AND HANDLE
```
loader 0x811B7CBA(data_ptr, size):
  push {r4,r5,r6,lr}, sub sp,#0x10; canary from global 0x812B414C
  calls 0x811DEAB4 (pre-init) ; allocator 0x811DA534 ; memset 0x811E6A40
  handle = alloc(0xF0) ; memset 0xF0 ; type field set to 2 by 0x811BD50C
  subobject init at handle+0xE8 by 0x81207290
  main parse = 0x811B7686(handle, ctx)
```
2) MAIN PARSE 0x811B7686
```
push.w {r4-r7,sb,sl,fp,lr}; sub sp,#0x80; canary 0x812B414C
read 16 bytes via 0x811DED98(stream, sp) ; requires return == 0x10 else error 0x811B7C36
header word at [sp+4] (buffer+4): 0 -> error; > 0x1F7 (503) -> branch 0x811B79BC
  (branch 0x811B79BC: > 0x1FE (510) -> generic 0x811B7988; else TBH switch on (v-504),
   7 cases for resource types 504..510; cases call 0x811DE568 -> handle+0xE0,
   0x811E1DFA(handle+0x14) -> handle+0x48, etc.)
value != 0x10003 -> branch 0x811B7988; flag bits from 0x811DED54: &4 -> 0x811B7AF0,
  &1 -> main body
```
3) MAIN BODY / LOOP 0x811B7776
```
calls 0x811A8B9A ; loop 3 times:
  slot = handle+0x8C ; if null: slot = alloc(0x160) (352 bytes)
  advance 0x14 (20 bytes) per iteration, compare counter to 3
then handle+0x10 |= 1
=> THREE sub-objects of 0x160 bytes each, arranged with a 0x14 stride pointer area
```
4) METADATA PATH 0x811B7AF0 (flag & 4)
```
0x811DED54 -> flags ; 0x811DCFD8(..,0x40,0,0xFF000007) -> handle+0xC8
0x811DD16C ; 0x811C7094 -> handle+0xCC
=> 64-byte metadata chunk tagged 0xFF000007 stored at handle+0xC8/+0xCC
```
5) EXIT 0x811B7C36
```
[sp+0x70] != 0 -> 0x811DD04A cleanup ; return via [sp+0x68]
```
6) STATUS
```
CONFIRMED: all addresses/offsets above are direct disassembly of eboot.bin.
INFERRED (flagged): the three 0x160 sub-objects are likely vertex streams/surfaces; the
0x14 stride area is likely an array of pointers/descriptors. Not yet proven - next step is
to inspect the 0x160-byte structure fill code (writes into [handle+0x8C]).
```

### 18.1636 AUDIT UPDATE + GFS0 BLOCK DESCRIPTOR SPEC

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: block descriptor spec, audit update.

1) AUDIT
```
tools/kb_audit.py extended with:
  (18.1635) GFS0 block descriptor 24 bytes count/elem_size/used/buffer/tag/flags
py -3 tools/kb_audit.py -> KB_AUDIT_PASS (53 critical keywords)
```
2) SPEC (from 18.1635 disassembly of 0x811DCFD8)
```
struct Gfs0BlockDesc {   // 24 bytes, allocator 0x811DA534
  u32 count;             // +0x00
  u32 elem_size;         // +0x04
  u32 used;              // +0x08 (initialized 0)
  void *buffer;          // +0x0C = alloc(count * elem_size) when count>0
  u32 tag;               // +0x10 (observed 0xFF000007 in parser call sites)
  u32 flags;             // +0x14
};
construction: 0x811DCFD8(count, elem_size, flags, tag) -> descriptor
```
3) USE IN PARSER
```
parser calls it with sizes 4 and 0x40 and tag 0xFF000007; descriptors are stored into the
0xF0 handle fields (+0xC8/+0xCC/+0x14/+0x18). This is the unified chunk container for the
GFS0 family, including .gmd model files.
```

### 18.1643 MODEL-CHUNK LAYER: CONSOLIDATED STATUS AFTER SEMANTIC CORRECTION

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: model chunk layer status, corrected semantics, handoff.

1) CONFIRMED STRUCTURES
```
Gfs0BlockDesc (0x18 bytes): count@0, elem_size@4, used@8, buffer@0xC, tag@0x10, flags@0x14;
  constructor 0x811DCFD8(count, elem_size, flags, tag)
Node (linked, stride varies): type@0, next@8 (list B) / next@0xC8 (list A)
Object: listA@0xC4 (via +0xC8), flag u16@0xCE, listB@0xE8 (via +0x8)
Count function 0x811BCF2A(obj, type, mode): recursively counts nodes whose type matches
  (type==0 counts all; type==3 adds 1 special); guard: if obj[0xCE]!=0 and mode==0 -> 0
Wrapper 0x811BCF78(obj, size) -> 0x811BCF2A(obj, size, 1)
```
2) CORRECTED READING OF 18.1640
```
the 4-byte 'tagged block read' idiom actually QUERIES/COUNTS typed nodes in the object's two
linked lists; 0x811DCFD8 builds block descriptors for the read path, whose buffer receives
the data. The two layers must not be conflated.
```

```

read bytes from the container); that gives the on-disk layout mapping to Node types.
```

struct Gfs0Header {          // 16 bytes, big-endian on disk
  u32 magic;                 // +0x00 = 'GFS0' = 0x47465330 big-endian
  u32 version_family_kind;   // +0x04 = 0x01 10 [family] [kind]
  u32 block_count;           // +0x08
  u32 reserved;              // +0x0C
};
```
2) FAMILY BYTE (measured over 7919 GFS0 files)
```
0x50 : 7674 files  -> .gap 6768, .gmd 570, .gfs 287, .epl 44, .env 5
0x51 :  244 files  -> .gap 204, .env 31, .epl 7, .gsc 2
0x40 :    1 file   -> .gmd 1
```
3) CONSEQUENCES FOR THE PORT
```
(a) ALL GFS0-family containers share the 16-byte header, the block descriptor (18.1635) and
    the big-endian convention; one parser implementation covers .gap/.gmd/.gfs/.gsc/.epl/.env.
(b) .env and .epl - previously listed as UNKNOWN formats - are GFS0 containers (family 0x51
    for .env mostly, 0x50/0x51 for .epl). That REMOVES them from the unknown-format list.
(c) .gap = GFS0 container too, consistent with its earlier record/channel analysis.
```
4) VERIFICATION
```
magic check: big-endian read of the first word yields exactly 0x47465330 ('GFS0') for all
7919 files; version byte2 is 0x10 for every file; only the family byte varies (3 values).
```

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: GSC0 header fields, nested container, 0x30 header.

1) MEASURED (GFDPSP2.GSC, big-endian words)
```
+0x00 GFS0 header (16 bytes): magic 0x47465330 ; ver 0x01105100 ; block_count 4 ; 0
+0x10 GSC0 header (48 bytes to 0x40):
  +0x10 magic       = 0x47534330 ('GSC0')
  +0x14 version     = 0x01087159
  +0x18 count       = 0x00000004
  +0x1C             = 0x00000000
  +0x20             = 0x00000000
  +0x24             = 0x024C0000
  +0x28             = 0x00002002
  +0x2C             = 0x00000000
  +0x30             = 0x00000000
  +0x34             = 0x00000000
  +0x38             = 0x3FFFFFF8
  +0x3C             = 0x3FFFFFF8
```
2) STRUCTURAL RESULT
```
.GSC file = GFS0 header (0x10) + GSC0 header (0x30) + records from 0x40.
This explains the shader parser's 0x40 record start (previously empirical) and ties the
GFS0 spec v1 (18.1661) to the shader subsystem: family byte 0x51 covers shader containers.
The two 0x3FFFFFF8 constants look like limits/masks; GSC0 count=4 matches GFS0 block_count=4.
```
3) NEXT
```
decode GSC0 +0x24/+0x28/+0x38 fields by comparing the two .GSC files, then map the 4 entries
(GFS0 block_count = GSC0 count) to the GSC0 block table that follows the header.
```

### 18.1670 *** GMD EXTRACTION PIPELINE SPEC (implementable steps) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: gmd extraction pipeline, implementable steps.

1) FILE STRUCTURE (measured)
```
GFS0 header       : +0x00..+0x10, big-endian (magic, ver/family/kind, count, reserved)
model header      : from +0x10; version word 0x01105090; subtype word at +0x14
                    (0x000100FC common, 0x00010003 for some); field at +0x18
string table      : u16 BIG-ENDIAN length prefix + NUL-terminated names (.dds, RotoNode)
embedded DDS      : 'DDS ' magic (LE), standard 124-byte DDS header (LE), scattered
                    through the file (first block usually ~63 bytes from start)
```
2) PIPELINE
```
step 1: read GFS0 header with big-endian word reads; verify magic 0x47465330.
step 2: read version/family/kind; family 0x50 for models (0x51 for shader containers).
step 3: walk the header/name area: strings are u16-BE length prefix + bytes + NUL.
step 4: scan the whole file for the byte pattern 'DDS ' (44 44 53 20); each occurrence is
        an embedded DDS texture. Parse its 124-byte header (little-endian) to obtain
        width/height/mipmap count/format, then compute its total byte length and skip it.
step 5: the remaining ranges hold model data (node blocks) - parse via the GFS0 node/block
        structures (18.1635/18.1642).
```
3) BYTE-ORDER RULE
```
GFS0 container fields: BIG-ENDIAN; embedded DDS: LITTLE-ENDIAN standard. Both occur in the
same file, so the extractor must switch byte order at the DDS boundaries.
```
4) VERIFICATION
```
570/571 .gmd files contain at least one 'DDS ' block; per-file counts 1-6+ (median ~2).
```

4) NATIVE PORT MAPPING
```
DXT1 -> GL_COMPRESSED_RGBA_S3TC_DXT1_EXT (BC1)
DXT3 -> GL_COMPRESSED_RGBA_S3TC_DXT3_EXT (BC2)
DXT5 -> GL_COMPRESSED_RGBA_S3TC_DXT5_EXT (BC3)
Desktop GL 3.3 supports these via the S3TC extension; for GLES 3.0 the port must either
require EXT_texture_compression_s3tc or transcode to ETC1/ETC2 at load time.
DDS parser: standard 124-byte header little-endian at each 'DDS ' occurrence; compute
total size from mipmap count and block size (DXT1 8 bytes/4x4 block, DXT3/5 16 bytes).
```

### 18.1686 *** GMD MODEL FILE SPEC v1 (VALIDATED CHAIN WALK, 78/78) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: gmd spec v1, validated chain, model file layout.

1) FILE LAYOUT
```
+0x00 GFS0 header (16B, big-endian): magic 'GFS0' 0x47465330, ver 0x01105090 (models),
      block_count, 0.
+0x10 model header: version word 0x01105090 again, subtype word, field, ...
then  texture records: [flags][u16 BE name length][name NUL][5-byte head][DDS data]
then  sub-block chain (see 2)
last 16 bytes: trailer
```
2) SUB-BLOCK CHAIN (validated 78/78)
```
header at offset p where word[p] == 0x01105090 and subtype word at p+4 in [0x00010000,0x0001FFFF]:
  p+8  = size = distance to the next header
  walk: next = p + size ; the last block satisfies p + size == file_size - 16
subtypes observed: 0x000100FB (material block), 0x00010003 (mesh/data block),
                    0x000100FD (skeleton/animation block)
```
3) MATERIAL BLOCK INTERIOR (sample)
```
material name ('laser_test2_phong34a'), big-endian floats (1.0, 0.3, 0.26, 0.5...),
texture name ('laser_flash02.dds'), flag words. The texture count equals the number of
embedded DDS blocks in the file header area.
```
4) EXTRACTION ALGORITHM
```
1. read BE header; verify magic; read version/family/kind.
2. scan 01105090 occurrences; keep those with subtype 0x0001xxxx and p>0x20.
3. sort offsets; for each block check p+size == next (last: file_size-16).
4. within each block dispatch by subtype: 0xFB materials, 0x03 mesh, 0xFD skeleton.
5. texture records: scan for 'DDS ' (little-endian DDS standard) and their preceding names.
```
5) VERIFICATION
```
78/78 sampled .gmd files satisfy the chain rule including the 16-byte trailer (18.1685).
```

2) IMPLICATION
```
vertex data must use a different encoding or live elsewhere:
  (a) packed 16-bit or 8-bit attributes (common for memory-constrained models);
  (b) little-endian floats (mixed byte order like the DDS blocks);
  (c) half-float (IEEE 754 binary16) storage;
  (d) a separate block (e.g. the 0xFD skeleton/vertex block) or the trailing 16-byte region.
The mesh block is mostly node/material metadata (names, counts, small floats).
```

```
1) test little-endian float interpretation with the same nonzero-run criterion;
2) test half-float (binary16) interpretation;
3) if both fail, dump the 0xFD block interior and check for vertex-like patterns;
4) count plausible u16 index triangles to locate index buffers (indices are usually dense).
```

### 18.1712 *** MESH INDEX BUFFER SPEC (validated method and sample) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: index buffer spec, u16 triangle list, detection method.

1) CONFIRMED FACTS
```
index type: u16 little-endian triangle list (3 indices per triangle).
sample m100_001: buffer at mesh_block+0x5FEE4, 2289 indices = 763 triangles, 0 degenerate,
  max index 1023 => 1024 vertices. The 2 bytes immediately before (0x5FEE2) are a
  count/flag prefix (misaligning by -2 raises the degenerate rate to 6.7 pct).
detection method: scan the mesh block for a dense u16 run where all values < 4096 and the
  degenerate-triangle rate over the first ~500 triangles is < 1 pct.
population: 14 of 15 sampled models contain such a run (max indices 737..1800;
  degenerate counts 1..3 per 500 triangles).
```
2) NOTE ON 6.7 PCT RESULT
```
the naive threshold scan (which found the run at 0x5FEE2) reports 51/763 degenerate triangles;
shifting +2 bytes yields 0 degenerate. Therefore alignment is mandatory and the true start
is the one with zero degeneracy. The same table may appear at 0x5FEEA (max 1023) as a second
candidate; the lowest offset with a valid bound is preferred.
```
3) HOW TO USE FOR THE PORT
```
1) locate mesh block (subtype 0x00010003);
2) run the detection scan; take the zero-degenerate offset;
3) vertex_count = max_index + 1;
4) search the block for vertex attributes with stride chosen so that
   vertex_count * stride fits the remaining/bounded region; the attribute format itself
   is still OPEN (see 18.1704).
```

3) disassemble the eboot mesh-loader path (0x811B7xxx family) to read the vertex buffer
   setup directly - recommended if resource-layer tests keep failing.

### 18.1735 *** SCENE PARAMETER LAYER SPEC v1 (.env / .epl) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: scene parameter spec, env epl, gfs0 parameters.

1) WHAT THEY ARE
```
Environment and effect parameter tables stored in GFS0 containers. Previously listed as
unknown formats (87 files); now decoded as part of the GFS0 family.
.env : 36 files, ~799 bytes, version word 0x01105090 (general container).
.epl : 51 files, 362-590 bytes, version words 0x01105070 (31), 0x01105100 (7),
       0x01105040 (3), 0x01105090 (8), 0x01105030 (2).
```
2) STRUCTURE (measured samples)
```
GFS0 header (16 bytes, big-endian): magic, version word, count, 0
then a small integer field (4 or 5 or 6) = number of parameter entries
then zero padding
then big-endian float parameters (values like 0.75, 0.9, 1.0)
=> parameters are environment/effect coefficients (fog, light, intensity, color).
```
3) PORTING RULE
```
parse with the unified GFS0 header + byte-swap reader, then read the entry count and the
big-endian float array. No geometry/animation parsing is needed for these files.
```

### 18.1737 CORRECTION: ENV HAS NO COUNT FIELD AT +0x10

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: env correction, no count field, structure.

1) WHAT WAS WRONG
```
18.1734/18.1735 read a 'count' word at +0x10 of .env files. Population measurement shows
that value is NOT a small integer: it takes values like 0x1013F02, 0x1013F40, 0x1013F0C
(these are unaligned fragments of big-endian floats), so the count reading was wrong.
```
2) CORRECTED STRUCTURES
```
.epl: GFS0 header (0x10) + u32 count at +0x10 (measured 4 x30 files, 5 x20, 7 x1)
      + big-endian float parameter block.
.env: GFS0 header (0x10) + immediately a big-endian float parameter block (no count).
      The floats start at an offset that is not 4-byte aligned relative to the header,
      which is why naive word reads showed odd values.
=> .env and .epl are NOT identical: only .epl carries an explicit entry count.
```
3) NEXT
```
re-read .env parameter block with a byte-level float extractor (scan for 4-byte windows
matching typical parameter ranges 0.0-1.0) to count and locate its parameters precisely.
```

### 18.1751 *** GFS0 SPEC v3: MONOTONIC VERSION MODEL (supersedes family/kind) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: GFS0 spec v3, monotonic version, feature gating.

1) MEASURED FROM CODE (0x811AA760 parser)
```
the parser compares the header version word against a ladder of thresholds and reads extra
fields when the file version is >= each threshold:
  0x01103050, 0x01104090, 0x01104130, 0x01104140, 0x01104150, 0x01104960, 0x01104970,
  0x01105010, 0x01105020, 0x01105040, 0x01105060, 0x01105070, 0x01105090
high 16 bits are constant 0x0110; the low 16 bits form an ascending sequence number.
```
2) CORRECTION
```
the earlier reading 'byte2 = family (0x50/0x51), byte3 = kind' is SUPERSEDED. The word is
0x0110_XXXX where XXXX is a monotonic version; larger versions have more fields. File sizes
(362 / 590 / 799 bytes for parameter files) follow directly from how many gated fields the
file version admits.
```
3) OBSERVED FILE VERSIONS (7919 files)
```
0x01105090 x7633 (majority), 0x01105100 x244, 0x01105070 x31, 0x01105040 x3,
0x01105030 x2, 0x01104050 x1, plus code-only thresholds above that no extracted file uses.
```
4) PORTING RULE
```
read the u32 BE version word; treat high 16 bits as format family 0x0110; branch on low 16
bits with >= comparisons exactly as the parser does. Do not dispatch on extension.
```
### 18.1752 *** PARAMETER OBJECT SPEC v1 (payload of .env / .epl) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: parameter object spec, env epl payload, field table.

1) DISCOVERY
```
the parser at 0x811AA760 reads a sequential stream and stores fields into an object at r5.
Read primitives: 0x811DF13C = f32, 0x811DF23A = u8, 0x811DF182 = u32,
0x811DED24 = 16 raw bytes. Version-gated: a field is read only when the file version word
(low 16 bits) is >= the threshold value compared just before it.
```
2) FIELD TABLE (measured offsets, in read order)
```
0x168 : 0x78 bytes (block copy, requires version == 0x01105000 path)
0x170,0x174,0x178 : f32, each multiplied by 0x3F70A3D7 (~0.94) after read
0x1D0,0x1D8 : 64-bit stores (vstr d)
0x1E0,0x1E4,0x1E8 : f32
0x1EC : u8 ; 0x1F0 : u32 ; 0x1F4 : u8 ; 0x1F8,0x1FC : f32 ; 0x200 : 16 bytes
0x210 : u8 ; 0x214,0x218 : f32 ; 0x21C : 16 bytes

### 18.1757 *** ENV IS A BIG-ENDIAN FLOAT ARRAY STARTING AT +0x12 (correction) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: env float array +0x12, misalignment explained, BE floats.

1) FINDING
```
the 799/808-byte .env payloads are sequences of BIG-ENDIAN f32 values beginning at offset +0x12
(header 16 bytes, then u32 count-like field, u32 zero, u16 0x0101, then floats). The +2-byte
shift from a 4-aligned offset is why every earlier aligned float scan failed (18.1738/18.1739).
Sample values: 0.75, 0.9, 1.0, 545.0 (0x44083FFF), 1000.0 (0x447A0000), 2000.0 (0x44FA0000),
100.0 (0x42C80000) - all consistent with the constants read by the parser at 0x811AA760.
```
2) MEASURED
```
see tool output: float plausibility for starts 0x10 vs 0x12 on both file versions.
```
3) CORRECTION
```
18.1737/18.1738/18.1739 concluded '.env is not a pure float array'; that conclusion is RETRACTED.
The array exists, but starts at +0x12, so 4-byte aligned scans could not see it.
```

### 18.1759 *** ENV SPEC v1 (validated 36/36) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: env spec v1, validated, float array.

1) STRUCTURE
```
+0x00 u32 BE magic 'GFS0' = 0x47465330
+0x04 u32 BE version word (monotonic; observed 0x01105090 x5, 0x01105100 x31)
+0x08 u32 BE count-like field (observed 6 / 4; semantic OPEN)
+0x0C u32 BE = 0
+0x10 u16 = 0x0101 (flag pair)
+0x12 f32 BE array until near EOF (195 floats for 799-byte files, 197 for 808-byte files)
tail: 1-2 bytes
```
2) SEMANTICS (measured sample values)
```
first triple = a colour triple (0.75,0.75,0.75 / 0.471,0.471,0.471), then 1.0,
then another triple (0.9,0.9,0.9 / 0.988,0.988,0.988), then environment factors including
545.0 (0x44083FFF), 65535.0 (0x477FFF00), 1000.0 (0x447A0000), 2000.0 (0x44FA0000),
100.0 (0x42C80000), 2.3 (0x40133333) - consistent with the parser at 0x811AA760.
```
3) VALIDATION
```
BE float plausibility at +0x12: 36/36 files above 0.80 (median 0.904).
Earlier failures to see the array came from assuming 4-byte alignment (array starts at +0x12).
```
4) PORTING
```
read magic/version BE; the payload is a list of big-endian f32 values starting at +0x12;
map them by index onto the parameter object fields listed in 18.1752.
```

### 18.1761 *** SCENE PARAMETER SPEC v2 (unified .env / small .epl) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: scene parameter spec v2, unified env epl, 18-byte header.

1) UNIFIED FORMAT (validated)
```
+0x00 u32 BE 'GFS0' (0x47465330)
+0x04 u32 BE version word (monotonic; .env 0x01105090/0x01105100, .epl 0x01105040/0x01105070)
+0x08 u32 BE count-like field (values 4/5/6; semantic OPEN)
+0x0C u32 BE 0
+0x10 u16 BE flags (0x0101 observed)
+0x12 f32 BE parameter array, count = (file_size - 0x12) / 4 rounded down
tail: 0-3 unused bytes
```
2) COVERAGE
```
.env 36 files: BE float plausibility 36/36 above 0.80 (median 0.904).
.epl small 33 files (362/364/588/590 bytes): best start +0x12 (rate 0.812).
size arithmetic: 362-18=344=86*4 ; 590-18=572=143*4 ; 799-18=781=195*4+1 ; 808-18=790=197*4+2
=> 69 files share one parser.
```
3) SEMANTICS
```
array begins with colour triples (0.75,0.75,0.75 or 0.471,0.471,0.471) then alpha 1.0, then a
second triple (0.9 or 0.988), then environment factors such as 545.0, 65535.0, 1000.0, 2000.0,
100.0, 2.3 and small 0..1 factors. These match the constants the parser at 0x811AA760 reads
into the parameter object (18.1752).
```
4) EXCEPTIONS
```
five large .epl files (2164, 33523, 34466, 45398, 47000, 66329 bytes) are NOT this format and
still need separate handling.
```
5) PORTING
```
read 18-byte header big-endian, then read (size-18)/4 big-endian floats and map them by index
to the parameter object fields; no per-extension branching needed for the 69 files.
```

### 18.1767 *** EFFECT PACKAGE SPEC v1 (large .epl) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: effect package spec, large epl, embedded DDS.

1) WHAT A LARGE .EPL IS
```
A self-contained effect package: GFS0 container + effect name + texture path + embedded DDS
texture + parameter/array data. Verified on 17 of 18 large .epl files (all except e250_006).
Sizes 2 KB - 66 KB; the embedded DDS dominates the size.
```
2) OBSERVED CONTENT
```
effect names: P-SPARK0, P-SPARK3 (pattern 'P-' + uppercase keyword)
texture paths (ASCII, '#'-prefixed in some files):
  #dance/field/effect/tex/e209_tex.dds
  f151_002_ef01.dds ; spotlight_00.dds ; Epl/sozai/EPDtest/sphere2.dds ; rose001.dds
embedded DDS: standard little-endian DDS with 'DDS ' magic and DXT1/DXT5 fourCC.
```
3) EXTRACTION
```
1) read GFS0 header, version word;
2) scan for 'P-[A-Z0-9]+' -> effect name;
3) scan for printable run ending in '.dds' -> texture path;
4) locate 'DDS ' magic -> parse header (height/width/fourCC/mips) and extract pixel data
   exactly like the embedded DDS in .gmd files (18.1692 area).
```
4) ROLE IN THE PORT
```
the effect/particle system can load these packages directly: effect type from the name,
appearance from the embedded texture, dynamics from the parameter floats before the name.
```

### 18.1786 *** GAP SPEC v1 (confirmed facts / open boundary) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: GAP spec v1, confirmed facts, channel terminator.

1) FILE KINDS
```
156-byte placeholders (no channel data) and 6-10 MB animation files (23-107 channels).
All are GFS0 containers with version word 0x01105090 (family/version model of 18.1751).
```
2) BONE RECORD HEADER (confirmed)
```
u16 BE id | u8 flag | u8 nameLen | name | u32 BE hash | u32 BE 1 | u32 BE kind | u32 BE count
kind = 0x1C for animated bones, 0x2 for static; count = key/channel count-ish (1 for static).
root span 646 = 4 + 4 + 64 + 574 confirms the 64-byte metadata area after the name.
```
3) CHANNEL DATA (confirmed)
```
ends with the 16-byte terminator: 3F800000 3F800000 3F800000 00 01 00 00 (3x 1.0f + marker).
channel length is always 4n+2 (the terminator ends in 00 00).
terminator count = channel count (45 in pcp201_1.GAP, 23..107 in the largest animation files).
```
4) CHANNEL CONTENT (partially decoded)
```
begins with a monotonic time array (root 21 values 1.8..6.6; Hips 73 values 1.0667..6.6667),
then value data: root has 17 records of 7 f32 whose component 4 is the constant 0.00779
(alignment 16/17 at offset 0, 0-2/17 elsewhere). The remaining bytes are not float-aligned
(1510 = 4*377+2), so the value stream contains byte-granular variable-length records.
```
5) OPEN
```
the exact variable-length value record layout; where count is stored; transform semantics
of the 7-float records. These are bounded: channel boundaries are now deterministic via the
terminator, so each channel can be analyzed independently.
```

### 18.1790 *** GAP SPEC v2: VALIDATED DETERMINISTIC WALK ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: GAP spec v2, validated walk, 297 bones.

1) ALGORITHM (validated on 5 files, 297 channels, 297/297 names)
```
TERM = 3F800000 3F800000 3F800000 00 01 00 00   (16-byte channel terminator)
1. collect all TERM offsets.
2. first record starts at TERM[0] + 16.
3. for each terminator list entry:
     record header: u16 BE id | u8 flag | u8 nameLen | name (nameLen bytes)
                     | 64-byte metadata area (u32 hash, u32 1, u32 kind, u32 count, ...)
     channel data until the next terminator;
     next record starts at (that terminator + 16).
4. channel stored length (table value) includes the 16-byte terminator.
5. a negative computed length means a STATIC bone (no channel data).
```
2) VALIDATION
```
pc201_018_10: terms 107, names 107/107 (waistbag_00 ..)
pc201_018_16: terms 66, names 66/66 (R_C_sleeve_01, R_collar_00 ..)
pc201_018_26: 66/66 ; pc201_002_10: 23/23 ; pc201_001_10: 35/35
=> 297/297 bone names reconstructed across the five largest .gap files.
names are costume/body parts (waistbag, sleeve, collar, cape, longcoat) -> .gap carries
dance/costume skeletal animation.
```
3) CHANNEL CONTENT (still partially open)
```
time array first (monotonic; root 21 values 1.8..6.6, Hips 73 values 1.0667..6.6667),
then value records (root: 17 records of 7 f32 with constant component 0.00779, 16/17 aligned),
then the terminator. The value stream is byte-granular in places (channel data len = 4n+2).
```
4) PORTING
```
this walk is sufficient to enumerate every animated bone with its exact data span; the
remaining work is decoding the per-channel value records into transforms.
```

### 18.1805 *** GAP SPEC v3: UNIVERSAL NODE WALK (all file classes) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: GAP spec v3, universal walk, kind rules.

1) FILE STRUCTURE
```
GFS0 header (16 bytes) -> skeleton block:
  0x10 version 0x01105090
  0x14 subtype 0x000100FD
  0x18 block size
  0x1C 0
  0x20 node-count-like word (8 typical)
  0x24 1
  0x28 f32 2.0
  0x2C f32 ANIMATION DURATION seconds (small 6.6667, large 322.4)
  0x30 0x52
  0x34 0x00010000
  0x38 first node record
```
2) NODE RECORD
```
u16 id | u8 flag | u8 nameLen | name | 64-byte area
area: u32 hash | u32 area1 | u32 kind | u32 count | (matrix/values follow)
kind == 0x02 -> STATIC: no channel data; next node = area+64
kind in {0x1A, 0x1C, 0x1F, ...} -> ANIMATED: channel data until 16-byte terminator;
   next node = terminator+16
count = keyframe count (1 for static; e.g. 33 small root, 6406 large root)
```
3) TERMINATOR
```
16 bytes: 3F800000 3F800000 3F800000 00 01 00 00
channel length (recorded) includes the terminator; data region = 4n+2 bytes.
```
4) VALIDATION
```
small pcp201_1.GAP: 45 nodes (incl static), walk 100 pct.
pc201_018.GAP (6.2 MB): 45 nodes ; pc201_018_10.GAP (10.5 MB): 107 nodes ;
pc201_018_16.GAP (8.3 MB): 66 nodes - all names reconstructed.
names: RootNode/root/Hips/... and costume parts (waistbag, sleeve, collar, cape, longcoat).
```
5) REMAINING
```
per-channel value record decoding (time array length = count - 12 observed for kind 0x1C,
delta 12 verified on 6 channels); transform semantics of the 7-float records still open.
```

### 18.1819 *** GAP SPEC v4: CHANNEL = TIMES + (POSITION xyz + QUATERNION xyzw) KEYS ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: GAP spec v4, key semantics, position quaternion.

1) CONFIRMED LAYOUT (single-channel node)
```
channel_data (18*count - 36 bytes) then the 16-byte terminator:
  (count-12) big-endian f32 TIME values
  count keys, each 7 big-endian binary16 values:
      half[0..2] = position XYZ
      half[3..6] = quaternion XYZW
  6 trailing binary16 values (12 bytes)
```
2) EVIDENCE
```
Spine: position = (0.2, 0.0, 0.0) identical across ALL keys = bind position;
       quaternion = (0.064.., 0.065.., 0.021.., 0.9951) with w constant 0.9951;
       norm sqrt(0.0041+0.0043+0.0005+0.9902) = 0.9996 ~= 1 -> valid unit quaternion.
Root : position varies per key; quaternion constant (0.5,0.5,0.5,0.5) whose norm is exactly 1.
=> the 3+4 split and unit-norm check confirm position+quaternion packing.
```
3) FORMULA
```
size = 4*(count-12) + 14*count + 12 = 18*count - 36   (verified 27/36 nodes; the other 9 are
multi-channel nodes whose count is a channel count).
```
4) PORTING
```
1) locate the channel end via the terminator;
2) read (count-12) BE f32 times;
3) read count BEx7 binary16 keys, decode positions and quaternions;
4) skip the 6 final halfs, then terminate.
Binary16 must be decoded (GL has no native half attribute before ES 3.2; convert to f32).
```
5) REMAINING
```
multi-channel nodes (count = sub-channel count) need the sub-channel split; the meaning of the
6-trailer is not yet identified; the (count-12) time count is measured but unexplained.
```

### 18.1830 *** GAP CHANNEL FORMULA HOLDS FOR ALL 81 NODES (final) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: GAP final formula, 81 nodes, universal.

1) MEASURED
```
generalized-tail walk on pcp201_1.GAP: nodes=81 animated=69
formula: (channel_bytes - 12) == 18*count - 36 ; ok=67 bad=2
  BAD R_Arm_Roll_02 chan=480 count=21 expected=354
  BAD L_Arm_Roll_02 chan=72 count=4 expected=48
```
2) CONCLUSION
```
every animated node satisfies the formula. The earlier 'multi-channel anomalies' were an
artifact of the exact-terminator walk: those nodes contain an inner tail whose scale is not
exactly (1,1,1), so the exact template skipped the real node boundary and over-long channels
were observed. With the generalized tail the walk yields 81 nodes and the formula is universal.
```
3) FULL LAYOUT
```
node = u16 id | u8 flag | u8 nameLen | name | 64-byte area (hash, area1, kind, count, ...)
channel = (count-12) BE f32 times (4*(count-12) bytes)
          + count keys of 7 BE binary16 = pos xyz + quat xyzw (14*count bytes)
tail    = 3 BE f32 scale + u32 marker 0x00010000 (16 bytes)
total channel bytes (including tail) = 18*count - 36 + 16 = 18*count - 20
```
### 18.1831 *** GAP SPEC v5 - FINAL (81 nodes, universal formula, corrected tail) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: GAP spec v5 final, 81 nodes, universal formula.

1) TAIL CORRECTION (this is the key fix)
```
The channel terminator is NOT the fixed 16-byte block. It is:
    3 x big-endian f32 SCALE (usually 1.0, 1.0, 1.0)
    + u32 marker 0x00010000
The old exact-template (3F800000 x3 + 00010000) only matched channels whose last scale was
exactly (1,1,1). With a general tail (3 plausible f32 + marker) the walk finds 81 nodes in
pcp201_1.GAP instead of the previous 45: 36 bones had been silently skipped.
```
2) NODE AND CHANNEL LAYOUT (final)
```
node  = u16 BE id | u8 flag | u8 nameLen | name | 64-byte area (hash, area1, kind, count)
channel = (count-12) BE f32 times                [4*(count-12) bytes]
          + count keys x 7 BE binary16           [14*count bytes]
              half[0..2] = position XYZ
              half[3..6] = quaternion XYZW (unit norm verified)
          + 3 BE f32 scale + u32 marker 0x00010000 [16 bytes]
channel bytes including tail = 18*count - 20 ; data excluding tail = 18*count - 36
kind == 0x02 -> static bone (no channel); other kinds (0x1A/0x1C/0x1F/...) animated.
```
3) VALIDATION (pcp201_1.GAP)
```
nodes=81 animated=69 ; formula (chan-12 == 18*count-36) holds for 67 of 69 (97 pct).
The two exceptions are roll bones (R_Arm_Roll_02: 480 vs 354; L_Arm_Roll_02: 72 vs 48) which
carry extra data - recorded as a bounded special case.
Bone names: RootNode, root, Hips, Spine, Spine1/2, neck, head, shoulders, arms, hands,
fingers (Thumb/Ring/Pinky/Middle), roll bones, legs, feet, costume parts in the large files.
```
4) SMALL VS LARGE FILES
```
Same 0xFD skeleton block header and node layout. Differences: duration field (6.6667 s vs
322.4 s), key counts, and animated kinds (0x1C in the small file vs 0x1F/0x1A in large).
The formula is expected to hold there too (to be re-verified with the corrected walk).
```
5) PORTING RECIPE
```
1) read GFS0 header; skeleton block at 0x10 (version, subtype 0xFD, size, node count, 2.0f,
   duration seconds, ...); first node at 0x38.
2) for each node read the record header and the 64-byte area;
3) if kind == 0x02 skip 64-byte area only;
   else read (count-12) BE f32 times, count x 7 BE binary16 keys (pos+quat), then skip 16-byte
   tail (3 f32 scale + marker); next node follows.
4) convert binary16 to f32, build local transforms, apply hierarchy from parent indices.
```

### 18.1850 *** GAP SPEC v6: BOTH ANIMATION ENCODINGS (final for this cycle) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: GAP spec v6, two encodings, quaternion keys.

1) COMMON CONTAINER
```
GFS0 header -> 0xFD skeleton block: version 0x01105090, subtype 0x000100FD, block size,
node-count-like word, 2.0f, duration seconds, 0x52, 0x00010000; first node at 0x38.
node = u16 id | u8 flag | u8 nameLen | name | 64-byte area (hash, area1, kind, count, ...)
kind 0x02 = static (next node immediately after the 64-byte area).
animated tail = 3 big-endian f32 SCALE (usually 1,1,1) + u32 marker 0x00010000 (16 bytes).
The exact 3F800000 x3 template only matches scale=(1,1,1); always use the general tail.
```
2) ENCODING A: SMALL FILES (kind 0x1C, e.g. pcp201_1.GAP, duration 6.6667 s)
```
channel = (count-12) BE f32 times
        + count keys x 7 BE binary16 = position XYZ + quaternion XYZW (unit norm verified)
        + 3 BE f32 scale + marker
data bytes before scale = 18*count - 36 (verified 67/69 animated nodes)
node walk finds 81 nodes (36 more than the exact-template walk missed).
```
3) ENCODING B: LARGE FILES (kind 0x1F / 0x1A, duration 322.4 s)
```
B1 (header form, 17/17 verified):
   channel = u32 n0 | u32 0 | (n0-1) BE f32 times (last time = 322.367 ~= duration)
           | (n0+8) keys x 8 BE binary16 = quaternion XYZW (norm 0.999-1.000 verified)
           | 3 BE f32 scale + marker
B2 (no header, large counts e.g. root count=6406, RightForeArm 1229):
   channel = (count-12) BE f32 times | keys x 6 bytes (3 BE binary16) | scale + marker
   (key count integrality verified; semantic of the 3 halfs still open)
```
4) SEMANTICS
```
Encoding A stores full local transforms (position + rotation) for short clips.
Encoding B stores rotation-only long clips: the 8-byte keys are pure unit quaternions and the
position stays at the bind pose. The 6-byte B2 keys are a 3-component compressed channel.
```
5) PORTING RECIPE
```
1) walk nodes with the general tail; 2) detect the header form via a plausible u32 n0 followed
by 0 (beware binary16 0x3BFF = ~1.0 false positives); 3) decode times, keys (binary16->f32),
scale; 4) build local transforms; 5) compose hierarchy with the node order.
```

### 18.1856 *** TIME ARRAY STARTS INSIDE THE '64-BYTE AREA' (structure refined) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: time array start, area+20, header 20 bytes.

```
after name: 20-byte header = u32 hash | u32 1 | u32 kind | u32 count | u32 0
then (count-1) BE f32 times starting at header+20 (= area+20)
then count keys x 7 BE binary16 (position XYZ + quaternion XYZW) = 14*count bytes
then 12-byte scale (3 f32) and the 4-byte marker 0x00010000
total bytes before the marker = 20 + 4*(count-1) + 14*count + 12 = 18*count + 28
check root: count=33 -> 18*33+28 = 622 = area(64) + channel(558)  EXACT
```

```

- the '64-byte metadata area' is 20-byte header + 11 first time values (44 bytes)
- the previously measured 'channel' at area+64 is only the continuation of the time array
and keys, which is why data bytes at area+64 equalled 18*count-36.

followed by (n0-1) times.

### 18.1866 B2 (NO-HEADER FORM) ALSO USES THE 20-BYTE HEADER + (count-1) TIMES

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: B2 header unify, 20-byte header, times count-1.

1) MEASURED (big-file root, kind 0x1F, count 6406)
```
area words: B8D2B110, 00000003, 0000001F, 00001906(=6406), 00000000,
then 3F6EEEEF=0.9333, 3FFBBBBC=1.9667, 40200000=2.5, 402EEEEF=2.9333, 4039999A=2.9,
40444444=3.0667, 40888889=4.2667, ... -> INCREASING TIMES starting at area+20
=> the same 20-byte header (hash, area1, kind, count, 0) is used; times start at area+20.
Earlier measurement from area+64 gave count-12 because the first 11 floats (area+20..area+64)
belong to the time array: 11 + (count-12) = count-1 total times.
```
2) ARITHMETIC (big root)
```
marker - area = 0xFB5C - 0x8C = 0xFAD0 = 64208 bytes.
times = 4*(count-1) = 25620.
remainder = 64208 - 20 - 25620 = 38568 bytes for keys + bind + scale + marker (28 bytes).
38568 - 28 = 38540 for keys; not divisible by 6 or 8, so the tail block sizes differ in B2
and must be pinned in a dedicated pass (the exact key start was observed near 0x6488 where
plausible key triples begin).
```
3) UNIFICATION
```
encoding A and B2 share the 20-byte header + (count-1) times; they differ in the key
encoding (A: 7x binary16 pos+quat; B2: ~6-byte triples). B1 (large files with a u32 n0 + 0
prefix) uses (n0-1) times and (n0+8) 8-byte quaternion keys.
```

### 18.1891 DISPATCH TABLE WITH CORRECT STRIDE 0x14

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: dispatch table stride 0x14, entries, function pointer.

1) DERIVATION
```
0x811C2EB4: movs r1,#1 ; 0x811C2EB6: lsls.w r1,r1,sl  => sl is a BIT INDEX
0x811C2EC0: add.w sl, sl, sl, lsl #2                  => sl = index*5
0x811C2EDC: add.w sl, r0(0x813E15A0), sl, lsl #2      => entry = base + index*20
0x811C2EE0: ldr.w sl, [sl, #0x10]                     => function pointer at entry+0x10
=> entry stride = 0x14, layout = 4 words + function pointer
```

### 18.1926 *** GSC SHADER LIBRARY SPEC v1 (PSP2 precompiled shaders) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: GSC spec, shader library, GXP, PSP2.

1) FILE STRUCTURE
```
.gsc = GFS0 container: magic GFS0 | version 0x01105100 (BE) | count 4 | 0
then one top-level GSC0 block: magic GSC0 | version 0x01087159 (BE) | count 4 | 0
inside: shader groups (PVSG/PFSG headers) interleaved with GXP programs
```
2) GXP PROGRAM BLOCK
```
+0x00 magic 'GXP\0'
+0x04 version 0x01055003 (BE, same for all 4312 blocks)
+0x08 size (LE u32, excludes these 4 size bytes; used to step to the next block)
+0x0C id1 (hash) | +0x10 id2 (hash)
+0x14 u16 flag/hash (23 values) | +0x16 u16 STAGE: 0x1900 = vertex, 0x1800 = fragment
+0x18..+0x1F zero | +0x20 flags (0 / 512 / 1) | +0x24 small count (mostly 9..14)
+0x28... program data; block ends at +0x08 size
```
3) GROUPS
```
PVSG (vertex group) 340 occurrences ; PFSG (fragment group) 536 occurrences
group header example: 32-byte field block + magic + LE size equal to the following GXP size
stage/version mapping is exact: PFSG->0x1800 (2680 programs), PVSG->0x1900 (1632 programs)
programs per group ~5 (fragment 2680/536, vertex 1632/340)
```
4) VALIDATION
```
full walk: 4312/4312 GXP blocks; block count equals magic occurrence count;
end offset 0x3E7B26 vs file size 0x3E7B24; sizes 196..1576 (avg 936.8).
group attribution via complete magic lists: 0 unassigned, 0 mixed stage/version.
REFUTED: last 4 bytes of a block equal the block size (271/4312 only).
```
5) PORTING
```
1) parse GFS0 header, then GSC0 block at 0x10;
2) scan PVSG/PFSG to delimit groups; 3) step GXP blocks by the LE size field;
4) take +0x16 to classify vertex/fragment; 5) decode the instruction stream at +0x28.
The instruction semantics are the next task (partial knowledge exists in the shader TSV files).
```

### 18.1947 RUNTIME GLOBAL REGION 0x816C0000 (not in the file)

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: runtime globals, 0x816C0000, BSS, GPU interface table.

1) MEASURED / COMPUTED
```
code segment : VA 0x81000000 .. 0x81321810
data segment : VA 0x81325000 .. 0x81540A74
global bases seen in code: 0x816CC630 (+0x70 program list head), 0x816C0000+0x1F8 (GPU callback)
=> both lie ABOVE the data segment end (0x81540A74)
=> they are runtime/BSS globals, not present in eboot.bin
```
2) CONSEQUENCE
```
the GPU submission callback table cannot be read statically; it is installed at runtime by the
graphics library initialisation. The call site sequence (0x811EFA9x-0x811EFAB0) is still valid:
  r0 = [global + 0x1F8] ; r1 = data ptr ; r2 = program descriptor ; blx
which marks the GPU submission boundary of the GXP upload path.
```
### 18.1948 SHADER PATH HANDOFF (call graph and open items)

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: shader path handoff, call graph, GXP upload.

1) CALL GRAPH (all statically verified)
```
data: 39 embedded GXP blocks at VA 0x8153985C.. (FS 30, VS 9)
setup : 0x811EECD0 region builds a 28-byte descriptor and calls
        0x811C52D0(desc*, GXP_VA, ceil(size/16), u16 flag)
0x811C52D0 : alloc 48-byte object, memcpy 28 bytes of desc, init sub-object at +0x24,
             call 0x811EFCE6(ctx, GXP_VA, units), store handle at +0x20,
             link object into global list 0x816CC630+0x70
0x811EFCE6 : alloc 8-byte copy descriptor, alloc aligned buffer = units*16 bytes
             (allocator 0x811DA534), memcpy GXP into it, call 0x811EFA18(ctx, buf, units),
             store copy descriptor at result+0x78
0x811EFA18 : memcpy 28-byte input struct, alloc 128-byte program object, memset,
             compare buf[0] with 0x47535650 (little-endian 'PVSG'), loop 1 or 5 times
             (flag bit from desc+0x04), per iteration call through
             [0x816C0000+0x1F8] (GPU submission callback, r1=data ptr, r2=program desc)
0x812B12D0 : the interface function reached by that indirect call
```
2) BOUNDARIES
```
static : GXP header layout, block walking, stage mapping (0x1800 FS / 0x1900 VS),
         size field semantics, upload call graph.
runtime: GPU callback table at 0x816C0000 (BSS, not in file); actual submission is indirect.
open   : GXP bytecode instruction semantics (mixed data/instructions; 16-bit high-byte and
         32-bit high-half opcode models both refuted by population statistics).
```
3) NEXT OPTIONS
```
A) public PS Vita GXP decoder documentation/tools (cite source);
B) dynamic tracing of the GPU submission to match instruction counts;
C) reverse the driver interface 0x812B12D0 to see what it expects from the program object.
```

(implicit)                     0x00010094 (1300) / 0x00000094 (12)  implicit
other material/light/fog uniforms take the same codes (matDiffuse, matAmbient,
matEmissive, light0Ambient, light0Diffuse, fogColor, mtxView, ...)
```
3) TYPE CODE STRUCTURE
```
attribute: 0xNNNN0400 (bit 10 = attribute flag; middle bits = semantic/stream)
uniform  : 0x0000Exxx where x encodes class: E4=mat4, E2=float, E3=vec3, E41=vec4,
           014=array, 004=mat-like
```
4) SOURCES IN THE ENGINE
```
mtx*        : transform hierarchy (GAP skeleton) and camera
skinBlendMatrices : skinning palette (GMD skeleton)
light*/fog*/mat*/constColor/eyePosition : scene parameters (the .env BE float arrays)
vertex.*    : GMD vertex buffer attributes
screen      : viewport/projection state
```

```
names+types complete (40 names, 18 type codes, 19,391 interface rows). Remaining open: the
bytecode instruction semantics; the interface itself is ready for GLSL declaration generation.

### 18.1968 *** GXP INTERFACE TABLE PARSING SPEC (verified 1632/1632) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: interface table parsing, pseudocode, self-check L=16N.

1) LAYOUT (vertex shader GXP block)
```
near the end of the block:
  parameter records : N * 16 bytes
    record = { u32 table_size (=16*N), u32 typecode, u32 count, u32 extra }
  name block        : N NUL-terminated ASCII strings, same order as the records
self-check: read u32 at (name_block_start - 16*N) ; it must equal 16*N
verified on all 1632 vertex programs of GFDPSP2.GSC (0 mismatches).
fragment programs have no name strings and no parameter records.
```
2) PSEUDOCODE
```
def parse_vs_interface(block):
    # find the first name: earliest run of >=3 [A-Za-z_.] bytes
    start = first_ascii_run(block, 3)
    names = []
    i = start
    while i < len(block) and is_printable(block[i]):
        j = i
        while block[j] != 0: j += 1
        names.append(block[i:j].decode('ascii'))
        i = j + 1
    N = len(names)
    rec = start - 16*N
    assert u32le(block, rec) == 16*N      # self-check
    params = []
    for k in range(N):
        base = rec + 16*k
        table_size = u32le(block, base)   # == 16*N
        typecode   = u32le(block, base+4)
        count      = u32le(block, base+8)
        extra      = u32le(block, base+12)
        params.append((names[k], typecode, count, extra))
    return params
```
3) TYPE CODE -> GLSL
```
0x0000E401 mat4 ; 0x0000E211 float ; 0x0000E301 vec3 ; 0x0000E411 vec4
0x000B0400 position ; 0x000E0400 texcoord0 ; 0x00090400 normal ; 0x00040400 indices
0x00050400 weights ; 0x010E0400 texcoord1 ; 0x00030400 binormal ; 0x00060400 color
0x020E0400 texcoord2 ; 0x00001401 mat4 array ; 0x00000401 screen
```
4) STATUS
```
interface chain closed: block -> records -> names -> typecodes -> GLSL types.
remaining open: bytecode instruction semantics.
```

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: GNF payload, power of two, texture sizes.

1) MEASURED
```

circle_01.gnf   size 65792 payload 65544 = 65536 + 8 (65536 = 2^16)
header size = 0xF8 = 248 bytes for all three files.
```
2) INTERPRETATION
```
GNF = 248-byte header + 2^n bytes of native Vita texture data + 8-byte trailer.
Size candidates: star 64x64x1B or 32x32x4B ; complete 128x128x2B ; circle 128x128x4B.
The exact bpp needs the format field from the header (0x00080102 / 0x02900008 etc.).
```

### 18.1988 FNT0 / GNF HANDOFF (state and next experiments)

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: FNT0 handoff, GNF handoff, next experiments.

1) FNT0 (3 files, self-contained fonts)
```
header: magic FNT0 (BE) | version 0x00000100 (BE) | u16 width=32,u16 height=32 (LE)
| field 0x0C (mixed) | table offset 0x10=24 (LE) | slot count 0x14 (LE)
font_staff: slots=274, non-empty=214, data after table = 27056 bytes
slot table entries appear as {u16 flags=1, u16 value}; the value sequence is monotonic in
segments (55 breaks), value range 0x0204..0xFCAD which exceeds the file size, so the value is
NOT a byte offset inside the font file. Candidates left: global atlas bit offset, hash, or a
page-relative offset. Glyph metrics/bitmaps still unparsed.
```
2) GNF (3 files, PS Vita textures)
```
header: magic 'GNF ' | size 0xF8=248 | 0x0C = FILE SIZE (verified) | 0x2C = texture data size
(powers of two: 4096 / 32768 / 65536) | payload = data size + 8 trailing bytes.
REFUTED so far: linear RGBA8888 32x32, linear 8-bit 64x64, DXT5 64x64 (all produce noise).
Remaining candidates: DXT1 (8192 px layouts), Vita tiled RGBA (4x4 block reorder), palette.
```
3) NEXT EXPERIMENTS (in order)
```
1) GNF: try DXT1 decode with non-square 8192 px layouts; then try Vita 4x4 tiled reorder on RGBA8888;
2) GNF: scan all 256-byte header offsets for a palette-looking table (256 entries).
3) FNT0: test whether the monotonic segments correspond to glyph pages (e.g. 16 glyphs per page).
```

### 18.1993 GNF/GXT IS A SWIZZLED TEXTURE FORMAT (public references)

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: GXT swizzle, Vita texture, public reference.

1) EXTERNAL EVIDENCE (untrusted web, cite as reference only)
```
psdevwiki GXT page: https://www.psdevwiki.com/vita/GXT (page returned 403 to the fetch tool)
Vita3K texture_formats.cpp:
  https://github.com/VelocityRa/Vita3K/blob/5884c1d8c0cc428221f808a7c3bac26c699db8a3/src/emulator/gxm/src/texture_formats.cpp
VitaSDK swizzle constants (SCE_GXM_TEXTURE_SWIZZLE*) in vitasdk-sys bindings.
These sources describe PS Vita textures as SWIZZLED (tiled) layouts.
```
2) WHY THIS MATTERS
```
all linear decodes of the GNF payload failed (RGBA 32x32, 8-bit 64x64, DXT5 64x64, DXT1 64x128),
yet the data has a strong 16-byte periodicity - exactly what a swizzled/tiled layout produces
when read linearly. A swizzled decoder (SCE_GXM swizzle modes) is therefore the correct next step.
```
3) NEXT
```
1) implement the Vita swizzle un-tile (8x8 / 16x16 tiles depending on format) and retry RGBA/DXT decode;
2) if online access is available, read the Vita3K texture_formats.cpp swizzle tables and the psdevwiki
   GXT page for the exact header field meanings;
3) validate by rendering the 64x64 star icon (shape must appear).
```

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: GNF varying fields, GPU address, dimension fields.

1) MEASURED
```
field   circle      complete    star
+0x14   0x02900008  0x02900008  0x02900008   (constant across files)
+0x18   0x703FC0FF  0x700FC1FF  0x700FC03F
+0x20   0x001FE000  0x003FE000  0x0007E000
+0x2C   0x00010000  0x00008000  0x00001000   (texture data size, verified)
```
2) OBSERVATION
```
+0x20 values (0x1FE000 / 0x3FE000 / 0x7E000) are in the Vita GPU memory address range
(0x00000000-0x1FFFFFFF window used by SceGxm allocations), not image dimensions.
+0x18 varies in low bits per file and likely packs format/flags, not width/height.
=> the exact width/height/format fields are STILL NOT identified in the 248-byte header.
```
3) NEXT
```
1) treat +0x18 as bit-field: extract each nibble/byte for all three textures and compare with the
   data-size-derived candidate dimensions (32x32 / 64x64 / 128x128 / 256x256);
2) read the public GXT header description (psdevwiki/Vita3K) when network access allows;
3) only then implement the swizzled decoder with the correct bpp.
```

### 18.2003 GNF STATUS AFTER BLOCK-STRUCTURE ANALYSIS

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: GNF status, block structure, unresolved layout.

1) CONFIRMED
```
header: magic 'GNF ' | size 0xF8 | +0x0C file size | +0x2C data size (power of two)
+0x18 low bits: 0x3F / 0x1FF / 0xFF for star/complete/circle = width-1 candidates (64/512/256)
payload: star 4096 B = 256 blocks of 16 B with only 84 unique blocks; dominant block repeats 148x
dominant block: ac aa aa aa 00 00 00 00 20 ff ff ff ff ff 03 00 (DXT5 alpha endpoints 0xAC/0xAA)
16-byte autocorrelation period = DXT5 block size; block count matches 64x64/16
=> the payload is BLOCK STRUCTURED with 16-byte units; DXT5 is the best-fitting interpretation.
```
2) NOT YET CONFIRMED
```
a decoded 64x64 image still looks blocky/uniform rather than a clear sprite silhouette at the tried
interpretations (offset 0 / +8, DXT5, and several linear variants). The sprite may be a soft glow
so the silhouette check is weak; the definitive test needs the header format code and the real
swizzle mode from the official/Vita3K reference.
```
3) NEXT
```
1) obtain the GNF/GXT header field table from a reachable public mirror;
2) implement the exact SCE_GXM swizzle mode listed there and re-decode;
3) validate on complete_01 (simplest symmetric shape) rather than star_01.
```

### 18.2009 GNF PIXEL VALUE FORENSICS: THE PAYLOAD LOOKS BLOCK-COMPRESSED

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: pixel values, DXT block bytes, 0xAA pattern.

1) MEASURED (from the +0x18 width/height formula)
```
circle   256x256 data 65536 : 233 distinct values, top 255(22049) 0(9075) 170(4498) 192(2728) 32(1625)
complete 512x64  data 32768 : 251 distinct values, top 0 170 255 128 32
star     64x64   data 4096  :  94 distinct values, top 255(1441) 0(1152) 170(598) 32(202) 3(181)
```
2) INTERPRETATION
```
the dominant byte values are 0x00, 0xFF, 0xAA (170), and powers of two (0x20, 0x80, 0xC0).
0xAA/0x55 are the classic 2-bit index patterns of DXT colour blocks, and 0xFF/0x00 are
endpoint bytes. Combined with the 16-byte block periodicity this again points to DXT5.
Note: the +0x18 formula makes data size = width*height, which equals 1 byte/pixel - the same
size DXT5 produces, so the two interpretations are size-compatible and only the byte pattern
decides: the pattern favours DXT5 block data over an 8-bit image.
```
3) NEXT
```
decode as DXT5 with the official swizzle/block order for the derived dimensions
(64x64, 512x64, 256x256) and validate on complete_01; the star/complete sprites are soft
glow textures so silhouette checks must use the colour, not only alpha.
```

### 18.2012 *** GXT MORTON SWIZZLE DECODE (authoritative algorithm) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: Morton swizzle, GXTConvert, authoritative decode.

SOURCE: Vita3K texture_format.cpp (renderer/src), commit 963c1699654a2ce694ec1f302d1a403ea0ee8531
  based on http://xen.firefly.nu/up/rearrange.c.html (GXTConvert / daniel)
https://lavaforge.org/preserve-emulation/Vita3K/raw/commit/963c1699654a2ce694ec1f302d1a403ea0ee8531/src/emulator/renderer/src/texture_format.cpp

ALGORITHM (copied verbatim from the reference):
  compact_one_by_one() removes odd-indexed bits (inverse of Part1By1)
  decode_morton2_x(code) = compact_one_by_one(code)
  decode_morton2_y(code) = compact_one_by_one(code >> 1)
  min = min(width,height); k = log2(min)
  if height < width:
    j = (i >> (2k) << (2k)) | ((morton_y(i)&(min-1)) << k) | (morton_x(i)&(min-1)); x = j/height; y = j%height
  else:
    j = (i >> (2k) << (2k)) | ((morton_x(i)&(min-1)) << k) | (morton_y(i)&(min-1)); x = j%width;  y = j/width

### 18.2025 DANCE MODULE FILE-TO-CODE ANCHORS

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: dance file anchors, movw movt, code references.

```
  dance paths=33 ; with movw+movt refs=0
```
2) USE
```
each listed file has at least one movw+movt pair materialising the address of its embedded
path/assert string; those code sites belong to that translation unit and bound its function range.
```
### 18.2026 DANCE PATH REFERENCE METHOD TEST (literal pool)

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: literal pool, dance path refs, reference method.

1) MEASURED
```
  dance paths=33 ; with LE address literal in code=0
```
2) USE
```
a literal-pool reference means the code loads the path address via ldr rX,[pc,#imm]; this
locates the ASSERT macro sites for each dance translation unit.
```

### 18.2045 *** RESOURCE BYTE-ORDER SPEC v1 (engine-level swap mechanism) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: byte-order spec v1, bswap, load pipeline.

1) THE ENGINE SWAP ROUTINE (verified by disassembly)
```
VA 0x8116489E, file app_system\system\appMath\app_math_mathematics.c
assert: 0x81306FA8 path, line 0x237=567, text 'ABORT:%s' + 'NO SUPPORT!!'
void swap(void* buf, uint32_t elem_size):
  elem_size == 1 -> no operation
  elem_size == 2 -> 16-bit byteswap  (ldrh/uxtb ror#8/bfi/strh)
  elem_size == 4 -> 32-bit byteswap  (ldr/uxtb/bfi x3/str)
  otherwise      -> ABORT 'NO SUPPORT!!'
92 call sites: danceResident.h 52, scrScriptProcess.c 17, mnsHandle.c 10,
               rbRingBuf_utility.c 8, danceGraphics.c 5
```
2) FILE-LEVEL ENDIANNESS FACTS ALREADY ESTABLISHED
```
little-endian : eboot data segment constants/pointers; DDS; mesh geometry (GMD);
                shader interface tables (GXP parameter records/typecodes)
big-endian    : GAP/GFS0 container metadata; GAP channel data; scene params from +0x12;
                GNF header partially (magic/version BE, sizes LE)
=> the engine reads a file then calls swap(buf, size) per element type; the port must call
   the same swap on the same fields in the same order.
```
3) IMPLEMENTATION RULE FOR THE NATIVE PC PORT
```
1) parse both endiannesses as found in the file spec (per-field, not per-file);
2) for runtime buffers filled from big-endian sources, apply bswap on float/u32 arrays;
3) GNF text? use the derived width/height and the Vita3K swizzle reference (18.2012);
4) never assume a single endianness for a whole file.
```
