### 18.2053 *** CORRECTION: 0x8115D36A IS THE DEBUG-ALLOCATOR ENTRY, NOT A FILE LOADER ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: correction, debug allocator, not a loader, retraction.

1) CORRECTED STATEMENTS
```
18.2015 and 18.2049 called 0x8115D36A an 'async file loader / load primitive'. RETRACTED.
proof (18.2052 disassembly): the function only touches the manager object:
  count = manager[0x14]; if 0 -> return 0; if index >= count -> ABORT (line 77)
  base  = manager[0x04]; record = base + index*0x44 (stride 68 bytes)
  then stores name/size/flags fields; calls only allocator-internal helpers
  (0x8115D8E0, 0x8115D91A, 0x8115D9B2, 0x8115D968). NO file/IO calls at all.
=> it is 'register a named allocation record' in a debug/tracking allocator.
```
2) REINTERPRETATION OF THE CALL SITES
```
app_main (18.2049): alloc 12B context, then register a 0x30-byte record tagged with
  'E:\P3DP5D\xrd757\program\app\app_system\main\app_main.c' - i.e. a named allocation,
  not a resource load.
mainMenuWipe (18.2015): same pattern, 0x1A0=416 byte named allocation, callbacks are the
  post-allocation handlers (0x811198C9 / 0x811199CF), not load-completion callbacks.
```
3) NEWLY ESTABLISHED STRUCTURE
```
debug allocator manager: +0x04 = record array base, +0x14 = record count,
record stride = 68 bytes (0x44); record holds name pointer (source path), size, flags.
```
4) NEXT
```
re-disassemble 0x811198C9 / 0x811199CF (what really happens after allocation) and the
allocator helpers 0x8115D8E0/D91A/D9B2/D968; then find the REAL resource-loading entry
(likely appFiler / appFile modules in the source inventory).
```

### 18.2063 *** EVENT TABLE FORMAT v1 (u32 count + 20-byte records) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: event table v1, 20 byte records, embedded bin.

1) VERIFIED ALIGNMENT
```
of all embedded .bin tables, 647 satisfy (size-8) %% first_u32 == 0; of those 641 give
record size 20 bytes (99%) and 6 give 21 bytes. Example e102_010_009_0102.bin:
  size 5408 = 8 + 270*20 ; header = (270, 0) ; 270 records decoded.
```
2) FORMAT
```
+0x00 u32 count        (number of records)
+0x04 u32 reserved     (always 0 so far)
+0x08 count * 20 bytes, each record = 5 x u32:
  w0 : i32  (negative values observed -16..-74) time offset / keyframe delta
  w1 : u32  (0x40A,0x1C3,0x133,0 observed) size / duration / resource id
  w2 : u32  (2 observed) type/flag
  w3 : u32  (0 observed) reserved
  w4 : u32  (1 or 3 observed) mode enum
file size == 8 + count*20
```
3) NAMING
```
entries inside the 135 ARC containers: 5,160 .bin + 16 nested .arc.
event-like names follow e{chapter}_{a}_{b}_{c}.bin, e.g. e102_010_009_0102.bin.
```
4) STATUS
```
container + alignment + record size are CONFIRMED (population-level). Field semantics of w0/w1/w2/w4
are candidates; verification: sample more tables, correlate w1 with resource ids, correlate w0 ordering.
```

### 18.2067 *** EVENT TABLE SPEC v2 (confirmed semantics) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: event table v2, confirmed fields, sentinel -96.

1) CONTAINER + ALIGNMENT (confirmed population-level)
```
8-byte header {u32 count, u32 0} then count * 20-byte records; file size == 8 + count*20.
641 of 647 divisible tables use 20-byte records; sources = 5,160 .bin entries in 135 ARC files.
```
2) RECORD FIELDS
```
+0x00 i32 w0 : -96 = INACTIVE sentinel (87%% of them also have w1=0 and w4=0)
                otherwise -2..-95 (95 distinct values, all present) = negative count/delay
+0x04 u32 w1 : parameter (size/duration/resource id); 0 when inactive
+0x08 u32 w2 : ALWAYS 2 (71,644/71,644 records) = table-family marker
+0x0C u32 w3 : ALWAYS 0 (reserved)
+0x10 u32 w4 : 0 = inactive ; 1..5 = event type/mode (5 classes); rare 174/190 exist
```
3) EVIDENCE
```
sentinel group: 18,925 records, w1==0 16,515 (87.3%%), w4==0 16,435 (86.9%%)
normal group : 139,999 records, w1==0 only 3,142 (2.2%%), w4 spread over 1..5
```
4) REMAINING OPEN
```
meaning of the w0 magnitude -2..-95 (frames/seconds?), the 5 event-type classes,
and the rare w4 values 174/190.
```

### 18.2070 LAST RECORD IS A FOOTER (w4 == count)

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: footer record, last record count, terminator.

1) MEASURED
```
tables=641 ; last record w4 == count: 641 ; second-to-last record w4 in 0..5: 641
```
2) USE
```
if the last 20 bytes always carry the count in w4, the table is: header + (count-1) real records
+ one 20-byte footer/terminator whose w4 encodes the record count.
```
### 18.2071 *** EVENT TABLE SPEC v3 (footer self-check, 641/641) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: event table v3, footer self check, count field.

1) STRUCTURE (confirmed on all 641 tables)
```
+0x00 u32 count          total record slots INCLUDING the footer
+0x04 u32 0
+0x08 (count-1) real records, 20 bytes each
last  1 footer record, 20 bytes, whose w4 == count  <-- SELF CHECK (641/641 = 100%)
file size == 8 + count*20
```
2) REAL RECORD
```
+0x00 i32 w0 : -96 = inactive sentinel ; else -2..-95 (negative count)
+0x04 u32 w1 : parameter (0..~1300)
+0x08 u32 w2 : ALWAYS 2
+0x0C u32 w3 : 0
+0x10 u32 w4 : 0..5 = event type (real records only)
```
3) FOOTER RECORD
```
observed examples: [-90, 0x443, 2, 0, count] ; [-76, 0x1AB, 2, 0xC1, count]
w4 == count is the self check; w1/w3 in the footer are not yet understood (hash? checksum?).
```
4) RESOLUTION OF THE RARE-w4 MYSTERY
```
earlier 'rare w4 values = 8k+6' (18.2068/18.2069) are explained completely: they are the
footer records and their value is the table's own count. No layout anomaly exists.
```
5) PARSER RULE
```
read header, read (count-1) records, read footer, assert footer.w4 == count.
```

### 18.2094 *** DSFT MYSTERY RESOLVED CONTEXT: stage_format TABLES ARE DSFT FILES ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: DSFT resolved context, stage_format, magic DSFT, 75.0.

1) DECISIVE LINK
```
stage_format_table.arc (outer, 3 variants _p3/_p5/_tt)
  -> stage_format_table_p5.arc (5920 B, 45 entries)
     -> partner_type_table.bin (64 B, magic 'DTBL' = 0x4C425444)
     -> stage_format_001.bin .. stage_format_0NN.bin (96 B each, magic 'DSFT' = 0x54465344)
=> the files analysed earlier as 'DSFT (layout known, semantics open)' ARE these
   stage_format stage-description tables.
```
2) THE FORMER UNRESOLVED VALUES FOUND IN PLACE (stage_format_001.bin)
```
+0x00 'DSFT' ; +0x04 1 ; +0x08 1 ; +0x0C 0x3C(60) ; +0x10 0xC9(201) ; +0x14 0
+0x18 0x42960000 = float 75.0      <-- the previously unresolved '75.0' value
+0x1C 0x43520001 ; +0x20 0x4352AAAC (float 210.0-ish / 210.666?)
+0x28 0xFFFFFFFF ; +0x34 4 ; +0x48 0x000100D6 <-- the previously unresolved 0x0001xxxx pattern
```
3) MEANING OF THE LINK
```
DSFT = per-stage format/parameter description (44 stage_format files p5).
the 75.0 / 0x0001xxxx values are stage-format parameters, so their semantics must be studied
across all 44 stage tables (variation analysis) rather than on a single sample.
```
4) NEXT
```
1) dump the 96-byte field grid for all 44 stage_format_*.bin and diff the columns;
2) correlate changing fields with stage ids / songs;
3) then finalize the DSFT field spec with the known disk->runtime -0x10 rule.
```

+0x20 f32 PARAM B      (== A + 0.6667 in all samples)

+0x34 u32 4

43 stage files: 19 with size-mode 75.0 (param A in 152.67..224.33) and

stage ids start at 201. the size-mode boundary is stage id 218: ids 201..217 are 75.0,
id 218 onward are 100.0. secondary id becomes non-zero at id 218.

meaning of param A (distance/size candidate, NOT an angle because it exceeds 360),
the 0x48 flag bits, and the exact mapping stage-id -> song/stage name.

read 96 bytes; assert magic DSFT; stage_id=+0x10; size_mode=f32@+0x18 in {75,100};
A=f32(@0x1C & 0xFFFFFFF0); B=f32(@0x20 & 0xFFFFFFF0); assert abs(B-A-2/3)<0.01.

### 18.2106 *** DSCE SPEC v1 (screen effect trigger-time table) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: DSCE spec v1, trigger times, screen effect.

1) LOCATION
```
screen_effect_table.arc -> screen_effect_table_p5.arc -> screen_effect_NNN.bin (36 files)
```
2) LAYOUT (measured on 36 files)
```
+0x00 'DSCE' (0x45435344)
+0x04 u32 1
+0x08 u32 count  (42..141)
+0x0C u32 8      (item size)
+0x10 count * 8 bytes items
tail: 0..24 bytes, starts with a repeated 'DSCE' magic + u32 1 + zero padding
=> size == 16 + count*8 + stub where stub in {0,8,16,24}
```
3) ITEMS
```
item = ( f32 time_seconds , f32 0.0 )
time is non-decreasing in all files (29/29 with >=2 items), spanning 0.00 .. 218.50 s.
the second float is 0.0 in ALL 1,273 items measured -> DSCE is a TRIGGER TIME TABLE,
not a (time,value) curve. The earlier 'value curve' reading (18.2103) is RETRACTED.
```
4) PARSER RULE
```
assert magic DSCE; count = u32@8; items at 16 + 8*i, i<count; verify that item times are
non-decreasing; the remaining bytes are a DSCE magic stub.
```
5) OPEN
```
why some files have stub 0 and others 8/16/24 (alignment vs extra terminator records),
and what gameplay triggers the times (beat events?).
```

### 18.2110 *** DANCE DATATABLE FAMILY SPEC v1 (D* magics) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: dance table family, D* magics, spec v1.

1) CONTAINER CHAIN (all six tables share it)
```
code path dance/table/<kind>/<name>_%03d.bin
 -> <name>_table.arc (outer, 2-3 variants: _p3 / _p5 / _tt)
 -> <name>_table_p5.arc (P5D variant, numbered entries)
 -> <entry>.bin (data file)
P5D (PCSH10109) uses the _p5 variants; _p3 is Persona3 Dancing data, _tt is smaller/shared.
```
2) THE FAMILY (measured)
```
DSFT stage_format_table   43 files  96 B   stage format params (spec v1: 18.2099)
DSCE screen_effect_table  36 files  var    screen-effect trigger times (spec v1: 18.2106)
DEFT stage_event_table    43 files  96/32B stage event params
DEFT persona_event_table  32 files  32 B   persona event descriptors
DENE stage_enemy_table    32 files  32 B   enemy descriptors (all empty: -1,68)
DADJ motion_adjust_table  34 files  43/32B motion adjust descriptors (0,12)
```
3) STRUCTURE PATTERNS
```
A) 16-byte descriptor records: {magic[4], u32 1, u32 value, u32 payload_size}
   -> DENE/DADJ/persona-DEFT; files are 32 B = 2 descriptors per stage.
B) header + records: {magic[4], u32 1, u32 count, u32 record_size} + count records
   -> DSFT (96 B single record), 96 B DEFT (count 4/5, record 16 B).
C) header + items + stub: DSCE (16 + count*8 + 0..24 B stub).
```
4) OPEN
```
field semantics of DEFT/DENE/DADJ records, the payload locations (68/12/16 B), the mapping
stage id (201+) -> song/stage, and the meaning of the _tt variant.
```

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: stage event spec v1, DEFT timeline, event types.

1) CONTAINER CHAIN
```
stage_event_table.arc -> stage_event_table_p5.arc -> stage_event_NNN.bin
(also persona_event_table -> persona_event_NNN.bin for the 32-byte descriptor variant)
```
2) LAYOUT (96/80-byte files)
```
subtable header: 'DEFT' | u32 1 | u32 count(4 or 5) | u32 16 (record size)
then count * 16-byte records; file may contain further empty subtables
records are sorted by time (verified 17/17 files)
```
3) RECORD
```
w0 = f32 time A (seconds, low bits flags; mask 0xFFFFFFF0)
w1 = u32 event type/flags: observed 4 (x31), 7 (x17), 0x64FF16 (x17), 0x640016 (x17)
w2 = u32 sub-type: 0 or 1
w3 = f32 time B (seconds, low bits flags)
time pairs observed: 75.5->107.0, 163.9->195.4, 87.8->117.3, 152.9->181.4
```
4) FIXED CONTENT PER FILE
```
every 96/80-byte stage event file contains: one 0x64FF16 event, one 0x640016 event,
one type-7 event and one or more type-4 events (with time intervals).
0x64FF16 vs 0x640016 differ only in the middle byte (0xFF vs 0x00) -> packed flags.
```
5) OPEN
```
bit layout of the packed 0x64xxxx value, semantics of types 4 and 7, and the mapping to
danceEvent.c / danceEffect.c.
```

### 18.2138 *** FLW0 EVENT-FLOW SCRIPT SPEC v1 ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: FLW0 flow script spec, event nodes, MSG SEL MND.

1) WHAT IT IS (decoded from payload strings)
```
e102_010.bf payload strings (offset : string):
  +0x0000 FLW0
  +0x0068 e102_010_INIT     <- flow nodes, 56 bytes apart (0x38)
  +0x00A0 e102_010_START
  +0x00D8 e102_010_MAIN
  +0x0110 e102_010_END
  +0x0464 MSG1
  +0x0524 MND_102_010_01
  +0x0570 MSG_102_010_02
  +0x05BC MSG_102_010_03
  +0x0690 SEL_102_010_04
  +0x06E8 MSG_102_010_05
  +0x07A8 MSG_102_010_06
=> FLW0 is the EVENT FLOW (script) format of the communication/event system.
```
2) STRUCTURE
```
payload header: 7 u32 = {FLW0, 0, 5, 1, 0, 0, 0}  (0x1C bytes)
descriptor pairs at +0x1C: (0x38,4) (0x70,1) (0x38,varies) (0x150,2) (0x04,...)
node array: 4 nodes x 56 bytes starting at 0x68 (INIT, START, MAIN, END)
each node: 32-byte name field + 24-byte fields (structure open)
message/selection section: MSG*/SEL*/MND* named nodes
```
3) MEANING
```
the event system is a NODE-GRAPH script engine:
  INIT/START/MAIN/END = flow phases,
  MSG = text message node, SEL = selection node, MND = command node.
node names encode the event id (e102_010) plus the phase/type.
```
4) PARSER RULE
```
read .bf per 18.2132; payload = d[8:8+plen]; assert FLW0; then read descriptors and the
56-byte node array; strings are NUL-terminated ASCII at node start.
```
5) OPEN
```
24-byte field layout inside nodes, message/secondary node layouts, and linkage of node
names to the e1xx event tables.
```

4) PARSER PSEUDOCODE
```
def parseFLW0(buf):
  assert buf[8:12] in (b'FLW0', big-endian variants after swap)
  if not (native magic or flags&1): swap BE->LE at +2,+4,+0xC,+0x10,+0x14,+0x16,+0x18,
    +0x1A,+0x1C,+0x20 and indexed +0x24+r4/+0x28+r4/+0x2C+r4
  flags |= 1
  if element_count(+0x10)==0: return
  t = u32@+0x20; if t>4: abort invalid type
  if t in (0,1):
    stride=u32@+0x24; count=u32@+0x28; base=u32@+0x2C
    for i in range(count): swap_u32(base+i*stride+0x30); swap_u32(base+i*stride+0x34)
```

```
00        id length = 0
01        color map type = 1
01        image type = 1 (color-mapped)
00 00     cmap first index 0
01 20     cmap length 256, cmap entry depth 32
00 00 00 00  x/y origin = 0
w (u16 LE) h (u16 LE) at +12/+14
08        bpp 8 (palette index) for most, 32 for a few
00        descriptor
+18       256 * 4-byte palette entries (BGRA order)
dominant sizes: 256x256x8 (187), 512x32x8 (122), 1024x1024x8 (78), 512x512x8 (57)
```
4) DDS SPEC (measured, 981 files)
```
'DDS ' + u32 0x7C header size + flags 0x1007 + height@+12 + width@+16
fourcc at +84: 'DXT1' 751 files (76.6%), 'DXT5' 220 files (22.4%), zero 10
dominant dims: 512x256 (406), 256x256 (252), 128x64 (235), 128x128 (70)
=> GL mapping: DXT1 -> GL_COMPRESSED_RGB_S3TC_DXT1_EXT,
               DXT5 -> GL_COMPRESSED_RGBA_S3TC_DXT5_EXT (within GLES3 subset / extensions)

### 18.2213 *** S3TC COLOR INTERPOLATION DECODED (milestone) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: S3TC color interpolation, magic 0xAAAAAAAB, 6-bit LUT 0x812EDA14.

1) FUNCTION 0x8100E678 (decoded instruction by instruction)
```
r3 = 0x812ED994   -> 5-bit -> 8-bit expansion table (32 entries) for R and B
r4 = (c0 >> 11) & 0x1F ; table -> R0
r5 = (c1 >> 11) & 0x1F ; table -> R1
r4 = R1 + 2*R0                     <- DXT 3-color-mode weights (2:1)
r5 = 0xAAAAAAAB (=-0x55555555)     <- division-by-3 magic
umull hi = (r4 * 0xAAAAAAAB) >> 32 ; then >>1 -> exact /3
same for G (6 bits, table 0x812EDA14) and B (5 bits, table 0x812ED994)
finally: shifts by stack bytes [sp+0x24..0x27] then ORR -> pack target pixel
```
2) THE FORMER MYSTERY TABLE 0x812EDA14 IS SOLVED
```
0x812EDA14 = 6-bit -> 8-bit expansion LUT (64 entries, values 0..255,
step 4 with two +5 corrections = round(v*255/63)).
0x812ED994 = 5-bit -> 8-bit expansion LUT (32 entries).
```
3) ALGORITHM (implementable)
```
expand5(v) = (v<<3)|(v>>2)  ; expand6(v) = (v<<2)|(v>>4)
color2 = (2*C0 + C1) / 3 per channel  (DXT1 3-color mode)
output packing controlled by four shift-count bytes passed on the stack.
```
4) STATUS
```
S3TC color path: CONFIRMED at instruction level (tables + /3 magic + 2:1 weights).
Remaining: DXT5 alpha path and the 2-bit index selection loop.
```

### 18.2225 *** DXT DECODE SPEC v1 (color + alpha, implementable) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: DXT decode spec v1, S3TC pseudocode, color alpha functions.

1) CODE MAP
```
0x8100DF94  DDS header parse / format dispatch
~0x8100EAxx-0x8100EE18  pixel block loop (12 calls to color selector)
0x8100E70A  color select by 2-bit index (mode 0..3)
0x8100E674  2-color interpolator: (2*C0 + C1)/3 via magic 0xAAAAAAAB
0x812ED994  5-bit -> 8-bit expansion LUT (32 entries), = round(v*255/31)
0x812EDA14  6-bit -> 8-bit expansion LUT (64 entries), = round(v*255/63)
0x8100EE94  DXT5 alpha decode (float math, 255.0f / 7.0f / 5.0f)
index extraction: ands #3 (bits0-1), ubfx #2,#2 (bits2-3), #6,#2 (bits6-7)
pixel store stride: 4 bytes
```
2) COLOR ALGORITHM
```
C0 = u16 LE, C1 = u16 LE, 32-bit index word (2 bits per pixel)
rgb565 expansion: R = expand5(C>>11), G = expand6((C>>5)&0x3F), B = expand5(C&0x1F)
index 0 -> C0
index 1 -> C1
index 2 -> (C0 + C1)/2      (2-color mode when C0 <= C1: index 3 -> black)
index 3 -> (2*C0 + C1)/3    (4-color mode when C0 > C1)
weight implementation: sum = 2*A0 + A1; result = sum/(-0x55555555 magic) = sum/3
output packing: channels shifted by four stack-passed shift counts, then ORR
```
3) ALPHA ALGORITHM (DXT5)
```
alpha0 = block byte 0, alpha1 = block byte 1; a0 = alpha0/255.0, a1 = alpha1/255.0
index 0 -> a0 | index 1 -> a1 | index 6 -> 0.0 | index 7 -> 1.0
if alpha0 > alpha1 (8-alpha mode): alpha = ((7-i)*a0 + i*a1)/7 , i = index-1
else (6-alpha mode):               alpha = ((5-i)*a0 + i*a1)/5 , i = index-1
implementation uses vcvt/vmul/vmla/vdiv floats (0x437F = 255.0f, 7.0f, 5.0f)
```
4) BLOCK LAYOUT (measured against DDS population)
```
DDS: 'DDS ' + 0x7C header; fourcc at +84; DXT1 751 files, DXT5 220 files
DXT1 block = 8 bytes (c0,c1,indices), DXT5 block = 16 bytes (a0,a1,alpha-idx,c0,c1,idx)
dominant sizes: 512x256 (406), 256x256 (252), 128x64 (235), 128x128 (70)
```
5) STATUS
```
DXT1/DXT5 decode = CONFIRMED at instruction level for both color and alpha paths.
Both LUT formulas verified exactly against the binary tables.
```

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: TGA spec v1, palette, header 18 bytes, validator rules.

1) POPULATION (data_extracted)
```
538 .tga files; dominant 8bpp palette: 256x256 (187), 512x32 (122), 1024x1024 (78),
512x512 (57), 16x16 (19), 256x32 (18), 2048x2048 (13), 128x128 (9), 64x64 (6);
a few 128x128x32 true-colour files.
```
2) HEADER (18 bytes, verified by both data and code)
```
+0x00 u8  id length = 0 (validator requires 0)
+0x01 u8  color map type (1 = palette present)
+0x02 u8  image type (1 = colour-mapped)
+0x03 u16 cmap first index
+0x05 u16 cmap length (<=16 when bpp=4, <=256 when bpp=8)
+0x07 u8  cmap entry depth (must be 0 when no palette)
+0x08 u16 x origin | +0x0A u16 y origin
+0x0C u16 width | +0x0E u16 height
+0x10 u8  bits per pixel (multiple of 4, <=32)
+0x11 u8  image descriptor
+0x12     palette: 256 entries x 4 bytes (BGRA)
```
3) CODE (appImageTGA.c)
```
0x810122CC  header validator (rules in 18.2227), returns 1/0
            callers: 0x81012312/376/3DC/41C/45E/26C8
0x81012366  header field writer (width@+0xC height@+0xE bpp@+0x10 desc@+0x11)
0x81012606  image buffer creator: size = w*h*(bpp>>3) + 0x2C; memset(buf,0,0x12)
            bpp==8 palette branch; tracked allocator; source line 0x10A
```
4) DECODE RULES (for the port)
```
1. read 18-byte header; require idlen==0, bpp%4==0, bpp<=32
2. if palette: skip id bytes, read cmap_length entries of (cmap_depth/8) bytes
3. pixel data: width*height indices (8bpp) or BGRA pixels (32bpp)
4. expand palette entries to RGBA8 (B,G,R,A order as stored)
```
5) STATUS
```
header layout, validator rules, size formula and palette path are confirmed from code + data.
OPEN: the exact palette expansion loop (0x810126C8 area) and the read-direction entry.
```

### 18.2235 *** GNF SOLVED: 8-BIT ALPHA TEXTURES (A8) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: GNF solved, A8 alpha texture, soft glow, 248-byte header.

1) EVIDENCE (histogram, decisive)
```
circle_01.gnf   : 248-byte header + 8 + 65536 bytes = 256x256x1 ; 233 distinct byte values
                  top: 255 (22049), 0 (9071), 170 (4501), 192 (2728), 32 (1625), ...
                  row0 mean 124.5 ; row128 mean 138.4 (brighter centre = radial glow)
complete_01.gnf : 248 + 8 + 32768 = 512x64x1 ; 251 distinct values
star_01.gnf     : 248 + 8 + 4096  = 64x64x1   ; 94 distinct values
a palette index texture would have very few distinct values; 94..251 values means
8-bit data, and the byte count equals W*H exactly => 8 bits per pixel.
```
2) FORMAT
```
+0x000 'GNF ' magic
+0x004 u32 header size = 248 (0xF8)
+0x00C u32 file size
+0x018 u32 size/dim bitfield: width = (v & 0x3FF) + 1,
        height = (((v >> 16) & 0x3FF) + 1) * 4   (verified for all three files)
+0x02C u32 texture data size (power of two: 65536 / 32768 / 4096)
+0x100 pixel data: W*H bytes, 8-bit alpha, 1 byte per pixel
```
3) USE IN ENGINE
```
three soft-glow sprites: star (64x64), circle (256x256), complete (512x64 band)
port: upload as GL_R8 / GL_ALPHA texture and use for additive glow sprites.
```

### 18.2242 *** ENV/EPL SPEC v1 (GFS0 stage environment/field params) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: env epl spec v1, GFS0 kind 0x5100 0x5030, float params.

1) FORMAT IDENTITY
```
both .env (36 files) and .epl (51 files) start with 'GFS0' -> they belong to the GFS0 family
header (16 bytes): 'GFS0' | u16 ver = 0x0110 | u16 kind | u32 f8 | u32 f12 (=0)
  .env kind = 0x5100 ; f8 = 4
  .epl kind = 0x5030 or 0x5070 ; f8 = 1
names: dance/env/f{track}_{nnn}.ENV and dance/field/f{track}_{nnn}.EPL
```
2) PAYLOADS (exact)
```
.ENV size 808 = 16 header + u16 0x0101 + 197 * f32 BE + u16 0x0002
  sample floats: 0.4706 (repeated), 1.0, 0.9882, then -0.05, 0.2, 1.0, 2.0, 3.004
.EPL size 588 = 16 header + 143 * f32 BE
  sample tail: ..., 1.4667, ...
=> both are big-endian float parameter tables; earlier 'mixed types' reading was a
   2-byte misalignment (floats start at +18 for ENV, +16 for EPL)
```
3) ROLE
```
.ENV = stage environment parameters (lighting/colour/intensity values)
.EPL = stage field/layout parameters (positions etc.)
paired with the DSFT stage-format tables: DSFT (format) + ENV (environment) + EPL (field)
```
4) PARSING RULE
```
assert magic 'GFS0'; ver=BE16@+4; kind=BE16@+6;
ENV: floats = BE32 array at +18, count=197, trailer BE16 at +806
EPL: floats = BE32 array at +16, count=143
```
5) OPEN
```
per-field semantics (which float is which lighting/field parameter) and the mapping track->stage id.
```

### 18.2248 *** CORRECTION + EPL SPEC v2: PARTICLE/EFFECT BLOCKS ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: EPL correction, particle effect blocks, P-SMOKE0 O-SPARK0.

1) RETRACTION of 18.2242/18.2240 for .EPL
```
18.2240/18.2242 described .EPL as '143 big-endian floats'. That is WRONG for most files.
The payload is a list of named sub-blocks; reading it as a float array just produces
garbage for the block area. The float reading only matches the leading zero/float region.
```
2) MEASURED (sub-block area starts at a fixed offset 131 in every .EPL examined)
```
offsets 124..131: 08 00 00 00 05 00 08   (block-area prologue)
at offset 131: ASCII block name (8 chars):
  'P-SMOKE0'  smoke particle block
  'O-SPARK0'  spark particle block
  'E-FILL0'   fill/other effect block
  'DXT1'      embedded texture marker
then 4-byte hash (e.g. 16 BF F7 28 / 46 FF 45 DE) and u32 counts (1 / 10 / 2 / 2 ...)
examples: e116_001.EPL (263524 B) P-SMOKE0 ; e151_002.EPL (34466 B) O-SPARK0
          e190_001.EPL (679501 B) O-SPARK0 ; e205_001.EPL (66423 B) P-SMOKE0
```
3) .EPL = STAGE EFFECT/PARTICLE DEFINITIONS
```
directory dance/field/ ; one EPL per track (e1xx naming) ; GFS0 header (kind 0x5030/0x5070)
=> EPL is the stage particle/effect configuration, not a float parameter table.
```
4) WHAT REMAINS TRUE FROM 18.2242
```
.ENV (36 files) = GFS0 container kind 0x5100, payload = u16 0x0101 + 197 BE floats
  (colour components 0.47..0.67 observed) -> stage lighting/environment parameters.
.EPL header = GFS0 + 16 bytes, same as ENV; sizes 588..679501 vary by content.
```

### 18.2263 FNT0 OFFSET UNIT CALIBRATION (CONTRADICTION FOUND)

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: FNT0 offset unit contradiction, 65376 max, retraction.

1) MEASURED (font_staff.fnt)
```
slot table at 0x18, 274 slots, 4 bytes each
data area starts at 0x460, size 27056 bytes
non-empty positive slot second-fields: 190
min second-field = 2 ; max second-field = 65376
```
2) UNIT TEST ALL FAIL
```
if second field were a byte offset   : max 65376 > 27056  -> impossible
if half-byte (nibble) : 65376/2 = 32688 > 27056 -> impossible
if 4-bit unit         : same as nibble -> impossible
if bit unit           : 65376 still > 27056*8? no (27056*8=216448) BUT then 190 glyphs
would span only 65376 bits = 8172 bytes, leaving most of the data area unused, and
the ascending deltas (1164..1664) become 145..208 bytes which is not a 32x32 1bpp glyph.
=> the second field is NOT a simple offset from the data-area start.
```
3) PARTIAL RETRACTION of 18.2262
```
KEEP: 0xFFFF is the empty-slot sentinel (60 slots in staff font).
KEEP: the last 12 slots have ascending second fields (28099..43913).
RETRACT: 'second field = glyph data offset' as a general statement.
```

```
a) the second field is an absolute file offset or an offset with a different base
b) the pair is (u16 something, u16 packed size/char data), not an offset

### 18.2266 FNT0 FONT STATUS v1 (structure + proven facts + open list)

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: FNT0 status v1, three layers, slot sentinel, index groups.

1) FILES AND HEADER
```
c_font_p5.fnt 1167652 B, font_p5.fnt 1245122 B, font_staff.fnt 28176 B
magic 'FNT0' (big-endian word 0x464E5430 never found in eboot, so parser is not a constant match)
header 24 bytes: +4 version 0x00000100, +8 u16 width 32, +10 u16 height 32,
                 +0x10 u32 slot-table offset 0x18, +0x14 u32 slot count (772/772/274)
```
2) SLOT TABLE (4 bytes per slot: u16 a, u16 b)
```
0xFFFF in field b = empty slot (60 in font_staff, 50 with b=0)
font_staff: 274 slots, 213 non-empty, 190 with positive b, b min=2 max=65376
last 12 slots of staff have ascending b (28099..43913)
b as byte/half-byte offset fails (65376 > data area 27056)
```
3) DATA AREA
```
starts at slot_table_offset + 4*slot_count (staff 0x460, p5 0xC28)
staff: begins with grouped records (u16 kind, u16 value): kind 1 (14 entries, ascending to
       64685), then kind 2 entries (516, 1992, 3790, 5359 ...), kinds increasing
p5   : begins with a different sequence (LE u16 322, 385, 143, 323, 386, 250 ...)
data sizes: staff 27056 B, p5 ~1.16/1.24 MB
```
4) FONT_ROLE
```
FNT0 = 32x32 bitmap font; font_staff = staff-roll names (274 glyphs), p5 = main UI font (772).
```
5) OPEN (honest)
```
exact meaning of slot fields a/b, the grouped-record semantics in the data area,
the glyph bitmap encoding (1bpp? variable width?) and the code-side loader (no magic in eboot).
```

### 18.2286 FNT0 BITPACKED STREAM HYPOTHESIS CHECK

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: FNT0 bitpacked streams, bit offsets, file bit capacity.

1) KEY CHECK
```
font_staff.fnt size = 28176 bytes = 225408 bits
observed second-field values: min 2, max 65376
65376 < 225408  => the values fit inside the FILE's bit space
(they do NOT fit the data area in bytes, which failed earlier)
data area starts at 0x460 = 1120 bytes = 8960 bits
=> the values are most plausibly BIT offsets measured from the file start
   (or from a fixed base inside the file)
```
2) SUPPORTING EVIDENCE
```
a) hmHuffman_utility.c decodes a BITSTREAM (0x81024D68): shifts by 1 bit per node,
   loads 32-bit words (|0x10000), walks a 6-byte-node table
b) FNT0 slot data is variable length and not byte aligned
c) data area head shows grouped pairs (u16 k, u16 v) with increasing v
=> FNT0 glyph data = Huffman bitstreams addressed by BIT OFFSETS
```
3) NEXT CONCRETE STEPS
```
1. verify that a second-field value, when doubled/used as bit index, lands on valid
   stream data (inspect bits at 2*value for several slots)
2. locate the Huffman node table in the file (needed by 0x81024D68 context [r3+8])
3. decode one glyph and render 32x32 to confirm
```

### 18.2304 *** FNT0 DECODE SPEC v3 (complete mechanism) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: FNT0 spec v3, glyph decode mechanism, metrics plus bitmap.

1) FILE STRUCTURE
```
+0x00 'FNT0' magic (checked bytewise by 0x810246D4)
+0x04 u32 version 0x00010000
+0x08 u16 width 32 ; +0x0A u16 height 32
+0x0C reserved (non-zero in c_font_p5)
+0x10 u32 slot table offset (0x18)
+0x14 u32 descriptor offset (staff 274, p5 772)
slot table @+0x10: 4 bytes/slot = {u16 a flags+width, u16 b}; 0xFFFF = empty
descriptor @+0x14: A@+0, B@+4, C@+0x18 (A=32 constant)
  p0 = descriptor + A          first data region
  p1 = descriptor + A + B      per-slot offset table (u32, increasing,
                               0xFFFFFFFF-terminated in font_staff: 162 entries)
  p2 = descriptor + A + B + C  symbol/pad region (0xFF padding)
```
2) RUNTIME OBJECT (loader 0x810246FC)
```
obj+0x00 = file base
obj+0x04 = file+8 (width/height pointer)
obj+0x08 = file + [file+0x10] -> slot table
obj+0x0C = file + [file+0x14] -> descriptor (huffman context)
obj+0x10 = obj+0x18 (decode buffer)
obj+0x14 = u16 cached last character code
alloc = width*height + 0x1E, zeroed
```
3) GLYPH DECODE (two accessors)
```
0x81020D06 : character code -> slot index (UTF-16 high byte branch)
0x81024864 : metrics accessor
   uxth(code) -> slot index -> 0x81024D4A (build 3 pointers) -> 0x81024D68 decode
   copies 6 bytes: 4 unsigned + 2 signed (width/height/advance/xoff/yoff)
0x8102490C : bitmap accessor
   same lookup, decodes, then returns decode_buffer + 6
=> ONE Huffman decode per glyph yields: [0..5] metrics, [6..] bitmap data
```
4) HUFFMAN UTILITY (hmHuffman_utility.c)
```
0x81024D4A : context builder: ctx+0=A, ctx+4=B, ctx+0x18=C ->
              out0=ctx+A, out1=ctx+A+B, out2=ctx+A+B+C
0x81024D68 : bit loop: read 1 bit, walk 6-byte nodes, leaf byte at node+4,
              reload 32-bit words with |0x10000, count output bytes in 0x8154AC0
```
5) STATUS
```
机制完整: header / slot table / descriptor / offset table / decode buffer /
          metrics + bitmap in one decode / character map / huffman utility
OPEN: bitmap pixel encoding (bpp) and final draw call; p1 unit calibration.
```

2) SLOT TABLE (SJIS character -> glyph info)
```
area between 0x18 and the descriptor offset
  font_p5 / c_font_p5: 0x18..0x304 = 748 bytes = 187 slots exactly
  font_staff        : 0x18..0x112 = 250 bytes (62.5 slots => 2-byte header + 62 slots,
                      OR staff uses a different slot size; OPEN)
slot = {u16 code, u16 info}: p5 code max 64513 = 0xFC01 (Shift-JIS range),
info small (advance/glyph index candidate), 0xFFFF = empty (20 slots in p5)
character encoding = Shift-JIS: 0x81020D06 branches on the high byte and uses
range constants 0x1F/0x81/0x1C/0xE0 (SJIS lead-byte ranges); ASCII path when high byte 0
```
3) DESCRIPTOR (32 bytes at [file+0x14])
```
+0x00 A=32            descriptor size
+0x04 B               p0 size (staff 528 / p5 3072; 6-byte records = ramp table)
+0x08 p2 size (bytes) verified == actual p2 region
+0x0C p2 size (bits)
+0x10 maxlen = 1030 
+0x14 entries        staff 159 / p5 3887 (verified == p1 entry count)
+0x18 C = entries*4  verified (p1 table byte size)
+0x1C total bitstream size
p0 = desc+A ; p1 = desc+A+B ; p2 = desc+A+B+C
```
4) REGIONS
```
p0: 6-byte records {u16 index, u16 pad, u16 value}: ramp table (staff step -17, p5 step -1)
p1: u32 bit-offset table relative to p2 (verified: p2 bits 213648 vs p1 max 213637, diff 11)

decode: slot info -> p1[i]..p1[i+1] bits of p2 -> huffman -> 6-byte metrics + bitmap
```

```

### 18.2319 *** FNT0 SPEC v6 (huffman tree solved; decoder algorithm) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: FNT0 spec v6, huffman alphabet, decoder algorithm.

1) HUFFMAN TREE (p0, 6 bytes per node)
```
node = {u16 childA, u16 flag, u8 symbol, u8 pad}
  flag == 0  -> leaf, output byte symbol (node+4)
  flag != 0  -> internal, field childA/flag used for descent indexing
font_p5   : 512 nodes = 256 leaves (symbols 255..0, full byte alphabet) + 256 internal
font_staff:  88 nodes =  44 leaves (symbols 255,238,221,... step -17 mod 256) + 44 internal
=> staff uses a 44-level quantised alphabet (lower quality); p5 uses all 256 byte values
```
2) DECODE ALGORITHM (from 0x81024D68)
```
inputs: p0 = node table, p1 = u32 offset table, p2 = bitstream, i = glyph index
start_bit = p1[i]; end_bit = p1[i+1]
window    = u16 at p2 + (start_bit>>3)   (bit offset -> byte offset = bit>>3)
loop until running bit count reaches (end_bit-start_bit):
  bit  = window & 1 ; window >>= 1
  node = p0 + node_index*6 ; node_index updates from the node fields
  if node.flag == 0: emit node.symbol ; continue
  when the 32-bit window is exhausted: reload next u16 with |0x10000
output bytes = 6-byte metrics followed by bitmap data (same buffer)
```
3) BITMAP
```
bitmap bytes follow the 6 metrics bytes in the decoded buffer; returned pointer = buffer+6
bpp still open (expected 1 or 2 bits per pixel for a 32x32 glyph)
```
4) STATUS
```
CONFIRMED: header / descriptor / p0 tree / p1 offsets / p2 bitstream / metrics+bitmap decode
OPEN: staff slot layout, bitmap bpp, draw call, and the exact node-descent field usage.
```

### 18.2324 *** FNT0 SOLVED: FULL DECODE PROVEN (maxlen match, 8bpp glyphs) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: FNT0 solved full decode, 8bpp glyph, 1030 bytes, maxlen.

1) PROOF (python decode of glyph #0, font_staff)
```
p1[0]=0, p1[1]=1074 bits; p0 nodes at file+0x132; p1 at +0x342; p2 at +0x5BE
decoder: win=u16[p2|start>>3]|0x10000; win>>=(start&0xF); pair=p0+2;
         bit=win&1; child=u16[pair+bit*2]; node=p0+6*child;
         if u16[node+2]==0: emit byte[node+4]; pair=p0+2 else pair=node+2;
         win>>=1; if win==1: p2+=2; win=u16[p2]|0x10000
result: 1074 steps -> 1030 bytes
  first 6 bytes (metrics): 13 4 7 1 0 2
  remaining 1024 bytes: 32x32 = 1024 pixels at 8 bits per pixel
  all ones count = 0 => glyph #0 is a blank/space glyph
MAGNITUDE MATCHES: 1030 == descriptor maxlen field; 6+1024 == record size
```
2) WHY 1074 BITS GIVE 1030 BYTES
```
root bit 1 -> node 44 -> leaf symbol 0 in ONE bit (node44 = (44,0,0))
a blank glyph is 1024 zero bytes = 1024 one-bit codes + metrics => ~1074 bits
=> the 'bit budget contradiction' is resolved: zero is a 1-bit code
```
3) FINAL FNT0 FORMAT (complete)
```
header 24B: magic/version/32x32/slot offset/descriptor offset
slot table: {u16 Shift-JIS code, u16 glyph info}; 0xFFFF = empty
descriptor 32B: A=32, B=p0 size, p2 bytes, p2 bits, maxlen=1030, entries, C=entries*4, total
p0 = huffman node table: {u16 self, u16 childA, u16 childB}; leaf = childA==0, symbol at +4
     p5: 512 nodes / 256 leaves (byte alphabet); staff: 88 nodes / 44 leaves (step -17)
p1 = u32 per-glyph BIT offset table relative to p2 (0xFFFFFFFF terminated in staff)
p2 = huffman bitstream: per glyph record = 6-byte metrics + 1024-byte 8bpp bitmap
metrics order [advance?, width, height, xoff, yoff, ?] - glyph0 = 13,4,7,1,0,2
```
4) STATUS
```
FNT0 = SOLVED at format+decoder level. Remaining minor: metrics field order,
staff slot layout, draw call.
```

loop nbits = end-start:
  child = u16[pair + (win&1)*2]
  node  = p0 + 6*child
  if u16[node+2]==0: emit byte[node+4]; pair=p0+2
  else: pair=node+2
  win >>= 1; if win==1: advance p2 by 2; win=u16[p2]|0x10000
record = 6-byte metrics + width*height bytes of 8bpp alpha
```
3) VALIDATION
```
font_staff: glyph0 blank; glyph1/2/5 render recognizable kana strokes
font_p5   : worst-case 256-symbol alphabet also decodes correctly
all glyph records = 1030 bytes = descriptor maxlen (6 + 32*32)
```

### 18.2337 *** FNT0 DELIVERY SPEC v7 (format + algorithm + APIs + tool) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: FNT0 delivery v7, APIs, reference tool, final spec.

1) FILE FORMAT
```
header 24B: magic F/N/T/0 (bytewise), version 0x00010000, width=32, height=32,
            slot table offset (0x18), descriptor offset
slot table: {u16 Shift-JIS code, u16 glyph info}; 0xFFFF empty
descriptor 32B at [file+0x14]: A=32, B=p0 size, p2 bytes, p2 bits, maxlen=1030,
            entries (staff 159, p5 3887), C=entries*4, total bits
p0 = descriptor + A              huffman node table (6B/node)
p1 = descriptor + A + B          u32 per-glyph BIT offsets (relative to p2)
p2 = descriptor + A + B + C      huffman bitstream
```
2) HUFFMAN + RECORD
```
node: {u16 self, u16 childA, u16 childB}; leaf: childA==0, symbol at +4
      p5 512 nodes/256 leaves (byte alphabet); staff 88/44 leaves (symbols step -17)
record: 6-byte metrics + width*height (1024) bytes of 8bpp alpha = 1030 bytes = maxlen
metrics: [u8,u8,u8,u8, i8 xoff, i8 yoff] (signedness confirmed at 0x81020508)
```
3) CODE / APIs
```
0x810246D4 isFNT0  | 0x810246FC loader (alloc w*h+0x1E, fills font object)
0x81020D06 char->slot (Shift-JIS ranges 0x1F/0x81/0x1C/0xE0)
0x81024864 metrics decode | 0x8102490C bitmap decode
0x81024D4A huffman context builder | 0x81024D68 huffman decode loop
0x81020508 getGlyphMetrics (copies 6 bytes) | 0x810205B4 getGlyphBitmap (returns ptr)
font module sources: appFontCoding.c / appFontSystem.c / data_table_v1/v2 / hmHuffman_utility.c
```
4) REFERENCE TOOL
```
tools/fnt0_decode.py - parses header/descriptor, walks the huffman bitstream,
decodes glyph records. Verified on font_staff (32x32, 159 entries, maxlen 1030).
```

### 18.2343 *** FNT0 FINAL SPEC v8 (format + decode + render layer) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: FNT0 v8 final, render layer, mode dispatch, width table.

1) FORMAT (proven by decoder)
```
header 24B, SJIS slot table, descriptor 32B, p0 huffman nodes, p1 bit offsets, p2 bitstream
record = 6-byte metrics + 1024-byte 8bpp bitmap (=1030 = maxlen)
```
2) RENDER LAYER (code)
```
0x810204A2  getGlyphInfo(obj, char, mode, out) - 4-way dispatch on obj+0:
  mode 0 -> returns 0 (empty)
  mode 1 -> static width table path: calls 0x81023910 (font data table v1)
            v1 object: +0 header ptr, +4 table size, +0xC table ptr; header+0x16 = valid flag
            table = u16 entries indexed by (SJIS code & 0x7FFF); entry byte[1] sign-extended = width
            writes out[0] and out[2] only (other 4 bytes zeroed)
  mode 2 -> FNT0 huffman metrics (0x81020508 -> 0x81024864)
  mode 3 -> FNT0 huffman bitmap  (0x810205B4 -> 0x8102490C)
=> layout uses mode1 (fast width) or mode2 (full metrics); rendering uses mode3 (bitmap)
```

[0] width-class (set by static table path)  [2] glyph width (set by static table path)

### 18.2347 *** FNT0 SLOT LAYOUT SOLVED (SJIS lead-byte grouping, 62 slots) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: FNT0 slot layout solved, SJIS lead byte, 62 slots, range table.

1) RANGE TABLE (reconstructed from 0x81020D06 stack init and loop)
```
stack table at sp+2: (1,0) then (0x1F,0x81) then (0x1C,0xE0)
 loop walks 3 entries; base accumulates len: 0 -> 1 -> 0x20
 match: high = (char>>8) & 0xFF in [ip, ip+len)
 index = base + (high - ip)
=> SJIS lead byte -> slot index:
   high 0x81..0x9F -> slot 1..31
   high 0xE0..0xFB -> slot 32..59
   high == 0 (ASCII) -> separate ASCII path (no high byte)
max index 59 <= assert limit 0x3D(61); slot table has 62 entries
```
2) SLOT ENTRY
```
slot = u32 read as [slotbase + index*4]
  low16  = offset from slot-table base (r4 = base + low16)
  high16 = nonzero flag/count (0 => invalid glyph)
  data pointer = base + low16 ; then u16 [ptr+0xF4] is read
0xFFFF fillers = empty slots (observed 60 in the 62-slot staff table)
```
3) IMPLICATIONS
```
staff font = 62-slot SJIS-grouped table (31 half-width + 28 double-byte groups)
the 159 glyph records are addressed indirectly through slot offsets
p5 font has 187 slots (different variant; its char->slot path not yet traced)
```
4) FNT0 STATUS: COMPLETE
```
format / huffman / record / 8bpp bitmap / render modes / slot layout ALL SOLVED.
remaining: GPU upload path, text-layout caller, p5 slot variant (non-blocking).
```

### 18.2396 *** GFS0 BIG-ENDIAN CONFIRMED + POSE CHUNK PARSER (Form C breakthrough) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: GFS0 big endian, pose chunk parser 0x811AA58C, kind family.

1) .GAP IS GFS0 WITH KIND 0x01105090 (data-level)
```
sample pc111340_p34.GAP head: 47 46 53 30 'GFS0' 01 10 50 90 (BE kind)
all 6,972 .GAP files share this header family; they are pose/animation containers,
not audio (retract the earlier 'GAP audio' wording; no lowercase .gap files exist).
```
2) STREAM READERS DO BE->HOST CONVERSION (code-level)
```
0x811DF23A read_u8  : read 1 byte via 0x811DE912, return byte
0x811DF13C read_f32 : read 4 bytes, byte-reverse (lsrs #0x18 + bfi #0x18,#8), return float
0x811DF182 read_u32 : read 4 bytes, same byte-reverse, return u32
underlying reader: 0x811DE912(stream, dst, count)
=> GFS0 payloads are BIG-ENDIAN on disk; all multi-byte reads are swapped centrally.
```
3) GENERIC GFS0 CHUNK PARSER 0x811AA58C (27 kinds)
```
entry: push {r4-r8,sb,sl,fp,lr}; vpush {s16,s17}; readers on r0=stream, r1=out struct
kinds dispatched by comparing [stream+4] (chunk kind) against movw/movt constants:
  0x01103050 0x01103FFF 0x01104010 0x01104020 0x01104030 0x01104090
  0x01104120 0x01104130 0x01104140 0x01104150 0x01104240 0x01104250
  0x01104960 0x01104970 0x01105010 0x01105020 0x01105030 0x01105040
  0x01105050 0x01105070 0x01105090
.GAP = 0x01105090 ; EPL effect blocks = 0x01105030 / 0x01105070 (family consistent)
out-struct offsets written: +0x00, +0x218(f32), +0x21C(16 bytes), +0x22C..+0x233(bytes),
  +0x238(u32), +0x23C(f32), +0x240(f32), +0x244(f32), +0x248(f32), +0x2A8(f32), +0x32C(u32)
branches: kind<=0x01105090 -> +0x233 ; >0x01105090 -> compare 0x01105070 etc.
```
4) LOAD PATH (code-level)
```
dance/persona path templates at 0x812F0BB4 / 0x812FA528.. (pc%03d_%03d.GAP variants)
0x810409E0 persona path formatter (snprintf 0x812B2280) callers: 0x81046264
0x8104159A generic resource load wrapper -> 0x81047960(file open) + 0x8103B6EA(slot register)
0x8103B6EA registers 8-slots (slot stride 0xC, bitmask +0x84) -> 0x810479D8 real load/parse
0x810479D8 resource cache lookup: entries stride 0x34, fields +0x14 id, +0x1C path, +0x20 hash
```

### 18.2427 *** GAP POSE FORMAT SPEC v1 (SOLVED: header + times + TRS keys) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: GAP pose spec v1, TRS keys, quaternion translation, implementable.

1) CONTAINER
```
.GAP = GFS0 big-endian container, kind 0x01105090 (pose/animation)
file header 32 B: 'GFS0' | kind | 1 | 0 | kind | 0x000100FD | payload_size | 0
then a flat list of node records until EOF:
  node = { u16 type, u16 name_len, char name[name_len] , body }
types seen: 88 skirt_root, 118 R_S_skirt_00, 119 R_S_skirt_01
```
2) NODE BODY HEADER (20 B, 8/8 files identical layout)
```
+0x00 u32 id (skirt_root 0x7D79FA33 ; R_S_skirt_00 0xBC612854 ; R_S_skirt_01 0xCB6618C2)
+0x04 u32 version = 1
+0x08 u32 F1 = 28 (all nodes) [OPEN: track count or flags]
+0x0C u32 kf = keyframe count (631..5281 samples)
+0x10 u32 0
```
3) TIMES
```
+0x14 f32 times[kf-1] : strictly increasing, 30 fps grid (value = frame/30)
t0 = 0 implicit; stored t1..t(kf-1)
VERIFIED: first non-monotonic float occurs exactly at index kf-1 in 8/8 files
note: node type 118 shows a 2-byte extra pad before keys (data-driven shift 2606)
```
4) KEYS (per keyframe TRS)
```
start = body + 0x14 + 4*(kf-1) (+2 pad for the type-118 variant)
record = 14 bytes = 7 big-endian halves:
   half4 quaternion (w,x,y,z)   |q| = 1
   half3 translation (tx,ty,tz)
VALIDATION: 3,200/3,200 records |q| within 1+-0.02 (100%) across 8 files;
            mean tz = 0.998..0.999 (skirt root height ~1.0 m)
record count = kf per node (node1/node2 both 100/100 at kf-1 shift +/- variant)
```
5) IMPLEMENTATION NOTES (native PC engine)
```
1. read file, verify 'GFS0' + kind 0x01105090, note big-endian
2. skip 32-byte header; loop: read {u16 type,u16 len,name}; read body header
3. read kf-1 BE f32 times, insert t0=0
4. read kf records of 7 BE halves; convert halves to float
5. quaternion -> rotation matrix (w,x,y,z), translation applied per node
6. node type selects parent/hierarchy role; name matches skeleton node by name
```
6) REMAINING OPEN
```
F1=28 meaning; node-type-118 exact pad rule; per-file node hierarchy order;
connection to runtime pose evaluation (apply to skeleton) is next.
```

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: ver3 raw stream, three independent half curves, alignment
checked, Euler angle unit hypothesis, quantized rotation values, skirt_root coincidence.

1) RAW-STREAM VERIFICATION (eliminates the alignment-artifact concern)
All nine below are decoded directly from the file bytes at the parser-reported key offset.

  keys: 3c00 3a87 3632 | 3bdf 3a74 3638 | 3bc7 3a60 3638 | 3bb4 3a48 3638 ...
  -> (1.00000,0.81592,0.38721) (0.98389,0.80664,0.38867) (0.97217,0.79688,0.38867) ...

  -> (0.99951,0,0) repeated

  -> (0.99951,0.99951,0) repeated

pc111_002_p.GAP  RightShoulder kf=5: 3bff 3bff 3bff ...      -> (0.99951,0.99951,0.99951)

  3bff 048a 91c8 | 3bfe 0000 85f7 ... -> (0.99902,0,0) ...

```
=> The 6-byte record is THREE INDEPENDENT half channels, byte-exact, no hidden padding.
   The pad search in the parser lands on the same stream; shifting by +-2 bytes only rotates
   channels (verified above), so there is NO separate sub-format producing "(1,0,0)" or
   "(1,1,1)" patterns: those patterns are simply STATIC triples of the same 3 curves.

2) WHY "UNIT" AND "ALL-1" CLASSES APPEARED (measurement artifact, retracted reading)
Full-chain ver3 records = 3,961,905. Per-node classification by dominant row pattern:
```
unit-dominant (|row|~1) nodes  : e.g. tail_01 91.4% unit, tail_03 97.7%, RightForeArm 99.8%
all-1-dominant rows            : R_S_hair_00 98.2%, R_F_hair_00 98.8%, R_collar_00 43.4%
neither                        : root, L_B_collar_00, R_S_ShirtsCollar_00
```
These are NOT different data layouts: they are static/animated values of the same 3 curves
(Spine1=(1,0,0), neck=(1,1,0), RightShoulder=(1,1,1), root=(1.0,0.816,0.387) all decoded from
identical 6-byte records of the same file). Any future reader must not model them as
separate record types.

3) SKIRT_ROOT COINCIDENCE (recorded so it is not re-invented)
skirt_root ver3 (0.99902,0,0) happens to look like the first 3 halves of the ver1 14-byte
record (0.99854,0,0,0.00227,...). This does NOT generalize: the 14-byte h[0:4] was validated
as a unit quaternion (|q|=1 on 55,463 records), while ver3 rows such as
(0.99951,0.99951,0.99951) have norm 1.73 and (1.0,0.81592,0.38721) norm 1.35, which cannot be
quaternion components. The visual match is a coincidence of near-identity orientations.

4) HYPOTHESIS (explicitly UNCONFIRMED, do not implement as fact)
The measured value domain is [-0.99, 2.00] with a large mass exactly at 1.0, 0.5 and 0.6875.
0.5 and 1.0 are exact half representation of 90 and 180 in the unit "half-turns"; 0.6875 = 123.75
degrees. Together with smooth per-channel curves this is consistent with
  【推测】ver3 record = 3 Euler angles expressed in HALF-TURNS (angle/180 degrees), half precision.
Verification methods (in order):
  (a) code side: find the consumer of (ver=3,F1=31) and read the conversion constant
      (a 180/pi or pi/180 or 0.5 multiplier would settle it);
  (b) data side: for a dynamic ver3 track, check whether the reconstructed orientation
      (apply the 3 angles in the node's rotation order) makes the child bone reach its
      animated target position in a static export comparison;
  (c) distribution test: angle-in-half-turns should never exceed 2.0 in absolute value on
      animated tracks; a confirmed counterexample would refute the hypothesis.

NEXT node. The immediate next node is R_C_sleeve_00 at 0x135BD. Likewise the earlier phrase

   pc201_002_27.GAP, walked header to header with zero gaps)

       + (kf-1) x BE f32 times

5) WHY THE PARSER NEEDED A PAD SEARCH (root cause now explained)
The historical pad values (0/2/4/6/8) in gap_pose_decode came from the 28-byte trailer being
mistaken for key data / wrong node boundaries. The trailer is NOT part of the key array.
NEXT PARSER STEP (v16): chain as kend = tstart + 4*(kf-1) + recsize*kf + 28 and validate the
next header at exactly kend; keep resync only as fallback. This should remove pad ambiguity.

Spine keys=0x54D9 kf=2). Hips keys end = 0x26D0 ; next header (Spine) at 0x54B8 ;

### 18.2506 *** VER3 CONTAINER LAYOUT SOLVED: 32B HEAD + (N+1) TIMES + (N+1) QUAT4h + 68B TAIL ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: ver3 container layout solved, 32-byte head, quaternion track,
30fps time array, 68-byte tail, N=frame count, unit quaternion validated, channel pair.

1) THE FORMULA (MEASURED, exact on every inspected node)
```
container_size = 32 + 12*(N+1) + 68
layout:
  +0    8 x u32 = {f32 a, f32 b, f32 c, u32 0, u32 0, u32 0, u32 0x20, u32 N}
  +32   (N+1) x BE f32   30 fps time array (first = 0.000000, second = 0.033333)
  +32+4*(N+1)  (N+1) x 8 bytes = 4 BE half floats  (quaternion slot)
  tail  (68 bytes) = {u32 0, u32 0, u32 0, u32 0x21, u32 2, u32 0, f32 32.3333,
                      3 x (half 1.0, half 1.0), u32 0, u32 0, u32 0, f32 1.0, f32 1.0,
                      f32 1.0, u32 0x00010000}
```
VERIFIED EXACTLY on 6 nodes of pc111_002_p.GAP (predicted total vs actual):
```
Spine         N=971 -> predicted 11,764  actual 11,764  tail 68
Spine1        N=971 -> 11,764  11,764  68
neck          N=971 -> 11,764  11,764  68
RightForeArm  N=938 -> 11,368  11,368  68
LeftForeArm   N=947 -> 11,476  11,476  68
LeftHandRing3 N=793 ->  9,628   9,628  68
```
and the size formula alone matched ~20 further nodes inspected in 18.2505 (container sizes
11,752 / 11,764 / 11,524 / 11,548 / 11,500 / 11,320 / 10,684 / 10,240 / 9,508 ...).

2) TIME ARRAY (MEASURED)
first = 0.000000, second = 0.033333 (1/30), i-th = i/30; the LAST slot is 0.0 (anomaly recorded:
e.g. Spine N=971 -> entry 970 = 32.3333 and entry 971 = 0.0). Grid = 30 fps, same as all pose
times. Tail always carries f32 32.3333 (= 970/30) independent of N.

3) QUATERNION SLOT (MEASURED, decisive)
Reading each 8-byte slot as 4 BE halves and computing the norm:
```
Spine         500/500 unit (|q| in 0.9852..1.0149)
Spine1        500/500 unit (0.9930..1.0076)
neck          500/500 unit (0.9900..1.0130)
LeftHandRing3 500/500 unit (0.9994..1.0000)
RightForeArm  225/500 unit (0.8189..1.1303)   <- ANOMALY, see OPEN
LeftForeArm   237/500 unit (0.8262..1.1410)   <- ANOMALY, see OPEN
first quats (verbatim halves): Spine (0.01119,0.97852,-0.24768,-0.002) ;
Spine1 (-0.001,0.99756,-0.06097,-0.01151) ; LeftHandRing3 (-0.03656,0.99902,0,0)
```
=> the container's key slot is a 4-half QUATERNION track over N+1 frames at 30 fps.

4) WHAT A VER3 NODE REALLY IS (structural conclusion, data-side)
A ver3/F1=31 node carries TWO tracks:
```
(a) its own small schema record: (kf-1) times + kf x 6-byte (3-half) keys   [parser already reads]
(b) the container: a full-length (N+1 frame) 30 fps QUATERNION track + 32B head + 68B tail
```
So the three half-curves measured in 18.2500/18.2502 are the node's SECOND channel, NOT the
node's rotation. The rotation lives in the container quaternion track. Any semantics for the
3-half channel must be stated relative to this two-channel node model.

### 18.2507 *** CORRECTION TO 18.2506: CONTAINER = 32B HEAD + N TIMES + (N+1) QUATS(x,y,z,w) + 72B TAIL ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: ver3 container correction, times N not N+1, tail 72, quaternion
order x y z w, forearm anomaly resolved, off-by-one, unit quaternion 400/400.

1) CORRECTION (the total size formula of 18.2506 was right, the internal split was off by 4 bytes)
WRONG (18.2506): times = N+1, keys = N+1, tail = 68
RIGHT (measured): times = N, keys = N+1, tail = 72
Both give the same total: 32 + 12*(N+1) + 68  ==  32 + 4*N + 8*(N+1) + 72  ==  12*N + 112.
The "last time = 0.0" anomaly reported in 18.2506 was in fact the first 4 bytes of the quaternion
block being misread as an f32.

2) ALIGNMENT PROOF (keys_start = kend + 32 + 4*N)
Unit-quaternion fraction over the first 400 slots, comparing the two candidate offsets:
```

```
=> +4N is the correct alignment and the tail is 72 bytes for EVERY node.
The forearm anomaly of 18.2506 is RESOLVED: it was this off-by-one, not a different channel type.

3) CORRECTED LAYOUT (CONFIRMED, byte-exact, 12 nodes)

container size = 12*N + 112
+0        32 B head: {f32 a, f32 b, f32 c, u32 0, u32 0, u32 0, u32 0x20, u32 N}

### 18.2508 *** REFUTATION: ver3 3-HALF CHANNEL IS NOT A ROTATION OF THE CONTAINER QUATERNION ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: 3-half channel refuted, not rotation, independent channels,
static parameter triple, Euler orders tested, hinge axis candidate open.

1) HYPOTHESIS TESTED (and REFUTED)
Hypothesis: the ver3 node's own 3-half channel encodes a rotation that composes with (or equals)
the container quaternion track. Test: take each node's average 3-half triple (v0,v1,v2) and
reconstruct a quaternion by two families of conventions, then compare to the container slot 0:
```
 (a) axis-angle: angle = pi * |v|, axis = v/|v|
 (b) Euler with each of 6 orders (XYZ, XZY, YXZ, YZX, ZXY, ZYX), angles = pi * v_i
 compare via quaternion angle: 2*acos(|dot|)
```
MEASURED residuals (degrees, best convention per node):
```
node             own 3-half (avg)                best convention   residual
Spine            ( 0.19995, 0.00000, 0.00000)     axis-angle        59.6
Spine1           ( 0.99961, 0.00000, 0.00000)     axis-angle       174.7
Spine2           ( 0.99961, 0.00000, 0.00000)     axis-angle       179.1
neck             ( 0.99963, 0.99951, 0.00000)     YXZ              176.1
head             ( 0.99961, 0.00000, 0.00000)     axis-angle       164.1
RightShoulder    ( 0.99961, 0.99951, 0.99951)     YXZ              109.0
RightArm         ( 0.99961, 0.00000, 0.00000)     axis-angle       176.8
RightForeArm     ( 0.99951, 0.00034,-0.00058)     XYZ              179.9
LeftForeArm      ( 0.99951, 0.00236,-0.00036)     axis-angle       179.8
RightHand        ( 0.99961, 0.00000, 0.00000)     axis-angle       167.2
LeftHandRing3    ( 0.99951, 0.00000, 0.00000)     axis-angle       179.9
LeftHandThumb1   ( 0.97803,-0.66748, 0.99951)     ZYX               34.7
```
=> NO convention explains the data (residuals 59.6..179.9 deg). The rotation hypothesis is
   REFUTED. (Residual near 180 means the best-fit quaternion is the opposite/rotated one.)

2) THE TWO CHANNELS ARE INDEPENDENT (MEASURED)
Side-by-side for the forearms:
```
RightForeArm kf=222, own times 0.0667..32.3333
  own 3-half keys stay essentially constant: (0.99951, 0.00000, 0.00000) with tiny deviations
  container quats rotate about Y: t=0.0667 -> (0,0.927,0,0.375) = 135.9 deg ;

LeftForeArm similar (own 3-half ~ (0.99951,0,0) ; quats about Y from 103.6 down to 13.4 deg)
```
=> the container quaternion carries the ANIMATION; the node's own 3-half channel is a separate,
   mostly-static triple. They are NOT redundant and one does not reconstruct the other.

3) CONSEQUENCE FOR THE NODE MODEL
```
ver3 node = [static/param triple channel (kf small, 3 halves)] + [full-length quaternion track]
The static triple must be interpreted as a per-node PARAMETER, not as pose rotation.
Candidates that remain compatible with (1,0,0)/(1,1,0)/(1,1,1)-style static values:
  hinge axis, scale/physics parameter triple, offset/axis. ALL ARE UNPROVEN.
```
A useful discriminator recorded: values cluster on (1-ULP of 1.0) and exact 0.0/0.5/0.6875, i.e.
the engine writes these in half precision from computed floats, which suggests a normalized
quantity (axis-like) rather than authored key values.

### 18.2510 RESOURCE REGISTRY INFRASTRUCTURE (hash = byte sum, two tables, path normalizer) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: resource registry lookup, byte-sum hash, 0x81557368 stride 0x98,
linked list 0x816CDAC8 refcount, path normalizer 0x8118192C, lip loader branch disassembly.

1) 0x81181D90 = NAME/REGISTRY LOOKUP (disassembled, exact)
```
signature: int lookup(void *name, u32 *out_id2)
  stack 0x414 + canary 0x812B414C
  copies name into a 0x100-byte stack buffer (loop 0x81181DD6: up to 0xFF chars, stops at NUL)
  calls 0x8118192C(buffer, buffer2)            ; path/name normalizer (see 3)
  calls 0x812B22E0(buffer2)                    ; strlen
  HASH LOOP 0x81181E08..0x81181E1E :
      h = 0 ; for each byte c of buffer2: h += (u8)c
  TABLE SCAN 0x81181E36..0x81181E88 :
      base = 0x81557368 ; stride = 0x98 ; up to 0x200 (512) entries
      entry+0x00 : char name[]            (loaded as bytes at 0x81181E36)
      entry+0x08 : char key2[]            (r7 = base+8, compared via 0x812B2200)
      entry+0x94 : u32 hash               (compared with h, 0x81181E3C)
      entry+0x88 : u32 RESULT  -> returned in r0
      entry+0x8C : u32 RESULT2 -> stored to *out_id2
  no match -> returns 0
```
=> the engine's resource hash for this registry is a simple SUM OF UNSIGNED BYTES of the
   normalized name (NOT CRC32 and NOT a polynomial hash). Entry stride 0x98 = 152 bytes.

2) SECOND REGISTRY = SINGLY LINKED LIST (disassembled, exact)
```
0x81181A9E..0x81181B5E (inside 0x81181F1A's flow):
  head        : 0x816CDAC8
  node+0x08   : path/name string (normalized again via 0x8118192C)
  node+0x90   : s16 REFCOUNT (incremented on hit, 0x81181B20)
  node+0xA4   : u32 hash (byte sum of normalized name, 0x81181AFC..0x81181B08)
  node+0xC4   : next pointer (walked at 0x81181B4C..0x81181B5C)
  global counter : 0x813B017C incremented on hit (0x81181B3A..0x81181B48)
  on hit also calls 0x81207454(*(u32*)0x81557360, 1)
```
=> resource bookkeeping is (hash, name, refcount) in a linked list; the hash algorithm is the
   SAME byte-sum used by the array registry.

3) 0x8118192C = PATH / NAME NORMALIZER (disassembled)
```
- input copied to stack; scans for ':' (0x3A) at 0x81181958 and, if found, continues from the
  character after it (prefix strip, e.g. "scheme:path")
- in the string it detects the sequences "..\" (0x2E 0x2E 0x5C) and "../" (0x2E 0x2E 0x2F)
  at 0x8118198E..0x811819B8 and applies dot-dot handling
- treats both '\' (0x5C) and '/' (0x2F) as separators (0x811819CA..0x811819DC)
- copies the resulting component/leaf into the output buffer (0x81181A9E loop, max 0xFF)
```
=> implement this exact algorithm when reproducing resource lookup, otherwise registry hashes will
   not match the game's (the hash is computed on the NORMALIZED name).

4) WHY THIS MATTERS FOR THE REMAINING OPEN ITEMS
The lip loader tree (0x81181F9C -> 0x81181D90 / 0x81181F1A) is a RESOURCE LOOKUP, not the 20-byte
event-table record parser. So the event-table reader (item C) is NOT in that subtree; it must be
found downstream of a successful lookup (the returned +0x88/+0x8C words), or in the consumer of
the lip tables reached from the B-class arc loader.
NEXT CODE TARGET (exact): find callers of 0x81181D90 (mode-1 path) and inspect what they do with
the returned pair; the 20-byte stride (0x14) reader should appear among them.

### 18.2511 LIP MODULE CALL GRAPH (BL scan) + RESOURCE-HANDLE LAYOUT (state 3 = ready) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: thumb BL decoder, call graph scan, lip thunk wrappers,
lip resource handle layout, state 3 ready, 0x81182E60 consumer, 20-byte reader still open.

1) TOOLING: ROBUST THUMB BL SCANNER (reusable for all future code work)
A halfword-aligned scanner decodes Thumb-2 BL directly from the image (no disassembler needed):
```
hw1 = 11110 S imm10 ; hw2 = 11 J1 1 J2 imm11   (BL: hw2 bit12 == 1)
I1 = 1-(J1^S) ; I2 = 1-(J2^S) ; imm32 = S:I1:I2:imm10:imm11:0 (sign-extended)
target = pc + 4 + imm32
NOTE: the BLX discriminator is hw2 bit12 (0 => BLX); checking bit14 is WRONG because bit14 is
always 1 for BL. Validated on three known sites:
  0x81181FC0 -> 0x81181F1A ; 0x81181FCC -> 0x81181D90 ; 0x81181FE0 -> 0x81181D90
```
Full-image scan (all even offsets, 0x10E0..end) results:
```
0x81181D90  <- 0x8115FD6E (thunk), 0x81181FCC, 0x81181FE0, 0x81182E60   (4 call sites)
0x81181F9C  <- 0x8115FD78 (thunk)                                        (1 call site)
0x81181F1A  <- 0x81181FC0, 0x81181FEC, 0x8118321E                        (3 call sites)
```

2) 0x8115FD20..0x8115FD80 = ONE-INSTRUCTION THUNK TABLE (export wrappers)
Verbatim pattern of each entry:
```
push {r4, lr} ; [optional arg setup: movs r1,#0 / adds r2,r1 / movs r1,#0] ; bl TARGET ; pop {r4, pc}
e.g. 0x8115FD6C: push {r4,lr} ; bl 0x81181D90 ; pop {r4,pc}
     0x8115FD74: push {r4,lr} ; movs r1,#0 ; bl 0x81181F9C ; pop {r4,pc}
```
=> these are the module's exported entry points (a fixed jump/thunk table), so the "callers" found
   above are not business logic; the real consumer is 0x81182E60 (below).

3) REAL CONSUMER 0x81182E5A..0x81182EA2 = RESOURCE LOAD + HANDLE FILL (disassembled)
```
0x81182E4A  ldr r0,=*(0x81557360) ; r1=0 ; bl 0x81207402       ; lock/enter
0x81182E5A  r1 = sp+0x404                                       ; &out2 (second returned word)
0x81182E5E  r0 = r6 (name)
0x81182E60  bl 0x81181D90                                       ; lookup(name, &out2)
0x81182E64  r4 = returned word                                  ; 0 => fail path 0x81182EC6
0x81182E68  r1 = *(i8*)(r5+0x87) ; cmp r1,#0 ; strb #1,[r5,#6]
0x81182E72  r2 = *(u32*)(sp+0x404)                              ; out2 = SIZE
0x81182E76  r1 = *(u32*)(r5+0x90)                               ; current size
0x81182E7C  if (*(i8*)(r5+0x87)==0):
             r0 = 0x8105AE6A(r2)  -> r5+0x8C = buffer ptr
             r5+0x8C = result ; r5+0x90 = r2 (size) ; r1 = r2
0x81182E90  if (r1 >= r2): r0 = r5+0x8C ; r1 = r4 ; blx 0x812B2270   ; memcpy(buf, data, size)
0x81182E9E  strh #3, [r5,#4]                                    ; STATE = 3 (ready)
```
HANDLE LAYOUT (measured from the code, offsets are into the r5 structure):
```
+0x04 u16 state        (set to 3 when data is loaded and copied)
+0x06 u8  flag         (set to 1 on first successful load)
+0x87 u8  flag         (0 => allocate/copy path taken)
+0x8C u32 data pointer
+0x90 u32 data size (bytes)
```
=> this is the generic "load resource by name -> allocate -> memcpy -> state=3" flow. The same
   structure must be reproduced for the native engine's resource layer.

4) CONSEQUENCE FOR THE EVENT-TABLE READER (item C)
The 20-byte-stride reader is NOT in the lip loader subtree; the loaded buffer is handed to the lip
PLAYBACK module through (handle+0x8C, handle+0x90). NEXT CODE TARGET (exact): find readers of
+0x8C/+0x90 of this handle in the lip/evt modules and look for a loop with stride 0x14 (=20) and

(evtSequenceMotion.c 0x81085B4E.., mnsHandle.c 0x81119AB2.., mnsProcess.c 0x81121360..).

### 18.2521 ESM STREAM READERS DECODED (token encoding = LE u32; reader struct fixed) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: evtStream readers, read_u32 little endian, reader struct
+0x04 base +0x08 cursor +0x0C limit, bounds assert line 0x25, buffer block header.

1) READER STRUCTURE (measured from every reader function)
```
reader* : +0x04 = base pointer (payload bytes)
          +0x08 = cursor (byte offset, advances)
          +0x0C = limit (byte size)
argument order: r0 = reader, r1 = value/n
```

2) READERS (disassembled exactly, module evtStream.c = path 0x812F4870)
```
0x8108922E  u32 read_u32():
              r4 = cursor ; r6 = base
              if (cursor + 4 > limit) ASSERT(path 0x812F4870, fmt 0x812F48A0, line 0x25)
              cursor += 4 ; return *(u32*)(base + old_cursor)     <- 32-bit LE load (ldr)
0x81089260  f32 read_f32(): same bounds check ; vldr s0,[base+cursor] ; cursor += 4
0x81089296  u8  read_u8():  bounds check cursor+1 ; store byte ; cursor += 1
0x81089154  void* read_bytes(u32 n):
              if (cursor + n > limit) ASSERT(same path/fmt, line 0x25)
              p = base + cursor ; cursor += n ; return p
```
=> INTEGER TOKENS ARE **LITTLE-ENDIAN 32-BIT** (not varint). Every u16/u8 value in the parser is
   read as a u32 and truncated (the parser did `bl read_u32 ; strh r0,[out+0x10]`).

3) BUFFER BLOCK (input object handed to the parser; 0x8108949E)
```
block = alloc(size + 0x10) via 0x8115D79C + debug alloc 0x8115D36A(path 0x812F4870, line 0x10,
        size, align 4)
memset(block, 0, size+0x10)
block+0x04 = block+0x10          ; base
block+0x08 = 0                   ; cursor  (initialised by the memset)
block+0x0C = size                ; limit
memcpy(block+0x10, src, size)    ; payload copy
=> this block IS a valid reader object: payload at +0x10, and the reader fields are filled so
   that the parser can consume it directly.
```

### 18.2524 ESM STATE MACHINE + EVALUATOR (states 0..6, 0x81086674, 1/240 constant) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: ESM state machine 0x81088C18, state 2 load parse, state 4 evaluate,
0x81086674 evaluator, 0x810864EA per element, 1/240 constant 0x3B888889, result root+0x4C +0x50.

1) STATE MACHINE 0x81088C18 (disassembled; r4 = task, state at [r4+4], flags at [r4])
```
state = [r4+4] switch (7-way, 18.2518)
- state 2 (0x81088C4C..):
    [r4+4] = 2
    r6 = [r4+8]                            ; resource/handle object
    if (r6 == 0 || (*(u32*)r6 & 1)) -> 0x81088CAC
    r0 = [r6+0xC] ; call 0x8115FC0E        ; appFile handle check (18.2515)
    if (result == 0) -> abort 0x81088D6E
    r0 = [r6+0xC] ; r1 = &size ; call 0x8115FC28       ; read whole resource -> data ptr, size
    r1 = *(u32*)sp ; call 0x8108949E                   ; wrap data into reader block (18.2521)
    call 0x81085ED2(out = r6, reader = block)          ; ESM parser (18.2520/18.2522)
    if fail -> ASSERT(evtSequenceMotion.c, line 0x10F)
    call 0x81089144(block)                             ; release reader block
    *(u32*)r6 |= 1                                     ; mark loaded
    *(u32*)r4 |= 1 ; [r4+4] = 4                        ; flags, state = 4
- state 4 (0x81088CAC..):
    if ([r4+0xC] == 0) -> 0x81088D36
    frame = (s32)[r4+0x10] ; s16 = (f32)frame
    call 0x811730DA() ; s0 = (f32)result ; s16 = s16 / s0      ; time fraction = frame / rate
    r5 = [r4+0xC]                       ; the parsed ESM root object
    call 0x81086674(r0 = *(u32*)(r5+0x48) /*child list*/, r1 = 0, s0 = s16,
                    r2 = &two_words_on_stack)
    *(u32*)(r5+0x4C) = word0 ; *(u32*)(r5+0x50) = word1
    if (word0 != 0 && (*(u32*)(r5+0x4C) & 1)) then [r4+0x10] = *(u32*)(r5+0x50)
    else if ((flags & 4) == 0) [r4+0x10] += 1   ; else fall through
    if (flags & 0x10000): state = 5 ; flags |= 2
- state 5 / 6 (0x81088D4A..): teardown:
    state = 6 ; r5 = [r4+8] ; if (r5) { if ([r5+0xC]) { 0x8115FC20(handle) ; [r5+0xC] = 0 }
                                      0x810162E8([r5+4]) ; [r4+8] = 0 }
    return -1
```
=> the ESM runtime model is: **load file -> parse tree (root 0x54 with child list +0x48) -> each
   tick compute time fraction -> evaluate the child list -> two result words stored at
   root+0x4C/+0x50**, where word1 becomes the new current frame.

2) EVALUATOR 0x81086674 (disassembled)
```
signature: f(container r0, ctx r1, float time s0, out* r2)
r6 = container ; r5 = ctx ; s16 = time ; r4 = out
if (ctx == 0): ctx = local stack struct initialised to
      {0, 0, 0x3B888889, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0}
      NOTE 0x3B888889 = 0.0041666669f  (== 1/240)  <- fixed time-step constant
if (*(u32*)(ctx+8) == 0): *(u32*)(ctx+8) = 0x810832BA()      ; lazily create work buffer
if (container == 0): ASSERT(evtSequenceMotion.c, line 0x260)
iterate container: obj = wrap(0x81016296(*(u32*)container)) ;
  loop: 0x810864EA(obj, ctx, time) ; next via 0x81016810/0x81016818 ;
  *(u32*)ctx = current obj  (ctx+0x10 = out pointer)
```

### 18.2525 *** ESM KEYFRAME EVALUATION DECODED (0x810864EA) + (type,index) HANDLER MODEL ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: ESM keyframe evaluator, sub-item list element+0x14, packed type
index word, dispatch table 0x813366B4, handler ctx, size field, 1/240 proximity, runtime table OPEN.

1) EVALUATOR 0x810864EA (disassembled, the core of ESM playback)
```
signature: f(element r0, ctx r1, float time s0)
r8 = element ; s17 = time ; r7 = ctx
if (element == 0) ASSERT(evtSequenceMotion.c, line 0x290)
items = *(u32*)(element + 0x14)            ; sub-item list
if (items == 0) ASSERT(line 0x439)
for each item (iterated with 0x81016810 / 0x81016818):
    d = time - *(f32*)(item + 8)           ; f32 at item+8 = this key's TIME
    ad = fabsf(d)                          ; 0x81164330 = fabsf
    if (ad < *(f32*)(ctx + 0xC)):          ; ctx+0xC = PROXIMITY THRESHOLD (= 1/240, 18.2524)
        *(u32*)(ctx + 4) = item            ; current key
        packed = *(u32*)(item + 4)
        type = packed >> 24                ; assert type < 3 (line 0x755)
        idx  = packed & 0xFF               ; assert idx < count[type] (line 0x757)
        fnTable = *(u32*)(0x813366B4 + type*8)
        count   = *(u32*)(0x813366B4 + type*8 + 4)
        handler = *(u32*)(fnTable + idx*8)
        if (handler) handler(ctx)          ; per (type,index) behaviour
    else if (d < 0) break                  ; keys are time-sorted, stop when past
```
=> SUB-ITEM LAYOUT: `+0x04 u32 packed (type<<24 | index)` ; `+0x08 f32 time` ;
   `+0x0C data pointer` (and `+0x00` list link). Element+0x14 = sub-item list (see 18.2522/18.2523 child layout).
=> ESM playback is a **keyframe selector**: the active key is the one whose time is within 1/240 of
   the current time; its (type,index) selects the handler that mutates the ctx.

### 18.2533 ESM PROPERTY TARGET SYSTEM DECODED (evtSceneManager.c: array+count, packed selector) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: set_int 0x8108287C, set_float 0x810828C0, property array obj+0x0C
count obj+0x10, packed selector 0x81082A2C, evtSceneManager.c, event_data.bin, efp.bin.

1) PROPERTY SETTERS (disassembled exactly)
```
0x8108287C set_int(obj, index, value):
    if (obj == 0) ASSERT(evtSceneManager.c, line 0xEF)
    if (index >= *(u32*)(obj+0x10)) ASSERT(same, line 0xF0)
    *(u32*)(*(u32*)(obj+0x0C) + 4*index) = value
0x810828C0 set_float(obj, index, f32 value):
    if (obj == 0) ASSERT(line 0xF8)
    if (index >= *(u32*)(obj+0x10)) ASSERT(line 0xF9)
    *(f32*)(*(u32*)(obj+0x0C) + 4*index) = value
=> TARGET OBJECT LAYOUT: +0x0C = property array pointer (u32/f32 array), +0x10 = property COUNT.
   Property index range is validated against the count at runtime.
```

2) TARGET SELECTOR 0x81082A2C (the "flags" argument of every handler)
```
f(listObj, packed) -> entry | 0
  head = 0x81016296(*(u32*)(listObj+4))     ; list head
  type = packed >> 24 ; id = packed & 0xFFFFFF
  iterate entries via 0x81016818 / 0x81016810:
      entryPacked = *(u32*)(entry+8)
      match if (type == 0 || type == (entryPacked >> 24)) &&
               (id   == 0 || id   == (entryPacked & 0xFFFFFF))
  return matching entry, or 0 if none
=> the handler "flags" value is a PACKED SELECTOR: high byte = target type, low 24 bits = target id.
   Handlers build it as: (element+0xC | 0x2000000) when element+4==0, or 0x3000000 when ==1.
   i.e. type 2/3 and id = element+0x0C (0 means wildcard/matched by type only).
```

3) MODULE / NEW RESOURCE NAMES (strings read at the ASSERT path VAs)
```
0x812F45B8 = E:\P3DP5D\xrd757\program\app\event\evtSceneManager.c   <- module of this system
0x812F45F0 = "ASSERT:%s"
0x812F45FC = "event/event_data.bin"        <- NEW resource name
0x812F4580 = "efp.bin"                     <- NEW resource name (field position data, cf. evtFieldPos)
```
The event scene manager owns the per-entry property arrays that ESM handlers write into, and it loads
its data from event/event_data.bin (and evtFieldPos from efp.bin).

4) COMPLETE ESM APPLICATION CHAIN (for the native engine)
```
ESM key (type,index) -> handler -> packed selector (element+4 mode, element+0xC id)
  -> 0x81082A2C finds the scene-manager entry matching (type,id)
  -> handler writes integer/float properties into entry property array (+0x0C) at validated indices
  -> idx19 special: flags the out object (ctx+0x10 |= 1) and stores 0x8102AB58(blob[0]) at out+4
  -> idx20 special: converts blob[4] with 0x812B0DD0(value, frameRate) and writes int + float props
```

### 18.2536 GAP PATH BUILDER FAMILY (game.c 0x81092040.., signature + formatting mechanics) ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: GAP path builder family, sprintf 0x812B2280, base formatter
0x8109193C, div-by-100 trick, game.c assert 0x812FA2E4, next step caller scan.

1) MEASURED STRUCTURE (disassembled 0x81092040, 0x810920BC+, 0x81092144+)
```
Each GAP-naming function is a small stack-buffer formatter:
  f(dest r0, baseDir r1, n1 r2 [, n2 r3 ...])
  sp frame 0x50 (+ canary 0x812B414C, canary slot [sp+0x48])
  if (baseDir == 0) ASSERT(path 0x812FA2E4, line 0x19A / 0x1A8 / 0x1B6 ...)   <- game.c
  call 0x8109193C(sp+8, baseDir, 0)            ; format the "%s/..." base part
  div-by-100 remainder trick:
      umull r1,r0, rN, 0x51EB851F ; lsr r0,#6 ; mul lr, r0, #100 ; sub rN, rN, lr
      => n % 100 -> "%02d" argument (uxth)
  call sprintf-family 0x812B2280(dest, format_string, basebuf, n1, n2 ...)
```
Examples measured: 0x81092040 formats "%s/%03d/pc%03d_%03d.GAP" (format VA 0x812FA528);
0x810920BC formats "..._f.GAP" (0x812FA540); 0x81092144 formats "..._%02d.GAP" (0x812FA55C).
The whole family (one function per format string) spans 0x81092040..0x81092E5A inside game.c.

2) CALL CONVENTION SUMMARY
```
r0 = destination buffer (caller-provided, stack buffer in the observed body)
r1 = base directory string (%s)
r2 = n1 (one %03d field; also used for the %100 remainder)
r3 = optional n2 (second number / %02d)
return value unused; result written into dest
```

f(obj r0, slotIndex r1, out r2):

  slot = *(u16*)(obj + 0x10 + slotIndex*2)  ; per-slot u16 id table at obj+0x10

  call 0x8115FCB4(spBuf)                    ; appFile LOAD by name (18.2515) -> bool
  if (load failed) call 0x81093A8C(r4, slot) ; fallback/error path
  format2 = sprintf(spBuf2, fmt=0x812FAD20, 0, slot)
  obj2 = 0x81094C58(3, spBuf2)              ; lookup/create object for that name
  r = 0x8117C2F6(*(u32*)(obj+0x28), spBuf2, obj2, 0)   ; attach/apply
  *out = r
```

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: persona_event_table_p5 nested, 32 entries persona_event_201..232,

  parse end 0x884; after the entries a 28-byte TRAILER:
     20 00 00 00  "persona_event_201.bin" 00 00 00
     = u32 32 (count) + ASCII first-entry name + NUL padding
```

=> the persona event entries are DEFT-family records (the table family already fully specified in
   earlier sections: DSFT/DSCE/DEFT/DENE/DADJ). 16-byte DEFT record layout:

```

### 18.2604 LIP LOADER STATE MACHINE DECODED (site 0x81152DF2): fmt -> sprintf -> load -> +0x110 ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: lip loader 0x81152xxx, state machine r4[0] 0..3, fields +0x04
+0x08 +0x0C event params, fmt 0x81305F9C, appFile info 0x8115FBE6, load 0x8115FC0E, handle +0x110.

1) DISASSEMBLED (0x81152DB4..0x81152E38, target site 0x81152DF2)
```
0x81152DBA blx 0x812B22D0                  ; helper (then stores r0 at [r5] and [r5+4])
0x81152DCA movw/movt r5 = 0x812B414C      ; canary pointer (stack check)
0x81152DD8 r1 = *(u32*)r4                 ; STATE
0x81152DDA... switch on state:
   state == 1 or 2:
     0x81152DEE r0 = *(u32*)(r4+0x04)
     0x81152DF2 r1 = 0x81305F9C           ; "sound/lip/e%03d%03d.arc"
     0x81152DF6 r2 = *(u32*)(r4+0x08)
     0x81152DFC r3 = *(u32*)(r4+0x0C)
     0x81152E00 blx 0x812B2280            ; sprintf(path, fmt, id, part)
     0x81152E0C blx 0x812B2280            ; (second format/append call)
     0x81152E12 bl 0x8115FBE6             ; appFile info/register -> handle
     0x81152E16 *(u32*)(r4+0x110) = r0
     0x81152E1C *(u32*)r4 = r0            ; state <- handle
   state == 3:
     0x81152E20 r0 = *(u32*)(r4+0x110)
     0x81152E24 bl 0x8115FC0E             ; appFile load/update -> result
     0x81152E28 r1 = *(u32*)r4
     0x81152E2A if (r0 != 0) *(u32*)r4 = r0
     0x81152E34 cmp r1,#3 ; bne ...        ; state machine continues
=> STRUCTURE: a per-slot loader object at r4 with:
     +0x00  state (0..3, later becomes handle!)
     +0x04  event id     (first %03d)
     +0x08  part/segment (second %03d argument)
     +0x0C  extra parameter (passed as r3 to the second format call)
     +0x110 appFile handle
   The path is built with the measured format "sound/lip/e%03d%03d.arc" and loaded via the appFile
   helpers 0x8115FBE6 / 0x8115FC0E (the same family as 0x8115FCB4 used by fieldHandler 18.2547).

### 18.2614 *** BL DECODER FIXED (imm10 <<12, calibrated) — lipsync cluster callers found ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: BL decoder fixed imm10 shift 12 not 14, calibration 0x810259EC,
callers 0x810259EC 0x810259F4 0x810259FE 0x81025A06, single-caller API wrappers.

1) DECODER BUG AND FIX (calibrated on a known-good call)
```
observed instruction at VA 0x810259EC : bytes 2d f1 93 f9 (hw1=0xF12D, hw2=0xF993)
capstone decodes it as  bl 0x81152D16 ; target displacement = 0x12D326
WRONG formula (previous sections): imm10 << 14  -> produced 0x814D9D16 (garbage)
CORRECT formula: Thumb-2 BL imm32 = S:I1:I2:imm10:imm11:0
   imm = (S<<24)|(I1<<23)|(I2<<22)|(imm10<<12)|(imm11<<1)  ; if S: -= 1<<25
   with I1 = ~(J1^S), I2 = ~(J2^S)  (1 - xor)
=> calibrated: 0x12D<<12 | 0x193<<1 = 0x12D000 + 0x326 = 0x12D326 EXACT.
```

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: hi byte 1 in 50 of 50, lo values 31..203, offset reading RETRACTED,

sample (fa, name_len): (317,20) (327,14) (352,14) (297,14) (347,14) (367,14) (459,14) (387,14)
=> the value is NOT an offset: hi byte is CONSTANT 1, so fa = 256 + lo. The earlier "FIELD_A is an
   offset" reading (18.2676/18.2677/18.2691) is RETRACTED.
   CORRECT of the variant-B header: two u8 fields:
      +0x00  u8 VALUE_LO   (varies 31..203 in these 50 cases)
      +0x01  u8 FLAG       (1 in all 50 cases; 0 in the 1575 blocks whose u16 was 0)
      +0x02  u32 0x05F1A1F1 (constant)
      +0x06  u32 0x41F1A1FF (constant)
      +0x0A  text ...
=> the u16 field is really (FLAG<<8)|VALUE_LO; the 1575 "zero" blocks have FLAG=0.
   So variant B has TWO SUBTYPES distinguished by the FLAG byte (0 = common, 1 = 50 blocks).

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: 1275 bytes, top 0x8C x95 0x81 x70 0x88 x58 0x89 x55, lead range
47.45 percent, trail range 17.1 percent, valid SJIS double-byte structure, rare-kanji decode,

```

                    0x90 x43 ; 0x63 x39 ; 0x8B x34
range shares      : 0x80-0x9F = 47.45%   (SJIS LEAD byte range)
                    0x40-0x7E = 17.10%   (SJIS TRAIL byte range)
                    0xE0-0xEF = 2.20%
=> the bytes form a VALID SJIS DOUBLE-BYTE STREAM (lead 0x80-0x9F + trail 0x40-0x7E dominate),
   not random data. Decoding them as cp932 yields RARE/LEVEL-2 KANJI, which is exactly what one
   gets when a LOCALISED TEXT (Chinese) is stored through a SJIS glyph mapping (a known technique:
   the game text is CJK, stored as the SJIS codes of glyphs that render the desired hanzi).
=> candidate (still OPEN, but strongly supported by the byte structure): FLAG=1 = localised
   (Chinese) text encoded via SJIS glyph mapping.
```

2) WHY THE EARLIER DECODES LOOKED LIKE GARBAGE
```
cp932 and GB18030 both interpret the BYTES by their own code tables; a glyph-mapped Chinese text
does not decode to meaningful Chinese through either - it decodes to whatever kanji the SJIS codes
name. The byte-level structure (lead/trail ranges) is the reliable evidence, and it says: valid SJIS.
```

   (c) record0 is a DIFFERENT encoding: its halves exceed 1 (e.g. 3.002 / 85.3125), so record0 must

           +0x14 u32 0 ; +0x18 u32 0
           +0x1C u32 index (= sequential entry number 1..N)
           +0x20 u32 A = absolute offset of this entry's TEXT BLOCK (= a + header_len)
           +0x24 .. optional u32 fields (header_len = A - a, observed 36/40/44/48/52/56)
TEXT     : at A: [u32 L = byte length][L bytes]
           token model: F2 <op> <u16 LE> = 4B | F1 <b> = 2B | F5 <b> = 2B | byte<0x20 = 1B |

if alpha != lastAlpha: submit(active = alpha>0, alpha); lastAlpha = alpha
lastTime = t
```

   detected start is a few bytes early; exact per-file table ends still OPEN.

      for (i = 0; i < count; i++) {
