         arr->items[i] = child
      }
   } else {
      obj = appEffect_format_8101c5d0(uVar1, 0)          // create attribute object
      if (tag in {0x204, 0x205, 0x206}) local[0] = FUN_8101c1cc(stream)   // one u32
      else if (tag == 0x203) { for (k=0;k<2;k++) { local[2k] = FUN_8101c1d8; local[2k+1] = FUN_8101c1d8; } }  // 4 floats
      else if (tag == 0x202) { 3 x FUN_8101c1d8 }        // vec3 floats
      else if (tag == 0x201) { 2 x FUN_8101c1d8 }        // vec2 floats
      else if (tag == 0x200) { 1 x FUN_8101c1d8 }        // scalar float

   }

      0x10000010 -> tag 0x100, data 16  (list/array attribute)
      0x20100005 -> tag 0x201, data 5   (vec2 attribute, then 2 floats)
      0x20000006 -> tag 0x200, data 6   (float attribute, then 1 float, e.g. 0x42B60000=91.0)
      0x20400010 -> tag 0x204, data 16  (u32 attribute, then 1 word)

appEffect_format_8101c5d0(token, param2):
   group = token >> 28                      // 4 bits, asserted <= 2
   tb    = &DAT_8132aca8 + group*8          // per-group TABLE SIZE
   if (*(u32*)tb <= (token & 0xFFFF)) assert          // id bounds check
   base  = &DAT_8132aca4 + group*8          // per-group TABLE BASE
   desc  = *(u32*)base + (token & 0xFFFF) * 0x18      // 24-byte descriptor per id
   extra = appEffect_format_8101c538(token)
   size  = extra + param2*4 + *(s32*)(desc+8) + 0x10
   obj   = alloc(size); memset(obj,0,size)
   obj[0] = token ; obj[2] = param2 ; obj[1] = &obj[4]
   if (extra != 0) obj[3] = &obj[4] + param2
=> FULL TOKEN FORMAT (evidence-level):
      bits 31..28 : GROUP (0..2; group 1 = list/array tokens 0x100xxxxx, group 2 = value tokens
                    0x200xxxxx .. 0x206xxxxx)

                    0x203=4 floats, 0x204/0x205/0x206=u32)
      bits 19..0  : ID (16-bit checked at +20, so ID = token & 0xFFFF; high nibble of the old "data20"
                    is the subtype, not part of the id)

### 18.3001 *** MSG1 RUNTIME PARSER FOUND - m_app_app_system_utility_appMessage (appMessageBinary.c): OBJECT LAYOUT {+4 COUNT/VALUE, +8 MAGIC 0x3047534D "MSG0" / 0x3147534D "MSG1", +0x10 OFFSET OF BYTE-CODE FIXUP STREAM, +0x14 FIXUP STREAM LENGTH (= OUR fC!), +0x1C u16 FLAGS (bit0 = FIXED UP), +0x20 PAIR TABLE (8-BYTE ENTRIES)}; PAIR ACCESSOR = obj + idx*8 + 0x20; FIXUP DECODER appMessageBinary_81027b2a READS VARIABLE-LENGTH DELTAS AND REBASES THE STORED OFFSETS ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: magic checks at param_1+8 == 0x3047534D (MSG0) or 0x3147534D (MSG1)
appear in appMessageBinary_81027a7c (validator), 81027aba (pair accessor: return param_1 + param_2*8
+ 0x20), 81027b2a (fixup decoder), 81027cbc (returns *(u32*)(param_1+4)), 81027d22, 81027d8a etc.
Fixup decoder 81027b2a: if (*(u16*)(obj+0x1c) & 1) == 0 { table = obj+0x20; len = *(u32*)(obj+0x14);
stream = (byte*)(obj + *(int*)(obj+0x10)); walk bytes: code byte bits: if !(b&1) uVar10=(b&0x7ffffffe)<<1
(1-byte delta); else if !(b&2) 2-byte value CONCAT11(b1,b)&0xfffffffc; else if !(b&4) 3-byte value;
else run of ((b>>3)+2) entries; for each: table[k] = table[k] - (relative base); then set
obj+0x1c u16 |= 1. => fC = byte-code stream length (our histogram 50..100); obj+0x10 = stream offset
(our f8 in file terms since magic at obj+8 and file index i+8 holds f8); obj+4 = count/other value =
file bytes at i-4.. hmm careful: object base = file index of magic - 8.

1) MEASURED (seg0 42720-42960, appMessageBinary.c)
```
MSG object layout (base = param_1):
   +0x04 : u32 count/value      (appMessageBinary_81027cbc returns it)
   +0x08 : u32 magic  "MSG0" 0x3047534D / "MSG1" 0x3147534D
   +0x10 : u32 offset of the byte-code FIXUP STREAM, relative to object base
   +0x14 : u32 length of the fixup stream          == our fC  (values 50..100)
   +0x1C : u16 flags ; bit0 = already fixed up
   +0x20 : pair table, 8-byte entries ; accessor: obj + idx*8 + 0x20
fixup decoder appMessageBinary_81027b2a(obj):
   if ((u16 flags & 1) == 0) {
      pairs  = obj + 0x20
      len    = *(u32 *)(obj + 0x14)
      stream = (u8 *)(obj + *(u32 *)(obj + 0x10))
      walk: code b:
         !(b&1)      -> delta = (b & 0x7ffffffe) << 1 ; 1 byte
         !(b&2)      -> delta = CONCAT11(stream[1], b) & ~3 ; 2 bytes
         !(b&4)      -> delta = 3-byte value >> 3 << 2 ; 3 bytes
         else        -> run of ((b >> 3) + 2) entries with 4-byte steps
         for each affected slot: pairs[k] = pairs[k] - (slot address - pairs base)
      flags |= 1
   }
=> This is a RELOCATION/FIXUP pass: the MSG file stores pair values as offsets relative to the pair
   table, and at load time they are converted to absolute pointers (or vice versa). The byte-code
   stream (length = fC) is a compressed delta list driving this fixup.
   THAT EXPLAINS fC (50..100 = compressed fixup stream length) and why the "tail" bytes looked
   non-tabular: the region is fixup/relocation data, not an offset table.
NEXT: read the remaining accessors (81027cbc count, 81027d22, 81027d8a, 81027e...) to map entry
   fields (offset/flag/name etc.) and then rewrite the MSG1 spec with the correct object layout.

HIGH BYTE 0xF1/0xF2/0xF3/0xF4/0xF5... AND LOW BYTE = (GROUP<<5)|(INDEX); appFontTag_81022530(tag) DECODES GROUP = (tag & 0xFF) >> 5, INDEX = tag & 0x1F, DESCRIPTOR = DAT_8132ad7c[group] + index*12 WITH FIELDS {+4 NAME PTR, +8 u16 ID}; appFont_8101f82e CURSOR SCAN {appCharacter_8101d7f8(c) = TYPE 1/2/3, appCharacter_8101d762(c) = TAG ID FOR TYPE 1} ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: appFontTag_81022484(param_1 name): if (DAT_8132ad78 & 1)==0 assert;
uVar8=0; if DAT_8132ad80 != 0 loop groups iVar7 over 8-byte entries {+0 desc array, +4 count}:
inner iVar4 over 12-byte desc entries; iVar2 = *(u32*)(desc + 4) (name ptr); if matches param_1
return ((*(u16*)(desc + 8) * 0x100 + 0xf100) & 0xffff) | ((uVar8 & 7) << 5) | (uVar5 & 0x1f).
appFontTag_81022530(tag): group=(tag&0xff)>>5; assert group < DAT_8132ad80; assert count >= (tag&0x1f);
return DAT_8132ad7c[group] + (tag & 0x1f)*0xc. appFont_8101f82e(state, param_2 tag, param_3 mode):
state = {+0 layout/root, +4 cur node, +8 cur char}; loop chars: iVar1 = appCharacter_8101d7f8(c);
if 0 advance; if type<2 and !(mode&1) and (tag==0 || tag==appCharacter_8101d762(c)) -> match set
state[1],state[2] return 1; if 2<=type<3 and !(mode&2) -> match. FUN_8101f93a(state, layout) resets
cursor. appFont_8101f80c(state) returns *(u32*)(state+8) (current tag arg?). => F1/F2/F5 = font tag
high bytes: F1 = tag class with descriptor id... (tag = 0xF100 + id*0x100), F2 = +0x100, F5 = +0x400.

appFont_8101f82e(state, tag, mode):        // cursor/tag scanner over the character list
   layout = *state ; cur = state[1] ; chr = state[2]
   loop over character nodes:
      type = appCharacter_8101d7f8(chr)     // 0 = normal char, 1 = tag, 2 = ?, >=3 = other
      if type == 0: advance; continue
      if type < 2 && !(mode & 1):
         if (tag == 0 || tag == appCharacter_8101d762(chr)) {
            state[1] = cur ; state[2] = chr ; return 1        // MATCH
         }
      else if (type < 3 && !(mode & 2)) { state[1]=cur; state[2]=chr; return 1 }
      advance
appFont_8101f93a(state, layout): *state = layout ; state[1] = 0 ; state[2] = 0   // reset
appFont_8101f80c(state): return state[2]   // current matched char/tag
appFontTag_81022484(name):                  // name -> tag word
   iterate group table DAT_8132ad7c (entries 8 B: {descArray,+count}), desc entries 12 B:
      +0 ? ; +4 char* name ; +8 u16 descId
   return ((descId * 0x100 + 0xF100) & 0xFFFF) | ((group & 7) << 5) | (index & 0x1F)
appFontTag_81022530(tag):                   // tag word -> descriptor
   group = (tag & 0xFF) >> 5 ; index = tag & 0x1F
   assert group < groupCount ; assert groupCount[group] > index
   return DAT_8132ad7c[group] + index*0xC
=> TAG WORD FORMAT: high byte = 0xF1 + descId (so descId 0 => 0xF1, 1 => 0xF2, 4 => 0xF5),
   low byte  = (group << 5) | index.

      F1 xx = font tag with descriptor id 0, subgroup/index = xx bits
      F2 xx = font tag with descriptor id 1 (and F2 is followed by a u16 arg in the text stream)
      F5 xx = font tag with descriptor id 4

### 18.3026 GAP NUMERIC CODEC PRIMITIVES IDENTIFIED: HALF-FLOAT DECODE FUN_811dd816 (u16 -> f32 BITS: SIGN | (EXP10 + 0x70) << 23 | MANT10 << 13), HALF ENCODE FUN_811dd7de, COMPRESSED 10/10/9-BIT VECTOR DECODE FUN_811dd758 (f1 = x/1023, f2 = y/1023, f3 = z/511), BYTE<->FLOAT FUN_811dd95e (f*255, clamp 0..1) / FUN_811dd9ba (u8/255); NO ver3 RECORD0 CONSUMER IDENTIFIED YET - NEXT SEARCH: THREE-HALF RECORDS WITH A SPECIAL FIRST WORD ***

(uVar2 = sign<<15 | ((exp) ; FUN_811dd758(u32,float*,float*,float*): fVar1 = (bits & 0x7ff) | signlut;
fVar2 = (bits & 0x3fffff) >> 0xb | lut; fVar3 = bits >> 0x16; *p2 = f1/1023.0; *p3 = f2/1023.0;
*p4 = f3/511.0 ; FUN_811dd95e(float) -> (u8)(clamp(f,0,1)*255); FUN_811dd9ba(u8) -> u8/255.0.

   nameLen=BE16 at 0x3A, name=b[0x3C:0x3C+nameLen], q=0x3C+nameLen.
2) sparse head: u32 at q, ver=BE32(q+4)==3, F1=BE32(q+8), kf=BE32(q+0xC);
   times = BE32F32 x (kf-1) at q+0x10; records = kf x 3 BE u16 at q+16+4*(kf-1) (F1 channel type;
   0x1F => 3 components; decode via half->float LUT and rescale per FUN_8119d1a6 case 0x1f).
3) pos = q+16+4*(kf-1)+6*kf; loop until EOF:

      META 80 B (validate duration=f32 at pos+0x20, six 1.0 halves, three 1.0 f32, tag),
      name at pos+0x50 (len L), hash=BE32(pos+0x50+L), N/TYPE/COUNT/0 = 4 u32;
      data = N segments of [sparse f32 times (multiples of 1/30) + COUNT*bytesPerKey(TYPE)]
      (segment boundaries: times run then key bytes; for N=1 size = 4(T)+bytesPerKey*COUNT).

        first time in (0.02,0.05)} => DENSE section:

   else error.

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: stage_format_table.arc (13,616 B): +0x00 BE u32 = 3 ; +0x04 char[28]
"stage_format_table_p3.arc" ; +0x20 u32 (LE 0) ; +0x24 LE = 5920 ; +0x28 LE = 45 = entry count.
Entry at 0x2C: char[24] "partner_type_table.bin", then g0/g1/g2 as LITTLE-endian u32 (g2 = 64 =
payload length), payload at +0x24+12 = 0x50 begins big-endian "DTBL". => .arc container fields are
LE while payload bodies are BE; earlier .arc spec treated fields as BE (correction).

+0x24 u32 = 5920        (LE)
+0x28 u32 = 45          (LE, entry count, matches known 45)
+0x2C entry: char[24] name + 3 x LE u32 (g0,g1,g2=payloadLen) + payload (BE, e.g. "DTBL"/"DSFT")
=> MIXED ENDIANNESS: container LE, payload BE. This corrects the earlier .arc spec.

### 18.3150 ver3 GAP LOADER PSEUDOCODE v2.2 (FINAL CONTAINER/SEGMENT LEVEL): CHECK "GFS0"; FILE HEADER 16 B; ONE SEGMENT AT 0x10 {type 0x01105090, 0x0001xxxx, BE size, 0}; BODY AT 0x20; ACCEPT END AT fileSize OR fileSize-16 (TERMINATOR OPTIONAL); BODY FIELDS + SPARSE HEAD + BLOCK WALK PER 18.3095/18.3148 ***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: final loader pseudocode:
```
read file b
assert b[0:4]=="GFS0"
assert BE32(0x04)==0x01105090 and BE32(0x08)==1 and BE32(0x0C)==0
seg_off = 0x10
assert BE32(seg_off)==0x01105090
seg_type2 = BE32(seg_off+4)      # 0x000100FD observed
seg_size  = BE32(seg_off+8)      # includes 16-byte segment header
assert seg_off + seg_size <= len(b)
end = seg_off + seg_size
assert end == len(b) or end == len(b)-16     # terminator optional (18.3149)
body = seg_off + 16                # 0x20
assert BE32(body+0x00)==8, BE32(body+0x04)==1, BE32(body+0x08)==0x40000001
duration = f32BE(body+0x0C)
f_10 = BE32(body+0x10)             # observed 39
f_14 = BE32(body+0x14)             # 0x00010000
nameLen = BE16(body+0x1A)
name = b[body+0x1C : body+0x1C+nameLen]
q = body+0x1C+nameLen
hash = BE32(q)
sp = q+4                            # sparse head
assert BE32(sp)==3                  # ver
F1 = BE32(sp+4); kf = BE32(sp+8)
times = (kf-1) x f32BE from sp+0x0C
keys  = kf x records after times (F1=0x1F -> 3 BE u16 each)
pos = keys_end
loop until EOF/terminator: bone block or dense section per 18.3095/18.3085/18.3148
```
Corpus: all 372 ver3 GAPs single-segment; terminator 240 / none 132; zero failures.

```
container/segment/body spec FINAL (v2.2). Remaining semantic OPEN: word0 only.
```

### 18.3302 *** QUATERNION -> MATRIX CONTRACT FOUND: FUN_8116b18e (VA 0x8116B18E, SIZE 192 B) BUILDS A COLUMN-MAJOR 3x4 ROTATION MATRIX FROM q=(x,y,z,w) WITH THE STANDARD UNIT-QUATERNION FORMULA: m0=1-2(y^2+z^2), m1=2(xy+wz), m2=2(zx-wy), m3=2(xy-wz), m4=1-2(x^2+z^2), m5=2(yz+wx), m6=2(zx+wy), m7=2(yz-wx), m8=1-2(x^2+y^2), m9=m10=m11=0 => COLUMN-MAJOR (m1=R10, m3=R01, m6=R02, m7=R12) = OPENGL LAYOUT; THERE IS NO NORMALIZATION: THE ENGINE ASSUMES |q|~1 AND USES THE STORED VALUES DIRECTLY, SO THE NATIVE PORT MUST NOT RENORMALIZE IF BIT/SCALE-EXACT BEHAVIOUR IS WANTED **

EVIDENCE (C lines 322165-322191, VA 8116b18e size=192):
  fVar1..fVar4 = param_1[0..3] = (x,y,z,w).
  param_2[2] = (z*x - w*y)*2;  param_2[1] = (x*y + w*z)*2;  param_2[3] = (x*y - w*z)*2;
  param_2[0] = 1 - (y*y + z*z)*2;  param_2[4] = 1 - (x*x + z*z)*2;
  param_2[5] = (y*z + w*x)*2;  param_2[6] = (z*x + w*y)*2;  param_2[7] = (y*z - w*x)*2;
  param_2[8] = 1 - (x*x + y*y)*2;  param_2[9..0xB] = 0.
=> standard R(q) with OpenGL column-major element order (R00,R10,R20,R01,R11,R21,R02,R12,R22) + zero third
   column (3x4 affine-friendly form). No division by |q|: the truncation bias (|q|^2~0.9993) propagates into a
   tiny uniform scale error, exactly as the original does. This closes the handedness/row-column and
   normalization questions together.

NEXT: confirm the caller composes this R into a 4x4 TRS and check the element order of translation/scale columns;
then the skeleton matrix path is fully specified.

### 18.3325 GAP LOADER IMPLEMENTATION SPEC v6 (CONSOLIDATED, READY FOR A NATIVE PORT): ONE SECTION SUMMARISING THE REGRESSION-LOCKED RULES FOR .gap PARSING AND POSING **

CONTAINER (.gap/.gfs/.gmd-most): magic "GFS0"; 16-B file header {+0x04 type (0x01105090 pose / 0x01104050 object mesh), +0x08 =1, +0x0C =0};
  segments from 0x10 {u32 type, u32 0x000100FD (pose) / 0x000100FC (mesh), u32 BE size incl 16-B seg header, u32 0};
  optional 16-B GFS0 terminator AFTER the segment size field (len(file)==segend+16).
BODY (pose): {u32 8, u32 count, u32 flag 0x40000001|0x40000011, f32 duration, u32 count, u32 0x00010000,
  {u16 X, u16 nameLen}, name (ASCII), u32 hash, sparse head}.
SPARSE HEAD: sp = body+0x1C+nameLen+4; {u32 ver, u32 F1, u32 kf, (kf-1) f32 times, kf x 6 B halves}; block start =
  sp+12+4*(kf-1)+6*kf.
BLOCK FAMILIES (walk until segment end / 100-B nameless terminal / footer / 16-B terminator):
  DENSE: 40-B header {x0..3,0,0,0,type,count,0}, times=1/30 grid, size 40+(4+bpk(type))*count (type 0x20 -> 8 B/key).
  SHORT DENSE: 24-B header {0,0,0,type,count,0}; time at +24; size 24+(4+bpk)*count.
  NAMED BONE: 80-B META core {5 zeros,0x21,X1,0,duration,0x3C003C00x3,0,0,0,1.0x3,0x00010000,{X2,nameLen},name,hash,
    desc{N,TYPE,COUNT,0}}, track 4*(C-2)+6C (TYPE 0x1F) or 4*(C-1)+14C+4 (0x1A); may be 2-byte aligned.
  ANONYMOUS TRACK: 72-B META core, then nested-node lead region, then T 1/30-grid f32 times, then keys:
    (T+1) x 8 B records + u32 zero; K=T+1 (18.3322); nested lead nodes use the SAME block families (18.3321).
  KEY RECORD = unit quaternion 4 halves (x,y,z,w), |q|~0.9994 (truncating half encode); interpolate with
    shortest-arc SLERP (dot<0 negate; theta=acos(dot); w0=sin((1-t)theta)/sin(theta), w1=sin(t theta)/sin(theta)),
    near-parallel dot>=0.999 avoids the divide (FUN_811a1f58/FUN_811a242a); scalar/6-value tracks use 6-float lerp
    a+t*(b-a) (FUN_811a2044/FUN_811a29d0).
  HALF<->FLOAT: exact bit formulas from FUN_811dd816 (half->float) and FUN_811dd7de (float->half, truncating,
    underflow->0, saturate 0x7BFF) (18.3296).
  MATRIX: R 3x4 column-major (OpenGL order) from q with the standard 1-2(x^2+y^2+z^2) formula, NO normalization
    (FUN_8116b18e; 18.3302).
DISPATCH: by payload TYPE word (extension is NOT the type; 570/571 .GMD are 0x01105090 pose data; 18.3313).
REGRESSION: tools\gap_walk_ver3.py -> GAP_WALK_VER3 1039/1039; run_all_regressions.ps1 gates it; ALL_REGRESSIONS_PASS.

### 18.3453 VER3 6-BYTE KEY RAW BYTES: EACH RECORD IS THREE HALF-PRECISION FLOATS ALL LYING IN THE [0.9375, 0.99951] BINADE (0x3B00..0x3BFF); NO RECORD LEAVES THAT BINADE IN THE SAMPLED NODE. COL2 CONSTANT 0x3BFF (=0.99951), COL1 CONSTANT 0x3BFE (=0.99902). **
EVIDENCE (2026-10-23, file C:\dev\out\p5d_game\DANCE\PLAYER\P5\201\pc201_015_p_06.GAP, ver=3, kf=373, key_start=0x62B, end=0xEE9, 6 B/record): first records `E73B FE3B FF3B` = 0.99658/0.99902/0.99951; `E53B FE3B FF3B` = 0.99609/0.99902/0.99951; last two records `FF3B FF3B FF3B` = 0.99951/0.99951/0.99951. So col0 animates 0x3BD9..0x3BFF, col1=0x3BFE, col2=0x3BFF. Half-float 1.0 would be 0x3C00, so every key is strictly below 1.0, always in one half binade. This rules out any interpretation as position (values would span many binades) and keeps OPEN whether these are color/intensity triplets, basis-lengths, or a normalized weight triple. WALKER NOTE: gap_walk_ver3.py uses first-node start = sp+12+4*(kf-1)+6*kf (=> 6-byte keys) while its (E) fallback speaks of 8-byte records; the 6-byte reading is the one matching the measured kf=373 at 0x62B..0xEE9. Semantics still OPEN (no guess).

### 18.3458 AUTO-PLAY CHEAT SOLVED AND VERIFIED: `.psv` code `$A100 0011B6FC 00001C00` is a 16-bit write at VA 0x8111B6FC; eboot file offset = 0x10E0 + (VA - 0x81000000) = 0x11C7DC. Original halfword D032 = `beq #0x8111b764`; patched halfword 0x1C00 = `adds r0, r0, #0` (fall-through). Forcing fall-through enters the hit-processing path at 0x8111B6FE and turns every note into a PERFECT. **

### 18.3495 *** SCORE FORMULA VERIFIED AT MACHINE-CODE LEVEL (VA 0x811251D6, judge case 1). Exact sequence and constants extracted from ARM, superseding the C-level reading. ***
MACHINE CODE (VA, verified by disassembly):
  0x81125B78 movs.w fp,#0x1140 / ldr.w fp,[sp,fp]      ; grade index (0..3) argument
  0x81125B80 movw r0,#0x1144 / ldr.w r1,[sp,r0]        ; note variant (0..1)
  0x81125B8A bl 0x81133266                             ; = float scoreBase[grade][variant]
  0x81125B8E vcvt.u32.f32 s0,s0                        ; float -> u32
  0x81125B92 ldr r0,[r6,#0x2dc] / add r0,r1 / str r0   ; score += (u32)base
  0x81125BD6 ldr r6,[mgr,#0x2e0]                       ; r6 = combo BEFORE increment
  0x81125BE2 cbz r2 -> 0x81125c00 (special note: no combo increment)
  0x81125BE8 adds r6,#1 / str r6,[mgr,#0x2e0]          ; else combo = combo+1 (this value used below)
  0x81125C00-C34: bonus = ((r6*0xCCCCCCCD>>35) + (r6*0x88888889>>36))*200 + (r6*0xA3D70A3E>>37)*300
       = (floor(c/10)+floor(c/30))*200 + floor(c/50)*300   with c = combo AFTER increment
  0x81125C5E bl 0x811332b6                             ; = float gradeMult[grade][variant]
  0x81125C76 mul r6,r6,r1                              ; bonus *= (u32)gradeMult (truncated)
  0x81125C7A-C8C: ldr score / adds / str score          ; score += bonus
  => FORMULA: score += (u32)scoreBase[grade][variant] + ((floor(c/10)+floor(c/30))*200 + floor(c/50)*300) * (u32)gradeMult[grade][variant]
TABLES (LE floats in eboot, verified bytes): scoreBase @0x813A7F14 = {400.0,800.0 | 200.0,400.0 | 100.0,200.0 | 0.0,0.0}; gradeMult @0x813A7F34 = {1.2,1.2 | 1.0,1.0 | 0.5,0.5 | 0.0,0.0} (u32 truncation => 1/1/0/0); gaugeBase @0x813A7F74 = {2.0,2.5 | 1.0,1.0 | 0.1,0.5}.
  The combo increment is SKIPPED for special notes (r2==0 branch, C 264077-264082) and combo resets on miss (0x81125BF0).

### 18.3517 *** CHART POSITION -> TIME CONVERSION SOLVED (with code evidence): the timeline is audio frames / 29.97 seconds; note positions are in MEASURES (4 beats); time = sum over tempo segments of (delta measure) * 4 * 60/BPM; MNS header BPM at +0x10; tempo-change events are track entries with data byte0 == 0x82. ***
EVIDENCE:
  * mnsProcess update (C L262097-262112): `uVar11 = *(int*)(mgr+0x1F0)+1; while (uVar11 < *(uint*)(mgr+0x1EC)) { uVar5 = FUN_811330d8(*(int*)(mgr+0x424), uVar11); ... FUN_8111bd76((float)uVar11 / 29.97, *(u32*)(mgr+0x1E0)); } ... FUN_8111bd76(*(u32*)(mgr+0x1E4), ...)`. => gameplay time = audio frame index / **29.97** (NTSC), stored at mgr+0x1E4 (float seconds) and stepped per frame into the mnsHandle state (+0x44).
  * live verification: completed Rivers run object mgr=0x4827D830C: mgr+0x1EC = 4575 frames, mgr+0x1E4 = 152.6526 s (4575/29.97 = 152.652) - exact.
  * FUN_8111BD76 (VA 0x8111BD76) sets state+0x44 = time and drives mnsHandle_8111B190 / 8111B64C (the judge/callback pipeline).
  * position encoding (FUN_8111A420 VA 0x8111A420 and its inverse in mnsProcess_8111D6 case 0 C L263705-263727): a note position word (low 16 bits of the first u32 of an MNS track entry) decodes to
        frac = ((low & 0xff) + (bit15 ? 0.5 : 0)) / 2^(((low & 0x7fff) >> 8) + 2)
        position = (word >> 16) + frac          [unit = MEASURE]
    and the inverse encoder builds the same value from time: measure = (int)(t / (4*(60/BPM))), etc.
  * time conversion FUN_8111A420: for each tempo-change entry (8 bytes: {u32 posWord, u32 data}) with posWord decoded as above and data flags: if (data & 0x7f) != 0x7f and (data & 0x80) != 0 then new BPM = (u16 at data offset +2) / 100.0; time accumulates (pos - prev) * (60/BPM) * 4.0. Initial BPM = *(float*)(state+0x0C) = MNS file +0x10 float.
  * mnsHandle_8111A2A6 builds state from mnsData: BPM = *(float*)(mnsData+0x10); musicId-ish = *(u16*)(mnsData+0x14); track list count = *(u32*)(mnsData+0x08); each track = 0xC-byte header {u32, u32 count, u32} + count * 8-byte entries {u32 posWord, u32 data}; first track starts at mnsData+0x18. state+0x08 gets the array of entries whose data byte0 == 0x82 (tempo-change list) via mnsHandle_81119E3C.
  => duration of a chart = FUN_8111A420(last position); with no tempo events it is posMax * 4 * 60 / BPM.

### 18.3521 *** CLASS-B LIP PAYLOAD STRUCTURE RESOLVED (goal item 3): container = nested table decoded by FUN_81174D64; each voice = payload {u32 frameCount; frameCount * 20-byte frames; padded to 32}; queried per 60 Hz frame by FUN_81152E72. ***
CONTAINER (all files sound/lip/e%03d%03d.arc, 129 files):
  file = { u32 entryCount; entry[entryCount] }
  entry = { char name[0x20] (NUL padded, e<AAA>_<BBB>_<CCC>_<DDDD>.bin); u32 payloadSize; payload[payloadSize] }
  payload size is rounded up to a 32-byte boundary (padding may contain stale bytes).
  VERIFIED by FUN_81174D64 (VA 0x81174D64, 88 B): if data starts with 'ARC' use header 16 bytes and count = data[1], else header 4 bytes and count = data[0]; entries start after the header; to seek entry i: ptr += ptr[8] + 0x24 for i times; out size = ptr[8]; return ptr+0x24. For lip files data[0] = entry count (e.g., e000000.arc = 8, e102010.arc = 21, e102020.arc = 46). Measured end offset equals file size exactly for all tested files.
  examples: e000000.arc entry0 = 'e000_000_001_0102.bin' payload 1952 = 4 + 96*20 + 28 pad; entry1 = 'e000_000_002_0102.bin' payload 8064 = 4 + 402*20 + 20 pad.
PAYLOAD (per voice line): { u32 frameCount; frame[frameCount]; } where frame = 5 x u32 = 20 bytes. Frames are indexed at 60 Hz.
  QUERY API: FUN_81152E72 (VA 0x81152E72, 108 B): FUN_81152E72(obj, voiceSlot, frame60, out5):
    if frame<0 return -1; if voiceSlot==0 return -2; if *(obj+0x110)==0 return -3;
    data = FUN_8115FC28(*(obj+0x110),0);   // loaded file bytes
    p = FUN_81174D64(data, voiceSlot-1, 0);
    if !p return -2; if frame >= *p return -1; else out[0..4] = p[frame*5+1 .. frame*5+5]; return 1.

  * half->float FUN_811DD816 (VA 0x811DD816): if (h & 0xffff)==0 -> 0 else bits = (h&0x3ff)<<13 | (h>>15)<<31 | (((h&0x7fff)>>10)+0x70)*0x800000. (no denormal/inf handling).
  * float->half FUN_811DD7DE (VA 0x811DD7DE): e = ((bits&0x7fffffff)>>23)-0x70; if e<1 -> 0; else if e<0x1f -> (bits>>31)<<15 | (e*0x400) | ((bits>>13)&0x3ff); else saturate 0x7bff. => TRUNCATING encode (no rounding).
B) TYPE 0x1F TRANSLATION HANDLER FUN_811A220E (VA 0x811A220E, 138 B): decode 3 halves A,B from the two key records (BE), then per component out_i = half( A_i + t*(B_i - A_i) ) via FUN_811DD7DE - exact linear interpolation in fp16 output. Keys are bone-local translation (18.3467); word0 = translation X; bytesPerKey = 6 (type table 0x813B338C row 0x1F).
C) TYPE 0x20 QUATERNION HANDLER FUN_811A242A (VA 0x811A242A) -> FUN_811A1F58 (VA 0x811A1F58, 236 B):
  disassembly semantics (VR verified): A = 4 floats from key A, B = 4 floats from key B (halves decoded), dot = A.B; if dot < 0 then dot = -dot and A = -A (shortest path); threshold = float bits 0x3F7FBE77 (~0.999):
    if dot >= 0.999: out = A*(1-t) + B*t  (nlerp)
    else: theta = acos_fn(dot); s = sin_fn(theta); w0 = sin_fn((1-t)*theta)/s; w1 = sin_fn(t*theta)/s; out = A*w0 + B*w1  (exact slerp)
    (the two external math calls are PLT-style thunks at 0x812B24C0 and 0x812B25E0; statically they are loader-patched stub slots, identity acos/sin is fixed by the mathematical structure: sin(theta) is used as the normaliser and sin((1-t)theta)/sin(t*theta) as weights).
  result is re-encoded to 4 fp16 (BE) via FUN_811DD7DE. bytesPerKey = 8 (type table row 0x20). Corpus proof of unit quaternions: 306 dense headers in PC201_001.GAP, |q| mean 0.99964 (18.3472).
D) EVALUATOR/CHANNEL SPEC remains as consolidated in 18.3127 (type table 0x813B338C + T*0x20 with +0x14 bytesPerKey: 1A/1C=14, 1B=20, 1F=6, 20=8, 21=6, 22=12, 23=14; handlers +0x08/+0x0C/+0x10/+0x1C; rescale FUN_8119D1A6; merge FUN_8119D892; sample dispatch FUN_8119C7B6; distance FUN_811A2382; channel struct +0x00 type, +0x04 count, +0x08 keys, +0x0C times, +0x10..+0x28 six f32).

### 18.3527 *** RESIDUAL A SOLVED: TOTAL NOTES / JUDGEMENT COUNT = TRACK ENTRIES + LONG-NOTE TAILS (data byte1 != 0) + HOLD-NOTE SECOND JUDGEMENTS (data bit 0x20000). Exact law verified on two live runs: 158+16+2=176 (Easy) and 276+50+11=337 (Normal). ***
LIVE PROOF (fresh instrumented run, trace4b: 4,839 samples logging mgr+0x1E4 game-time, mgr+0x1EC frame, +0x2DC score, +0x2E0 combo, +0x30C..+0x314 grade counters; result max combo 337, grade PERFECT counter 337):
  335 combo-increment events observed (2 first notes judged before the recorder attached); judgement game-times = frame/29.97 exactly.
  chart = dance/mns/mns208_1.bin (BPM 130): 276 track entries; entry time t = pos * 240/130 s (pos from key word decode).
  candidate model: for every entry add head judgement at t; ADDITIONALLY if data byte1 != 0 add a TAIL judgement at t + 4*(60/BPM)*(data_byte1/32); if data bit 0x20000 is set add a HOLD judgement at head + 5 frames.
  count law: 276 heads + 50 byte1-tails + 11 hold-seconds = 337 = max combo = PERFECT counter = displayed TOTAL NOTES.  Easy cross-check: mns208_0: 158 + 16 + 2 = 176 = live Easy max combo.
  TIME MATCH: heads + byte1-tails alone give 326 candidate times; 324 of them match observed judgement times within 0.12 s (the 2 misses are the two pre-recorder notes). Example tail: entry t=20.308 s, data=0x00001001 (byte1=0x10) -> tail t=20.308+4*(60/130)*(16/32)=21.231 s, observed judgement 21.188 s.
  HOLD OFFSET: the 11 data&0x20000 entries (data byte2 = 0x02, creation-function hold flag note[6]&2 -> object flags |=0x100) each produced an extra judgement detected at frames ceil(t*29.97)+5 in 9/11 cases and +4 in 2 (detection quantisation) => offset = 5 frames = 5/29.97 = 0.1668 s. NOTE the creation function stores obj+0x20 = time + (60/BPM)*4*fVar12 with fVar12=0.125 default (=0.2308 s at BPM 130) - this does NOT equal the measured 5 frames, so the hold second-judgement trigger is not simply obj+0x20 (recorded OPEN below).

TYPE TABLE (VA 0x813B338C rows): row 0x23 = {+0x00 0x811A2E9B, +0x04 0x811A2F6B, +0x08 0x811A2FBB, +0x0C 0x811A2FF9, +0x10 0x811A3045, +0x14 bytesPerKey 14, +0x18 14, +0x1C 0x811A0F5B}.
HANDLERS (decompiled):
  * FUN_811A2E9A (interp wrapper): decodes 7 halves from each of the two key records (14 halves total), then calls FUN_811A20D6.
  * FUN_811A20D6 (VA 0x811A20D6, 312 B): the compound interpolator.
      quaternion part (components 0..3): dot = A.B; if dot<0 -> dot=-dot and A=-A; threshold 0.999 (float 0x3F7FBE77): if dot>=0.999 -> lerp weights (1-t, t); else theta=acos_fn(dot), s=sin_fn(theta), w0=sin((1-t)theta)/s, w1=sin(t theta)/s; out0..3 = A*w0 + B*w1.
      scale part (components 4..6): out[4+i] = A[4+i] + w1*(B[4+i]-A[4+i])  <-- NOTE: uses the quaternion slerp weight w1, not the raw t (implementation detail; in the nlerp branch w1=t).
      math calls are the same loader-patched thunks 0x812B24C0 (acos) / 0x812B25E0 (sin) as 18.3522.
  * FUN_811A2F6A = decode 7 halves -> 7 float words; FUN_811A2FBA = read 7 BE halves from stream (FUN_811DF1C6); FUN_811A2FF8 = write 7 halves (FUN_811DF068); FUN_811A3044 (614 B) = distance/norm between two 7-component keys; FUN_811A0F5A = +0x1C marker stub.

  header form {u32 0; f32 f4 = 0.0; f32 1.0; f32 1.0; 12 zero bytes; u32 type=0x23; u32 count; u32 0}; times = count BE f32; keys = count x 14 B (7 BE halves).

In ENV the payload after the 16-byte header decodes as BE floats that start with a 2-byte 0x0101 tag then a 7x7 grid per section: measured 4 sections x 49 BE f32 = 784 bytes, all values inside [0.0, 1.0] (e.g. f100_001.ENV section0 starts 0.4705, 0.4705, 0.4705, 1.0, 0.9882...); footer '40 40 40 FF 00 00 00 02' (8 B). => ENV = per-stage lighting/environment probe grid (4 x 7x7 RGB-ish), consumer = stage lighting path; exact per-channel meaning OPEN.

  * in dance/player/p5/201/pc201_018_08.GAP the node descriptor: '... 00 00 00 1F 00 01 00 00 00 5A 00 0D 52 5f 73 6c 65 65 76 65 5f 72 6f 6f 74 <u32 id=0x188398A4> <u32 trackCount=2>' (name R_sleeve_root), then track[0] = {u32 type=0x1A, u32 count=4194, u32 0} at 0x51.

  * the node also carries track[1] = {type=0x21, count=2} (= the kt33 scale track noted in the earlier ctrl listing). The trailing 20 B of track[0] and the exact 7-component split of the 0x1A key remain OPEN (candidate: final/blend key or a 5-float tail).
F3) EVENT-TABLE FOOTER (reconstructed 641-table corpus = all arc members satisfying size == 8 + count*20; these are the event-cue tables stored inside sound/lip arcs):
  * structure re-confirmed: {u32 count, u32 0} then count x 20-B records; last record is the footer with w4 == count (641/641).
  * measured footer laws (all 641 tables): w2 == 2 always (641/641); w0 in [-96,-2] same domain as record w0 (most common -96 = inactive sentinel, 246/641); w1 in 0..1300 same domain as record w1 (408 distinct values); w3 mostly 0 (586/641), else 180..380.

### 18.3536 SMALL-ITEM 1 SOLVED: THE HOLD/LONG SECOND JUDGEMENT IS THE TWO-PHASE LIFECYCLE OF THE SAME JUDGE FUNCTION mnsHandle_8111B64C; TRIGGER TIME = OBJECT FIELD +0x20 (the creation-function formula IS correct), WINDOW = [-0.06633333, +0.033333335] s. THE EARLIER '5 FRAMES != 0.2308 s' CONTRADICTION IS RESOLVED BY THE EARLY-SIDE WINDOW. ***
CREATION (FUN_8111A644, VA 0x8111A644, 512 B) - two independent branches both write obj+0x20:
  * LONG branch (data byte0 & 0x80 == 0 && byte0 & 0x7f != 0x7f) and data byte1 != 0: flags |= 4; obj+0x20 = note_time + (60/BPM) * 4.0 * (byte1/32)   [byte1 from note[5]*0.03125].
  * HOLD branch (data byte2 (note[6]) & 2 != 0): flags |= 0x100; obj+0x20 = note_time + (60/BPM) * 4.0 * fVar12 with fVar12 = 0.125, or 0.0625 when data byte2 & 4 != 0 (half-beat default).
  (obj+0x1C = note_time, obj+0x14 = pointer to the 8-byte MNS record copy, obj+0x18 = param_2.)
JUDGE LIFECYCLE (mnsHandle_8111B64C, VA 0x8111B64C, 1834 B) - the same per-note judge runs twice and emits TWO kind-1 callbacks:
  * gate/window (lines 255475-255490): target time fVar13 = (flags&4 && flags&8) ? obj+0x20 : ((flags&0x100 && flags&0x200) ? obj+0x20 : obj+0x1C); if (time - fVar13) < -0.06633333 -> not judged; if (time - fVar13) > 0.033333335 -> not judged. => judge window = [target-0.06633333, target+0.033333335] seconds (about -2.0..+1.0 frames at 30 fps).
  * LONG note first pass (flags&4 && !(flags&8), line 255659): target = obj+0x1C, flags |= 8, callback kind1 (score/combo), callback kind3.
  * LONG note second pass (flags&4 && flags&8, line 255699): target = obj+0x20, SECOND callback kind1, callback kind3, flags |= 0x80, then note removed from the active list (255742-255746).
  * HOLD note first pass (flags&0x100 && !(flags&0x200), line 255604): target = obj+0x1C, flags |= 0x200, callback kind1, callback kind3(0).
  * HOLD note second pass (flags&0x200, line 255631): target = obj+0x20, SECOND callback kind1, callback kind3(0), flags |= 0x80 (255655), removal (255742-255746).
RESOLUTION OF THE TIMING PARADOX: hold offset = (60/130)*4*0.125 = 0.2307692 s = 6.923 frames at 29.97 fps; because the judge window lets the FIRST pass fire up to 0.06633333 s (about 2 frames) BEFORE the target, the observed first->second detection gap in the live trace (4.97..5.88 frames) is exactly consistent with 6.923 frames minus 1..2 early-side frames plus sampling jitter. The earlier note in 18.3527 ('obj+0x20 formula is not the trigger') is RETRACTED: obj+0x20 IS the trigger.
CONSISTENCY: this two-phase mechanism is exactly why the TOTAL NOTES judgement count = entries + long-note tails + hold tails (18.3527): each long/hold note object produces two kind-1 judgements, hence two combo/score increments, while remaining one note for display.

### 18.3537 SMALL-ITEMS 2 AND 6 SOLVED + MAJOR CORRECTION: THE 641 'EVENT TABLES' ARE A MISALIGNED VIEW OF LIP PAYLOADS; THE REAL LIP FORMAT IS 32-BYTE-ALIGNED WITH PREFIX-COPY PADDING. LIP ch2/ch3/ch4 ARE PROVEN RESERVED/UNUSED. ***

CORRECTION (supersedes 18.2070-18.2074 and the 'event table' part of 18.3532 F3):
  * full-corpus re-measure of all 129 sound/lip arcs / 5,160 entries: every payload = {u32 frameCount; frameCount x 20-B frame(5 x i32); pad} where pad = (-(4+20*frameCount)) mod 32 (0..28, multiple of 4). 5,160/5,160 entries have entry size % 32 == 0 and exactly this pad length.
  * the pad bytes are NOT free: for every entry with pad>0 (4,536/4,536), pad bytes == the FIRST pad bytes of the payload (prefix copy). This is a wrap-read helper for the 60-Hz frame ring.
  * the 641 files previously classified as 'event tables' (size == 8 + count*20, last record w4 == count) are exactly the entries whose pad == 4: 641/641 such entries have their last u32 (the pad word) equal to frameCount, and reading a record array starting at +8 instead of +4 shifts every frame by one field. The apparent 'records' are therefore (frame_i.w1, w2, w3, w4, frame_{i+1}.w0) = (negative weight, loudness, 2, extra, next viseme) -> this is why w2 was ALWAYS 2, w4 in 0..5, w0 negative and w1 in 0..1300, and why the 'footer' w4 always equalled the count. There is NO event-table family and NO footer record semantics: w0/w1/w3 of the 'footer' are ordinary frame fields and w4 is the pad word (= frameCount). §18.2070-18.2074 are RETRACTED.
  * FINAL LIP PAYLOAD SPEC: class-B arc member -> {u32 frameCount; frameCount x 5 x i32 @60 Hz; prefix-copy pad to 32 B alignment}; entry size = align32(4+20*frameCount); query FUN_81152e72(obj, voiceSlot=1-based arc ordinal, frame60, out5) returns the 5 ints of that frame.

4) MNS TIME-BASE CORRECTION (authoritative) + LEGACY/PORT ISOLATION
```
AUTHORITATIVE MODEL (in-game code, seg0):
  note record = {u16 type; u16 measure; u32 data};
  measure = record+2 u16; sub-measure fraction is encoded in TYPE:
     denom = 1 << (((type & 0x7fff) >> 8) + 2);  num = type & 0xff;
     frac  = num/denom + ((type & 0x8000) ? 0.5 : 0);
  seconds(measure) = measure * 240 / BPM (1 measure = 4 beats), piecewise over tempo records.
  EVIDENCE: FUN_8111A420 (fVar8=(u32>>16); fVar6=u32&0xff; fVar9=1<<(((u32&0x7fff)>>8)+2);
    bit15 adds 0.5; per-tempo sec += (Δmeasure)*(60.0/bpm)*4.0); FUN_8111A644 (target =
    base + (60/bpm)*4*fVar12); mnsProcess_811251d6 (fVar22=240.0 and (60.0/bpm)*4.0).
  OLD '60/BPM' (§18.382/§18.433) RETRACTED: it was calibrated against its own harness.
  CROSS-CHECK: mns218_2 old duration 78.703 s -> *4 = 314.81 s; music218.wav = 323.13 s;

  size 0x60; fields:
    +0x20 name[16]; +0x44 U(u32); +0x48 V(u32); +0x4C W(u32); +0x50 H(u32)

### 18.3550 【PORT M9】原版对局叠加层 3D 锚定（相机 MVP 世界→屏幕投影）：音符环/Scratch 环/星环/轨道跟随舞者***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: 3D anchored authentic overlay, camera MVP projection, project_world column-major, projected dancer anchor CX CY, ringPx from projected height, scratch ring/trails/star ring follow dancer, judge left big, camera timing WIP.

1) PROJECTION (new, verified):
```
  The character shader uses gl_Position = uMVP * vec4(aPos,1) with the matrix uploaded GL_FALSE,
  i.e. GLSL mat4 column-major. CPU-side equivalent used by project_world():
     clip[i] = m[i]*x + m[4+i]*y + m[8+i]*z + m[12+i]
     ndc = clip.xyz / clip.w ; screen.x=(ndc.x*.5+.5)*960 ; screen.y=(1-(ndc.y*.5+.5))*544
  MEASURED at c108.GFS / t=0.5s (stage f208): world (0,95,0) -> screen (487.4, 295.8),
     depth w=520.02 ; world height 95->260 cm -> 362.1 px => projection is correct & usable.
```

2) SCREEN-SPACE SCALE FROM PROJECTION (important pitfall):
```
  Projecting a fixed 240 cm world offset in a close-up frame gives 1488 px (useless); so the overlay
  radius is derived from the PROJECTED DANCER HEIGHT instead:
     ringPx = projected_height_px * 0.95, clamped [90,360], fallback 220.
  (c108/t=0.5: height 362 px -> ringPx=344 px; matches the real gameplay ring/dancer ratio.)
```

3) WHAT MOVED TO THE PROJECTED ANCHOR (src/assets/p5d_play.cpp authentic_gameplay_draw):
```
  CX,CY = projected dancer mid-point (was fixed 480,300)
  - scratch_01 'Scratch!' ring: scale = ringPx*2/508, centred on (CX,CY), slow spin
  - dance_01 blue/grey trails: (CX -/+ ringPx*1.10, CY - ringPx*0.55), scale from ringPx
  - notes: still 3D world ring (radius 250->100 cm, height 120 cm) projected per note;
    icon scale uses 600/clip.w perspective factor
  - ring_red scratch circles: (CX-ringPx*0.95, CY-ringPx*0.55) and (CX-ringPx*1.10, CY+ringPx*0.42)
  - combo star ring: diameter ringPx*2.3
  - judge word: (CX-ringPx*1.25, CY-ringPx*0.55) scale 2.35 (left side of ring, matches real frames)
  - fever gauge + score stay at fixed top-left / top-right (real frames place them at screen corners)
```

```

    LONG branch : data byte0 & 0x80 == 0 && byte0 & 0x7f != 0x7f && data byte1 != 0
                  flags |= 4 ; offset = byte1/32 (measure units)
    HOLD branch : data byte2 & 2 != 0 -> flags |= 0x100 ; offset = 0.125 (0.0625 if byte2 & 4)
  mnsHandle_8111B64C runs the SAME judge twice and emits TWO kind-1 callbacks per long/hold note
  => TOTAL NOTES = entries + LONG tails + HOLD tails (18.3527/18.3528).
  Mapping to our MNS schema (18.3556): byte1 = data bits 8..15 (= holdLen), byte2 = bits 16..23.
```

  expandHoldTails(Chart&): appends a synthetic tail Note per LONG/HOLD note:
      time = note.time + tailMeasures (measure units; useMeasureTiming active), same mask/type/id,
      isTail = true. The existing Judge then judges the tail as a second note => second hit/grade/combo
      exactly like the game's second kind-1 callback. HUD skips isTail notes.
  p5d_play calls expandHoldTails() after useMeasureTiming() and prints [JUDGE] two-phase counts.

### 18.3560 【ROUTE DECISION / PORT M19】用户选定 AOT 重编译路线 + 阶段1 落地：Thumb-1 → x86-64 原生代码翻译器自测通过***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: route decision AOT recompilation ARM Thumb to x86-64, native execution, interpreter fallback oracle, thumb_aot.h thumb_aot.cpp, Windows x64 ABI rcx rdx r8 r9 shadow space, flags helper aot_flags_add sub aot_nz, self-test THUMB_AOT_SELFTEST_PASS, regression line 8 AOT_TRANSLATOR_SELFTEST_PASS, remaining stage2 memory ops.

0) USER DECISION (2026-10-23):
```
  Asked which porting route to take; user selected: 'AOT 重编译（最难但最“正确”）'.
  => The project goal was updated accordingly (goal revision 3): original ARM/Thumb binary is
     statically translated to x86-64 native code + GXM->Vulkan bridge, single native PC exe.
  Rationale (why this is the 'correct' route):
    - emulator/interpreter route (eboot_probe) is NOT native execution;
    - clean-room native rewrite (old route 2) needs per-screen reverse engineering (UI layout etc.);
    - AOT gives native x86-64 execution AND logic identical to the original code (it IS the original code).
```

1) ARCHITECTURE (stage 1 implemented):
```
  guest Thumb basic block (16-bit halfwords)
     -> src/arm/thumb_aot.cpp: decoder + x86-64 emitter
     -> x86-64 machine code buffer (VirtualAlloc RWX, cached per guest PC in later stage)
     -> executed by the host CPU: uint32_t block(AotState*) -> next guest PC
  Guest state: AotState { uint32_t r[16]; uint32_t apsr; }  (N=31 Z=30 C=29 V=28)
  Stage 1 keeps guest registers in memory; later stages allocate them to host registers.
  Runtime helpers (C ABI, called from generated code):
     aot_nz(s,res), aot_flags_add(s,a,b,res), aot_flags_sub(s,a,b,res)
  The interpreter (src/arm/thumb_interpreter.cpp) stays as fallback for untranslated blocks and
  as the differential oracle for tests (until AOT coverage is 100%).
```

2) STAGE-1 SUPPORTED THUMB SUBSET (all self-tested):
```
  movs Rd,#imm8 ; cmp Rn,#imm8 ; adds/subs Rd,#imm8 ; adds/subs Rd,Rn,Rm ;
  bx Rm ; b (uncond) ; beq/bne ; (block ends: branch/limit/unsupported instruction)
```

3) EVIDENCE (deterministic):
```
  generated x86-64 for 'cmp r0,#12 ; beq +0 ; bx lr' was disassembled with objdump
  (blockE): prologue saves rbx/rdi/rsi/r12/r13 + sub rsp,32 shadow space; mov r12,rcx;
  mov eax,[r12+0] ; mov edx,0xc ; mov ecx,eax ; sub edx,ecx ... helper call ...
  test eax,0x40000000 ; jne 0x44 ; jmp 0x56 ; taken: mov eax,6 ; mov [r12+0x3c],eax ... ret
  full self-test (C:/dev/tmp/build_aot/thumb_aot_test.exe):

4) BRING-UP BUGS FOUND & FIXED (do not reintroduce):
```
  - host ABI: generated code first used SysV (rdi/rsi/rdx/rcx) on Windows x64 -> args garbage.
    FIX: Windows x64 ABI: state in RCX, a in RDX, b in R8, res in R9; save rbx/rdi/rsi/r12/r13.
  - Windows requires 32-byte shadow space for callees -> added 'sub rsp,32' in prologue /
    'add rsp,32' in epilogue; without it helper prologues can smash captured registers.
  - 0x89 /r direction: modrm.reg is the SOURCE, modrm.rm is the DEST; mov r8d,edx = 41 89 D0
    (the first attempt emitted 41 89 C2 = mov edx,eax -> wrong args, nondeterministic flags).
  - RCX clobber ordering: 'mov rcx,r12' destroyed the res value before it was copied to r9d;
    FIX: copy b->r8d and res->r9d FIRST, then load rcx, then a->rdx.
```

### 18.3563 【ROUTE CLARIFICATION / PORT M22】本方案与模拟器的本质区别：静态重编译(AOT) + 本地兼容层(HLE)，并规划“一次性翻译成原生程序”***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: static recompilation vs emulator, HLE compatibility layer, original binary unchanged, no CPU emulation at runtime, GPU command translation to Vulkan, savedata0 host file mapping, N64Recomp PS2 static recompilation WINE Rosetta2 analogy, offline pre-translation pass persistent native cache file p5dnative.

0) USER QUESTION (2026-10-23): '这种移植方法应该和模拟器有本质上的区别吧？'
   ANSWER: YES. The described method is static recompilation (AOT) + a local high-level compatibility
   layer (HLE), not a hardware emulator. It reuses the original binary unmodified but does NOT emulate
   the console hardware at runtime.

1) ESSENTIAL DIFFERENCES:
```
  ASPECT            EMULATOR (e.g. Vita3K)              THIS PROJECT (AOT + HLE compat layer)
  CPU               fetch/decode/interpret or JIT the   original code translated ONCE into native x86-64
                    guest ISA at runtime, emulating      machine code; executed directly by the host CPU
                    CPU behavior/timing                  (no fetch/decode/interpret loop in steady state)
  HARDWARE          emulates console hardware: GPU      does NOT emulate hardware; replaces OS/driver APIs:
                    command stream, kernel, DSP, caches,  file/savedata -> host files, input -> host pad/touch,
                    clocks, memory cards                 graphics commands -> native Vulkan calls
  SYSTEM CALLS      virtual kernel + virtual FS          HLE: sceIo*/mceFios2 handlers call host APIs
                    (savedata0: -> emulator FS)          directly (savedata0: -> local savedata dir)
  GRAPHICS          emulates GXM hardware pipeline      translates GXM draw calls to Vulkan; the 12 original
                    incl. all hardware state               USSE shaders are translated once (src/usse)
  ARTIFACT          generic emulator + game image       single native PC exe + original game data folder
  SCOPE             runs many games (generic)           one game (P5D) purpose-built compat layer
  PERFORMANCE       guest code at emulated speed        guest code at native speed
  ANALOGY           PS1/N64/PSV emulators               N64Recomp / PS2 static-recompilation projects,
                                                         WINE (HLE layer, no CPU emulation), Apple Rosetta 2
                                                         (binary translation) - but here CPU translation is static
  COMMON GROUND     original binary & assets unchanged, original game logic executes (it is the real game)
```

2) PROJECT MAPPING (evidence):
```
  original SELF/eboot loaded byte-identically      src/loader/self_loader.cpp
  static translation of original ARM/Thumb code    src/arm/thumb_aot.cpp (+ executor native blocks)
  OS API HLE                                        src/loader/nid_*.cpp, src/filesystem/sce_io.cpp/sce_fios.cpp
  save read/write -> host file (user's example)     eboot_probe.cpp:6130-6136, 6274-6276, 7499, 8209
  input HLE                                         src/input/*
  graphics HLE (GXM -> Vulkan)                      src/gxm/* + src/usse/*
  guest address space -> host buffers               src/mem/address_space.cpp
```

3) GAP TO THE USER'S EXACT MODEL + NEXT MILESTONE:
```
  User's model: '开玩之前直接把原版游戏的代码一次性翻译重写存成电脑能直接运行的原生程序'
  Current: AOT executor translates each basic block on first execution and caches it in memory (block cache).
  NEXT: add an OFFLINE PRE-TRANSLATION PASS:
    * scan the loaded eboot/SELF modules, translate every reachable basic block to x86-64 once (AOT),
      record indirect-branch targets via the existing interpreter/oracle run -> fixed point coverage;
    * persist the translated image + relocation/import tables into a cache file (e.g. P5D_native.p5dc);
    * at game start load the native image directly (no translation at play time); fallback interpreter only
      for residual untranslated paths (should trend to 0 as stage3 Thumb-2/VFP/SVC coverage grows).

  native program, matching the user's model and clearly distinct from any emulator.
```

1) QUANTUM SEMANTICS BUG & FIX (root cause of 'AOT exits early'):
```
  PROBE (eboot_probe.cpp:8249-8265): ROUND=20,000,000 ; QUANTUM=120,000 ; mx->set_quantum(QUANTUM) is called ONCE
  before the main loop. In the INTERPRETER, quantum is decremented with `--quantum==0`; after it reaches 0 the next
  run() wraps it to 0xFFFFFFFF, i.e. preemption effectively disables itself and each later run() executes the full
  ROUND. In the AOT executor we instead returned STOP_QUANTUM forever once quantum_ hit 0 (and the probe's
  total += QUANTUM accounting then burned the 1.2e9 CAP in ~10k fake rounds) -> the process printed diagnostics
  and exited while only ~176k real instructions had run.
  FIX (src/arm/thumb_aot_executor.cpp): at the start of run(), `if (quantum_ == 0) quantum_ = 0xFFFFFFFF;`
  => exactly mirrors the interpreter's wrap semantics.
```

1) VERIFIER DESIGN (src/arm/thumb_aot_executor.cpp, env P5D_AOT_VERIFY=1):

```

           AOT(r0=0x276CC558) vs INTERP(r0=0x816CC630) -> r0 was never written by the MOV.
  FIX:     use 0xFF00 mask:  (insn & 0xFF00) == 0x4400 / 0x4500 / 0x4600.
  (Also added: AotBlock.hasConditionalBranch marking and verifier skip; CacheEnt.hasCondBranch.)
```

### 18.3574 【PORT M33 / BREAKTHROUGH】LDM/STM 基址被覆盖 bug 修复：BADMEM 消失，AOT 持续运行 120 秒并进入 GXM 渲染数据解析阶段***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: LDM STM base address overwritten bug, Rn in register list LDMIA r0!,{r0,r1}, insn C803 4770 at 0x812615B4, AotState scratch slot offset 68, scratch_store scratch_load, BADMEM gone, AOT runs 120s, blocks 8232 aotInsn 1912251 fbInsn 3087753, GXM vertex attribute parsing VATTR2, next verifier MEM DIFF 0x81279C22 0x81279C94 IT context.

1) ROOT CAUSE (real AOT translation bug, now fixed):
```
  fault block 0x812615B4 instructions: C803 4770  =>  LDMIA r0!,{r0,r1} ; BX lr
  before state: r0=0x8153FB00 (valid!), r1=0x1, r2=0x1, r3=0x8153FAC0, lr=0x8126081D
  AOT executed: first loaded word written into r0 (base register), then the SECOND element address was
  re-computed by re-reading r[rn] -> r0 had been overwritten by the first loaded value (0) -> second load
  at [0+4] = 0x4 -> BADMEM. Interpreter saves the base once and loads correctly.
  => GENERAL BUG: any LDMIA/STMIA whose register list contains Rn. The translator re-read r[rn] for every
     element instead of keeping the original base address.
```

2) FIX:
```
  - AotState gains a 'scratch' slot (offset 68) used to save the base address.
  - Emitter: scratch_store(reg) / scratch_load(reg)  (41 89/8B 44 24 44).
  - Translator LDMIA/STMIA: save base once into scratch, use scratch+offset for every element, writeback
    from scratch (+n*4) only when Rn is NOT in the list (ARM semantics: loaded Rn value wins otherwise).
```

3) RESULT (decisive): BADMEM GONE, boot continues:
```
  after fix, 120 s run (killed while still running, exited_early=False):

    fogFactor/constColor/skinBlendMatrices...).
  => the AOT backend now survives the previous crash point and runs real original engine code far deeper;

### 18.3587 【PORT M46 / ROOT-CAUSE FIX】AOT 栈破坏根因修复：嵌套 call_guest 的 stale sync_to_fallback 覆盖实时解释器状态；STACKCHK/UNDEF 全消失，DISPENTRY 668 帧***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: nested call_guest from inside fallback, AotExec call_guest sync_to_fallback overwrites live interpreter state stale AOT snapshot SP r, callback runs on wrong stack overwrites caller canary 0xA016E020, fix inFallback_ skip sync_to/from, STACKCHK 0 UNDEF 0 BADMEM 0, DISPENTRY 668 g_draw 2001, 240s stable render loop QUEUEW PRES, next capture later frames and advance to TITLE.

1) ROOT CAUSE (AOT-only, explains every earlier symptom):
```
  ImportBridge installs the probe's HLE handlers bound to the ACTIVE executor object (AotExec in AOT mode).
  When the fallback interpreter executes an SVC during AOT mode, inFallback_=true, and HLE handlers that call
  active_executor()->call_guest() (per-frame display/vsync callbacks, fn=0x8117BA31) end up in
  AotExec::call_guest. The old implementation called sync_to_fallback() unconditionally, which writes the
  AOT state snapshot (taken BEFORE the fallback batch started) into the interpreter - overwriting the LIVE
  guest SP/registers of the frame that is currently executing. The callback then runs on that stale SP
  (0xA016E020, i.e. inside the caller's frame), writes 0xA016E040 over FUN_81159de4's canary slot, and after
  returning to the interrupted function its epilogue canary check fails -> __stack_chk_fail -> execution
  continues into the data segment -> UNDEF at 0x816CDA02. The interpreter-only run never hits this because
  call_guest there is the interpreter's own method operating on its live state.
```

2) FIX (src/arm/thumb_aot_executor.cpp AotExec::call_guest):
```
  const bool nestedCall = inFallback_;          // HLE called us from inside the fallback interpreter
  if (!nestedCall) sync_to_fallback();           // only sync when the AOT side owns the live state
  ... active executor switch, fallback_->call_guest(...) ...
  inFallback_ = prevInFallback;                  // preserve nesting flag
  if (!nestedCall) sync_from_fallback();         // never clobber the live interpreter state
  (also from 18.3586: clear_pending_jump() in sync_to_fallback so stale force_npc cannot hijack a run)
```

3) RESULT (240 s AOT run, same binary, no other flags changed):
```
  STACKCHK count = 0     (was 75+ and crashed)
  UNDEF    count = 0     (was [EBOOT-START] stop=4 UNDEF 0x816CDA02)
  BADMEM   count = 0
  DISPENTRY#668 g_draw=2001, PRES count 668, 43,236 log lines, still running when killed
  tail = normal render loop: QUEUEW/PRES/DISPENTRY/MEMREL/EVT/JOB/PUMP
  [STAGE] step=1 DEBUG MENU->initread; [F1-STAGE] hit st=4 (internal stage advance)
  => the AOT backend now runs the original game's frame loop stably for hundreds of frames with NO stack
     corruption and NO crash. This was the root cause of the earlier 'canary failure + data-segment UNDEF +
     black render targets' symptom cluster.
```

4) NEXT:
```
  a) capture LATER frames (e.g. frames 100/200/300/400, not the first 14) and check whether the render
     targets now contain real game content (the black-frame observation was from the first 14 frames only);
  b) run longer and watch [STAGE] advance (initread -> next state -> TITLE);
  c) keep STACKCHK/UNDEF counters as a regression check for future AOT/HLE changes.
```

### 18.3592 【PORT M51 / ROOT-CAUSE FIX】AOT 特异 BADMEM 根因：解释器内 NGS-loop-fix hook 在 AOT 块执行时被绕过；含 hook pc 的块强制走解释器后 TITLE 阶段稳定运行（DISPENTRY 3478）***

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. 1) ROOT CAUSE (why interpreter was fine but AOT crashed after TITLE):
```
  thumb_interpreter.cpp has two probe fixes implemented as INTERPRETER PC HOOKS:
    pc==0x81274D96: if (int)r0 outside [0,0x380] -> r[0]=0   ('[NGS-LOOP-FIX] bogus count -> 0')
    pc==0x81274EBA: if (int)r2 outside [0,0x380] -> r[2]=0   ('[NGS-LOOP-FIX2] bogus count r2 -> 0')
  These hooks run inside the interpreter's instruction loop. In AOT mode the same instructions were executed
  by translated blocks, so the hooks NEVER ran: the bogus count 0x1CB365A (LSRS r2,r0,#6 of a garbage value)
  stayed live, the audio parameter loop (FUN_81274b30) iterated a huge count, walked a garbage pointer
  (r3=0xB4654FD8) and hit the unmapped page 0xB4655000 -> BADMEM. The interpreter ran the hooks, clamped the
  counts to 0, skipped the loop and never crashed - exactly the observed AOT-only difference.
  (18.3590's verifier DIFF at 0x81274EB8 was the same phenomenon: AOT r2=bogus vs INTERP r2=0 after hook.)
```

2) FIX (src/arm/thumb_aot_executor.cpp, before executing a cached block):
```
  static const SceUInt32 kInterpHookPcs[] = { 0x81274D96u, 0x81274EBAu };
  if any hook pc is inside [pc, pc+ce.insns*2):
      sync_to_fallback(); activate interpreter; fallback_->run(ce.insns);  // hooks apply per instruction
      sync_from_fallback(); quantum accounting; continue;

```

ANTI-FORGETTING ENTRY. Keywords: incident save-write patch misclassified RDONLY as write mode, SCE flags SCE_O_RDONLY 0x0001 WRONLY 0x0002 RDWR 0x0003, log IO OPEN(write) app0:/data/vita.cpk fd 0x4001 flags 0x4001, vita.cpk truncated from 2GB+ to 0 bytes 2026-10-24 18:41, fix condition isSaveOpen and (flags&3)==2 or 3 build OK, recovery options vita_extracted holds complete unpacked content movie 13 usm ~1.1GB and sound acb/awb, option A HLE directory fallback in CpkReader preferred small change, option B write a CPK packer (CriPakTools only extracts/replaces, no directory pack), next implement directory fallback and verify.

1) THE INCIDENT:
```
  The save-write patch added a write branch to n_io_open using a wrong access test:
      bool _wr = (_acc==1 || _acc==2);      // _acc = flags & 3
  but SCE flags are: SCE_O_RDONLY=0x0001, SCE_O_WRONLY=0x0002, SCE_O_RDWR=0x0003.
  So flags=0x4001 (RDONLY | 0x4000) was treated as WRITE -> app0:/data/vita.cpk was opened with L"wb":
      [IO] OPEN(write) app0:/data/vita.cpk fd=0x4001 flags=0x4001
  Result: C:\dev\p5d_rom\data\vita.cpk went from a large data file to 0 bytes (2026-10-24 18:41), and runs
  after that produce no DISPENTRY (game cannot mount/read vita.cpk).
```

2) FIX (already applied, build OK):
```
  bool _wr = isSaveOpen && (_acc==2 || _acc==3);
  => write mode ONLY for savedata0: paths and ONLY for WRONLY/RDWR; all data files (app0: etc.) are never opened
     in write mode again.
```

3) RECOVERY OF vita.cpk:
```
  No backup copy exists on disk. But the unpacked original content is available and complete:
    C:\dev\p5dsrc\game\PCSH10109\vita_extracted\movie\*.usm  (13 USM, ~1.1 GB total)
    C:\dev\p5dsrc\game\PCSH10109\vita_extracted\sound\**   (acb/awb + wav, complete sound set)

       serve member reads from the vita_extracted directory tree (name -> file). This is exactly what a
       compatibility layer should do (CPK access mapped to local directory), and requires no re-packaging.

### 18.4056 PORT M516 / STATIC-RECOMP STAGE 6kx: ★★★★ FOUND THE REAL ROOT CAUSE - A GENERATOR BUG: SHIFTED-REGISTER ADD IS TRANSLATED WITH THE SHIFT LOST ("+2" INSTEAD OF "*17").
The probes:
```
  [D3A6] r8=846968A4 [r8+4]=846968C0 r9=00000000 (n=1)
  [D3A6] r8=846968A4 [r8+4]=846968C0 r9=00000001 (n=2)
  [D3B2] r0_out=846968C0 r1=00000000 sb=00000000 (n=1)
  [D3B2] r0_out=846968C2 r1=00000002 sb=00000001 (n=2)
```
So [r8+4] is stable (0x846968C0); the difference comes purely from r9 (sb) = 0 vs 1 multiplied by 2: r0 = base + sb*2. BUT the actual instruction at 0x8115D3AA is **`add.w r1,sb,sb,lsl #4` = sb + (sb<<4) = sb*17, NOT sb*2**! And the generated code for blk_8115D3A6 is `s->r[1] = s->r[9] + s->r[9];` - **the `lsl #4` SHIFT OPERAND IS LOST**.

So the AOT generator drops the shift on register-shifted ADD (and likely other shifted-register ALU ops), producing sb*2 instead of sb*17 -> the array index is wrong -> the container pointer lands 2 bytes off (and would be much more wrong for larger sb) -> [obj+4] read from a misaligned address -> 0x1F8469 garbage -> BADMEM. **This is a CORE GENERATOR BUG (like the earlier id_reg LR bug), not a game/object issue.**

**FIX**: in `_gen_split.py`, when emitting shifted-register ALU instructions (`add.w Rd,Rn,Rm,lsl #N` etc), apply the shift to the Rm operand: `s->r[d] = s->r[n] + (s->r[m] << N)` (and analogously for lsr/asr/ror and for sub/and/orr/eor). Then regenerate all batches (7-10 min), relink, run 10M - the appMemoryHandler crash chain should clear.***

### 18.4058 PORT M518 / STATIC-RECOMP STAGE 6kz: FOUND THE EXACT ALU BRANCH THAT DROPS THE SHIFT - `_gen_batch2.py` lines 643-667. The add/sub/rsb branch is:
```python

    ...

        L.append("{ uint32_t _a = %s; uint32_t _b = %s; ... }" % (R(reg(1)), R(reg(2)), ...))
```
Sub-cases: (a) `isi(1) and len(ops)==2` (imm), (b) `isr(1) and isi(2)` (reg+imm), (c) `isr(1) and isr(2)` -> `_b = R(reg(2))` **(no shift handling - our bug)**, (d) immediates, (e) 2-operand high-register form. The and/orr/eor/bic branch follows at line 696+. The correct pattern to copy is `mem()` (lines 89-107) which reads `o.shift`/`o.mem.shift` and emits `<<` / `>>` / arithmetic `>>`.

**FIX**: add a helper next to R()/reg():
```python
def _shreg(i):
    r = R(reg(i)); sh = getattr(ops[i], 'shift', None)
    if sh is None: return r
    if isinstance(sh,(tuple,list)): st,sv = sh[0],sh[1]
    else: st,sv = (getattr(sh,'type',0) or 0),(getattr(sh,'value',0) or 0)
    if st==1: return '(%s << %d)' % (r,sv)              # LSL
    if st==2: return '(%s >> %d)' % (r,sv)              # LSR
    if st==3: return '(((int32_t)%s) >> %d)' % (r,sv)   # ASR
    if st==4: return '(((%s >> %d) | (%s << (32-%d))))' % (r,sv,r,sv)  # ROR
    return r
```
then use `_shreg(2)` instead of `R(reg(2))` in the (c) branch and `_shreg(1)` in the 2-operand branch, and similarly in the and/orr/eor/bic branch.

### 18.4082 PORT M542 / STATIC-RECOMP STAGE 6ln: ★★★ FOUND THE REGISTRATION FUNCTION (ARRAY APPEND) - 0x8115D1D0 - AND LEARNED 0x8117306A IS A 'REGISTER + INITIALIZE OBJECT' FUNCTION.
Disassembly of 0x8115D1D0:
```asm
  8115D1D0 push {r4,lr}
  8115D1D2 adds r4,r0,#0    ; r4 = container
  8115D1D4 ldr r1,[r4,#4]    ; capacity
  8115D1D6 ldr r0,[r4,#8]    ; count
  8115D1D8 adds r0,#1        ; count+1
  8115D1DA bl 0x812B0E8E
  8115D1DE ldr r1,[r4]       ; array base
  8115D1E0 rsb r2,r0,r0,lsl #2 ; r2 = 3*count
  8115D1E4 str r0,[r4,#8]    ; store new count
  8115D1E6 add.w r0,r1,r2,lsl #2 ; = base + 12*count
  8115D1EA movs r1,#0
  8115D1EC str r1,[r0,#8]    ; zero-init new entry
  8115D1EE pop {r4,pc}
```
So 0x8115D1D0 **APPENDS a 12-byte entry** to the array described by r4 (`[+0]`=base, `[+4]`=capacity, `[+8]`=count) - this is THE REGISTRATION MECHANISM.

And 0x8117306A calls it with `r0=[0x81555E98+8]` (the global container's array-struct pointer), followed by 0x8116E734 (manager state init), 0x81173602 (more init; reads global 0x813AFCDC) and 0x81004B8E (init of another object; reads global 0x81328B04). So **0x8117306A = 'REGISTER + INITIALIZE ONE OBJECT'**. Therefore the registry that lookup misses is the array at [0x81555E98+8]; if this array's count stays 0, nothing was registered.

**NEXT**: find the callers/loop of 0x8117306A (who registers the 4 objects) and instrument [0x81555E98+8] (count field) to see whether 0x8117306A ever runs.***

```asm
  8116489E push {r4,lr}

### 18.4126 PORT M586 / STATIC-RECOMP STAGE 6mv: ★★★ MAJOR CORRECTION - 0x810168A6 IS A LINKED-LIST INSERT AND [manager+8] IS THE LIST TAIL (0 = EMPTY LIST, LEGITIMATE); THE M577 'MUST BE NON-ZERO' CLAIM WAS A FLAG MISREAD.
Full disassembly 0x810168A6-0x81016938:
```asm
  810168A8 adds r5,r0,#0        ; sets flags on r0 (manager)
  810168AE bne 0x810168C6        ; manager != 0 -> skip assert; else assert line 0x15 (manager NULL)
  810168C6 cbnz r4,0x810168DE    ; node != 0 -> skip; else assert line 0x16 (node NULL)
  810168DE ldr r0,[r4]; cbz r0   ; node->[0] must be 0 (line 0x17) i.e. node not already linked
  810168F8 ldr r0,[r5]; [r4]=r5  ; node->manager = manager
  810168FE adds r0,#1; [r5]=r0  ; manager count++
  81016902 [r4+4]=0; [r4+8]=0   ; node->prev=node->next=0
  81016906 cbnz r6,0x8101691E    ; if r6 (=[manager+8] tail) != 0 -> insert AFTER r6
  81016908 ldr r1,[r5,#4]        ; else insert at HEAD using [manager+4]
  81016914 ldr r0,[r5,#8]        ; tail
  81016916 [r5,#4]=r4; [r5,#8]=r4 or keep tail
  8101691E ldr r3,[r6,#8]; [r4+8]=r3; [r6+8]=r4; [r4+4]=r6; ...
```
So the structure is a doubly-linked list: [manager]=count, [manager+4]=head, [manager+8]=tail, node+0=manager, node+4=prev, node+8=next. **[manager+8]=0 means EMPTY LIST and is perfectly legal** - 0x810164F4 simply passes the tail as the insert-after parent (0 = insert at head).

CORROBORATING RUNTIME EVIDENCE: the memory watch added to wr32 in all 26 batches fired exactly once: `[WATCHW] GLOB813AFC0C v=84896B80 prev=00000000 blk=8116E688` (global slot written once at manager creation), with ZERO writes to [obj+8] or [array+8] - consistent with tail staying 0 for an empty list, and NOT a missing registration. **The 'registration gap' theory is DEAD.**

### 18.4129 PORT M589 / STATIC-RECOMP STAGE 6my: ★★★★ TWO MORE SYSTEMATIC GENERATOR BUGS FOUND WITH EXACT NUMERIC PROOF.
BUG (a) SHIFT-TYPE MAPPING INVERTED:
- capstone 5 constants are ASR=1, LSL=2, LSR=3, ROR=4, RRX=5, but the generator assumed LSL=1, LSR=2, ASR=3.

- Static check: handler object 0x813144F4 in the ELF holds valid Thumb pointers 0x8125CFB7, 0x8125CFC1, ... so no bogus data exists.

### 18.4146 PORT M606 / STATIC-RECOMP STAGE 6nf: ★★★★★ THE WILD-POINTER ROOT CAUSE IS THE SIXTH AOT GENERATOR BUG - TWO-OPERAND THUMB REGISTER-SHIFT `lsrs r0,r1` WAS SILENTLY DROPPED.

```

### 18.4148 PORT M608 / STATIC-RECOMP STAGE 6nh: ★★★★★ SEVENTH AOT GENERATOR BUG - CONDITIONAL BRANCH ALIASES `bhs`/`blo` MISSING FROM COND MAP, SO THE BRANCH WAS SILENTLY EMITTED AS UNCONDITIONAL FALLTHROUGH.

```

811C0E10 bhs 0x811C0E6E     <- bail out when the bin mask >= 0x80
811C0E12 asrs r3, r3, #2

but the generated block 0x811C0E0A ends with an UNCONDITIONAL `return 0x811C0E12u` - the `bhs` branch is gone.

### 18.4208 PORT M668 / STATIC-RECOMP STAGE 7e: ★★★★★ THE DOUBLE-INITIALIZATION ROOT CAUSE IS FOUND AND FIXED - THE FIBER2 PUMP WAS REPLAYING APP INIT; ALL FIVE ASSERTS ARE GONE.
EVIDENCE (new `g_loop_site` dispatch-loop tag added in 18.4208):
```
[INITW] initEntry-A-336 #1 loop=0 lr=81198C18 sp=A05FFFE8 fib=84846860
[INITW] sysInitAgg #1 loop=0 ... appPad-init #1 loop=0 ... appGxScene-init #1 loop=0 ...
[INITW] initEntry-A-336 #2 loop=3 lr=81198C18 sp=A05FFFF0 fib=84846860
[INITW] sysInitAgg #2 loop=3 ... appPad-init #2 loop=3 ... appGxScene-init #2 loop=3 ...
```
The same init entry ran once in dispatch loop 0 (fiber_exec) and once in loop 3 (fiber2 pump), from the same caller `lr=0x81198C18` and the same fiber `0x84846860`.

ROOT CAUSE: the pump start did `f1=g_cur_fiber; save f1; f2=other; if (pump_first || c2.r[15]==0) { force-reset c2 to entry 0x81198C0A }`. Even though fiber2 had already executed and its context was saved, the first pump pass discarded it and re-ran from the entry - replaying the whole app-init sequence and triggering all five \"singleton already initialized\" asserts.

FIX (18.4208 (note b)):
```cpp
static uint32_t g_f2_seen = 0;   // last fiber whose context was genuinely saved by execution
// in the fiber save path: if (g_cur_fiber) { g_f2_seen = g_cur_fiber; ...save... }
const bool f2_ran = (g_f2_seen == f2);
if ((pump_first && !f2_ran) || c2.r[15] == 0u) { ...force-reset to entry... }
else { resume saved ctx; pump_first = 0; }
```
RESULT (30M run, clean baseline + assert HLE + this fix):
```
[PMP2] fiber2 RESUME saved ctx pc=8120766A (f2_ran=1)
[PMP2] fiber2 RESUME saved ctx pc=811E5EE8 (f2_ran=1)
[PMP2] fiber2 RESUME saved ctx pc=811E5ECE (f2_ran=1)
init sequence runs EXACTLY ONCE; ALL FIVE ASSERTS DISAPPEAR.
new (much later) blocker: [BADMEM] guest va=0x00000002 block=0x81207344
  81207344 push {r4,lr}
  81207346 ldr r0,[r0]        <-- called with r0=2 (guest VA 0x2: a small handle/index used as a pointer)
  81207348 movs r1,#1
  8120734A movs r2,#0
  8120734C blx 0x812B2830
  81207350 pop {r4,pc}
```

**NEXT**: find who calls 0x81207344 with r0=2 and why a small handle/index is used as an object pointer (it is in the thread/scheduler HLE region; likely a stale thread/handle value).***

### 18.4234 PORT M689: ★★★★ WaitEventFlag MODE-BITFIELD SEMANTICS FIXED; NEXT BLOCKER = EVENTFLAGS 0x60014000/0x60015000 NEVER SET.

Old-runtime `n_wait_eventflag` semantics (recovered from eboot_probe.cpp):
```
mode is a BITFIELD:
  bit0 = OR wait (otherwise AND wait)
  bit2 = CLEAR     -> on success: pattern &= ~requestedBits
  bit4 = CLEAR_ALL -> on success: pattern = 0
on success: *resultp = CURRENT pattern (not the requested bits)
on failure: thread blocks, yields, and the wait is replayed on resume
```
Harness case 0x812B2880 rewritten to exactly this: mode-aware evaluate, CLEAR/CLEAR_ALL, result=cur,
main-thread path pumps workers + retries up to 2000 times, and SetEventFlag wake now honours each
waiter's OR/AND mode (`HThread.wait_mode`).

[EVW] wait obj=60015000 bits=00000001 mode=2 cur=00000000 ok=0 thr=40019000 lr=811732C2
```
Only TWO WaitEventFlag calls in the whole run; both threads block forever because **nothing ever sets
0x60014000 / 0x60015000** (guest or HLE). The main thread still repeats
`SetEventFlag(0x60016000, bit1)` at lr=8127BE56 and `[SIG2]` stays 0.

### 18.4243 PORT M698: ★★★★★ SceDisplay NID MAPPING WAS WRONG - CRASH LOOP (17137 -> 2 BADMEM) ELIMINATED; VBLANK THREAD WORKS.

Verified against the real import table (`docs/eboot_imports_with_nid.json`):
```
0x812B1810 = SceDisplay      NID 0x05F27764  sceDisplayWaitVblankStartMultiCB   (NOT GetFrameBuf)
0x812B1820 = SceDisplay      NID 0x7D9864A8  sceDisplayWaitSetFrameBufMulti     (NOT SetFrameBuf)
0x812B1800 = SceDisplayUser  NID 0x7A410B64  sceDisplaySetFrameBuf              (the REAL one)

```

Root cause of the crash loop:
```
guest graphics code 0x811539F2 loop:
   bl 0x81236D22                              ; per-frame graphics/state-machine step
   movs r0,#2                                 ; vblank count = 2
   blx 0x812B1810                             ; sceDisplayWaitVblankStartMultiCB(2)
our mis-mapped HLE treated r0=2 as a FRAME-BUFFER POINTER and did GP(2)
   -> [HLE-BADMEM] va=00000002 ... (17137 times, 8787 in one 30M run)
```

Fix (18.4243):
```
0x812B1800 SetFrameBuf: records addr/pitch, no-op present
0x812B1810 vblank wait: increments g_vblank_n; host-thread path sleeps count*16 ms (clamp 1..4)
0x812B1820 WaitSetFrameBufMulti: 1 ms sleep in host-thread mode
0x812B2410 strncat: real implementation (find end, append up to n, NUL)
```

```
Default cooperative config unchanged: `30M: exit=0, BADMEM=0, GXM=12, FSW=16`.

    built by guest FUN_81207924:

      81207950  str r1,[r5]; ldr r0,[r1]      ; data pointer

    -> [BADMEM] guest va=0x00000008 block=0x811C0DA8

### 18.4274 PORT M729: BOOT DEADLOCK BROKEN BY A LOADER-PUMP SCHEDULING EMULATION (ENV-GATED).

Motivation: the main thread is legally blocked in `0x811E5EC2` on `[task+2]==6`, while the Fios load
state machine that would set it is only driven from (a) the loader-fiber loop `0x811E5BFE` and (b) the
main loop's bit1-CLEAR branch `0x811E5EEA`. After app-init sets bit1, neither context runs in our harness
-> the pending load task never advances (M722-M728 evidence: task 0x84BF3870 state=0 forever,
`[TASKST]=0`, `[FIOSSM2] RUN=0`).

Implementation (default OFF, `P5D_LOADPUMP=1`):
```
at a safe point in the fiber dispatch loop:
  task = [0x816CDA2C]; if (task && [task+2] != 6 && (blocks % 20000)==0)
     call_guest_cb(s, 0x811E5928, 0, 120000)      // bounded guest run of the Fios state machine
```
This is scheduling emulation, not a guest-code patch: the original binary is untouched; the HLE supplies
the "other context" that real hardware would run.

RESULT (`P5D_LOADPUMP=1`, default 30M):
```
[LOADPUMP] n=1420000 task=84BF3870 state=0 -> run FUN_811E5928
[LOADPUMP]   -> ret=812B4150 state now=7
[LOADPUMP] n=1440000 task=84BF3870 state=7 -> run FUN_811E5928
[LOADPUMP]   -> ret=812B4150 state now=6          <- DONE, the wait loop exits
then the game advances:
[GXMP] HLE 812B1380 r0=816CBEC8 r1=00484000 r2=3F800000 r3=81A00000 lr=811EAB1E
[GXMP] HLE 812B1660 r0=816CBEF8 r1=00044000 r2=00011000 r3=00000440 lr=811EAB3C
[GXMP] HLE 812B1250 r0=816CBEF8 r1=00000004 r2=00011000 r3=00000440 lr=811EAB44
       (GXM render-target setup region 0x811EAAxx is reached for the first time)
[MEMA] AllocMemBlock uid=0x157 size=0033D000 addr=81F50000 name=8130CC88 lr=812077AC   <- 960x544 RT memsize
[MEMA] ... uid=0x158 0x40000 / 0x159 0xF00000 / 0x15A 0x3200000 / 0x15B 0x400000 / 0x15C 0x800000 / 0x15D 0x40000
[TASKWATCH] task=8284B980 state=0               <- next async task registered
[CONSUME] FHRead calls=3 bytes=4,218,956 FIOS-opens=12291   (was 1 call / 62,100 B)
[CNT] 81198BEA=74 811E5CDA=74 811E5928=74        <- the guest loader loop itself now steps the state machine
```

### 18.4276 PORT M731: SECOND LOAD TASK TYPED (GFDPSP2.GSC, 4 MB) + 16-BIT STATE-WRITE INSTRUMENTATION GAP.

Object layout validated from `[TASKWR]` + `[E59]` (Fios load task, 0x2C bytes):
```
+0x00 flags word                      +0x02 u16 STATE (state machine: ldrsh [r6,#2])
+0x04 pointer to self+0x2C            +0x08 Fios file handle
+0x0C read buffer                     +0x10 read size
+0x18/+0x1C counters                  +0x20 Fios op handle
+0x24 next-task link
```
Evidence (30M, P5D_LOADPUMP=1):
```
task 0x84BF3870: +08=0x3001 (fh), +10=0xF294 (62,100 = GFDPSP2PRESET.GSC), +0C=0x88291D30 (buf),
                 +20=0x5001 (op), +24=0x8284B980 (link to next task, blk=0x811E5E42)
new head task 0x8284B980 = [FIOS] OPEN 'app0:/data/GFDPSP2.GSC' -> fh=0x3002 size=4094756
[E59] n=1643939 r6=8284B980 state=0   (loader fiber 84836840 itself is processing it - not the pump)
[E59] n=1643939 r6=84BF3870 state=6   (already-completed old task is STILL LINKED/referenced)
[CONSUME] FHRead calls=3 bytes=4,218,956 = 62,100 + 62,100 + 4,094,756
```
Interpretation: after the pump completes the first task, the guest loader loop takes over and starts the
second (4 MB GSC) load, and the guest really reads it; but the **completed task is not unlinked from the
Fios list** in this context, so the wait loop / list traversal keeps seeing a state-6 node and the main
scheduler plateaus (`pc=812B27B0` loop), with no BeginScene yet.

Instrumentation gap found: the Fios state field is written with a **16-bit store** (`strh [r6,#2]`), but the
generated batch prelude has no watch hook for 16-bit writes:
```
static inline void wr16(RecState* s,uint32_t a,uint16_t v){ std::memcpy(P(s,a),&v,2); }   // in every batch_*.cpp
```
=> add `wr16_watch(a,v)` to all 26 batch preludes + `_gen_split.py`, rebuild the batches (~5 min), and the
0/1/2/7/6 transitions become traceable.

### 18.4277 PORT M732: ROOT CAUSE - TBH TABLE TARGETS ARE NOT BLOCK LEADERS (id_tbh RE-EXECUTES THE STATE WRITE).

Instrumentation delivered (16-bit writes were invisible):
```
- wr16_watch() added to the prelude of all 26 batch_*.cpp + _gen_split.py:
    extern "C" void wr16_watch(uint32_t a, uint32_t v);
    static inline void wr16(RecState* s,uint32_t a,uint16_t v){ if (g_watch_on) wr16_watch(a,(uint32_t)v); std::memcpy(P(s,a),&v,2); }
- all 26 batches rebuilt (Start-Job x6, 400 s, 0 failures) and relinked successfully
- harness wr16_watch logs writes into the watched Fios task object ([W16] a off v blk fib thr)
```
Trace (P5D_LOADPUMP=1, 30M):
```
task 0x84BF3870: state 1 -> 2 -> 4 -> 7 -> 0x13FC -> 6        (blk 0x811E5996/59EA/5A34/5B60/5A6A/5A9C)
task 0x8284B980: state 1 -> 2 -> 4 -> 7 -> 0x13FC -> 6 -> 0x13FC
the 0x13FC writes are tagged blk=0x811E5A6A and blk=0x811E5A9C, r0=0x13FC (stale op value)
=> the final state is 0x13FC, so the 0x811E5EC2 wait loop never sees 6 and the boot plateaus
```
ROOT CAUSE:
```
Fios state machine dispatches via tbh at 0x811E597E.
Real table (base = Align4(tbh_pc+4) = 0x811E5982), state 0..8 ->
  0x811E5994 0x811E5998 0x811E59EC 0x811E5A36 0x811E5A56 0x811E5A62 0x811E5A9E 0x811E5A6C 0x811E5AB0
Several targets are MID-BLOCK in the generated code:
  state7 target 0x811E5A6C is inside block 0x811E5A6A ("strh r0,[r6,#2]" first instruction)
  state6 target 0x811E5A9E is inside block 0x811E5A9C (ditto)
The generator emitted leaders ~2-4 bytes early (observed 0x811E5A68/5A6A/5A9C instead of the true targets).
At runtime id_tbh computes the correct target, gbn(t) fails, then gbn_back backs up 2..16 bytes and executes
the containing block FROM ITS START - re-executing "strh r0,[r6,#2]" with the current r0 (0x13FC) instead of the
7/6 the preceding instruction had set. => state corruption -> wait loop never sees 6.
This is a general AOT correctness bug for TBH/TBB/indirect dispatch targets that are not block leaders
(not Fios-specific).
```
FIX PLAN:
```
1. _gen_split.py: derive TBH/TBB leaders with base = Align4(tbh_pc + 4), read every table entry, and add each
   computed target as an explicit block leader (then the dispatcher lands on a real entry block; no gbn_back rollback).
2. regenerate the 26 batches + rebuild (~10 min) and re-run the state trace: expected 1->2->4->7->6 with no 0x13FC.
3. if the wait loop then exits, continue on the next boot stage / GXM BeginScene.
```

### 18.4286 PORT M741: PUMP STALE-PC BUG FIXED (CANARY-LR CORRUPTION GONE); NEXT BLOCKER = GFD TYPE-3 OBJECT PATH RETURNING INTO DATA 0x003E7B24.

The bug: `call_guest_cb()` saves all 16 registers and restores them at the end, so after a pump call the
dispatcher's own `pc/fn` remain valid. The pump code however did:
```
call_guest_cb(...);  pc = s.r[15]; if (pc) fn = gbn(pc); if (!fn) { pc = 0x811E5EC6; fn = gbn(pc); }
```
`s.r[15]` can be a stale mid-block value; when it happens to be a valid block (e.g. **0x811E5EF0**, the wait
helper's epilogue `pop {r4,pc}`), the dispatcher jumps there with the wrong register/stack state.
Evidence `[CANARYPC]` before the fix:
```
[CANARYPC] blk=811E5EF0 fib=848468E0 r0=00000006 r1=812B4150 r4=848468E0 r5=812B414C r6=1 r7=00000470
           sp=A0D7FD98 lr=8120765C   -> block returns pc = 0x812B4150 (the stack-canary guard value)
```
After removing the stale-pc reassignment in **both** the fiber-loop pump and the targeted wait pump:
`[CANARYPC] = 0`, `[THREADWEMU] = 0` (path changed), and the main thread no longer dies at the canary.

New blocker (lp+wemu 30M):
```
[ODDPC] nxt=003E7B24 blk=811E5EF0 fib=848468E0 lr=811E6A52 r0=6 r1=r2=812B4150 r3=4 r4=0 r5=82C334F0
        ring: 811DE9B2 811DE9B4 811DE986 811DE98C 811E6A4C 812B2270 811E6A52 811DE998 811DE94C 811DE9BA 811DED6C ...
```
- `0x003E7B24` = 4,094,244 (~ GFDPSP2.GSC size 0x3E7D64) - a DATA value used as next pc.
- The preceding ring is the **GFD type-3 object factory/introspection path**: `0x811DE9xx` (FUN_811DEAB4 /
  FUN_811DE912 from M735), `memcpy 0x811E6A4C`, HLE stub `0x812B2270`.
- i.e. after the two Fios loads complete, the main thread reaches the same GFD object-construction subsystem whose
  introspection returned -1 on a zero payload in M735; now it produces a bad control transfer instead.

### 18.4287 PORT M742: WAIT-HELPER EPILOGUE READS THE GSC PARAM BUFFER - THE HELPER IS ENTERED WITHOUT ITS PROLOGUE (act=0).

`[RET_EPI]` probe = fires when any block returns next-pc 0x811E5EF0 (the wait helper's `pop {r4,pc}`):
```
[RET_EPI] act=0 from blk=811E5EC6 fib=848468E0 sp=A0D7FDB8 lr=811E6A52
  words: 00000000 003E7B24 8284B9C0 47534330 01087159 00000004 00000000 00800000 ...
```
Interpretation:
- word[sp+0] = 0 (would be saved r4; actual r4 later popped as 0)
- word[sp+4] = **0x003E7B24** (would be saved LR; a GSC data value!)
- word[sp+8] = 0x8284B9C0 (a Fios task pointer)
- word[sp+0xc] = **0x47534330 = "GSC0" magic**, then 0x01087159, 4, 0, 0x800000 - the **GSC file header**.
=> the memory popped by the helper's epilogue is the caller's GSC param-buffer, not a helper frame. `act=0` proves the
helper's prologue block `0x811E5EC2` (`push {r4,lr}`) did NOT run for this invocation, yet loop-entry block
`0x811E5EC6` (the back-edge target `b 0x811e5ec6`) DID run - so the loop is entered directly and `pop {r4,pc}`
reads caller data as PC = 0x003E7B24.
The first `[RET_EPI]` event shows a NORMAL variant (`words: 8284B980 811E5CB6 ...` = saved r4=task, saved
LR=0x811E5CB6 = thunk return), so both a proper call path and a direct-entry path exist.

Also identified: `0x811E6A4C` is the **memcpy HLE thunk** (`push {r4,lr}; blx 0x812B2270 (HLE memcpy); pop {r4,pc}`)
and the ring `811DE9xx ... 811E6A4C 812B2270 811E6A52 811DE998 ...` shows the GFD factory path performing the
0x10-byte GSC-header memcpy into a stack param buffer immediately before the bad return.

NEGATIVE: `P5D_WLGUARD=1` (save/restore 0x40 words around the targeted wait pump) does NOT change the result
(`[ODDPC]=20` remains) - the corruption is not from the targeted pump's own stack writes.

`[ODDPC]=[RET_EPI]=[WLFRAME]=0`; lp+wemu 30M `exit=0, BADMEM=0, HLE-BADMEM=13`.
